Gate the work on `A11y.enabled()` (a headless test forces it through `A11y.force_enabled`); the terminal's value follows the screen text at most once per `A11Y_PUSH_MS` and is deliberately not gated on the settle window - that window keys off the grid's damage counter and delays only the one-line announcement, because a counter-gated push starves every publication as soon as something repaints (2026-11-13); the publish host is re-resolved per push; a live region states one line, never a buffer. Prove the metadata with `scripts/ui-capture --audit-accessibility <state>` and the exposed tree with `scripts/accessibility-probe` against a rebuilt export. An element's value and role have no path to the 4.7.2 adapter (`AccessibilityServer.update_set_value`/`update_set_role` never reach the node, and a custom `Control` carries no `Text`/`Value` interface): the name is the creation snapshot, so `A11y.publish` replaces a slot only when its text or live mode changed - an idle pane republishes its last line every second and must not take the node a reader is on. The probe prints an `a11y-values:` line (`text-interfaces`, `value-interfaces`, `marker-in-value`, `role-names`) for exactly that re-test. A surface that records a value (`A11y.set_value`/`set_text`) must forward `NOTIFICATION_ACCESSIBILITY_UPDATE` to `A11y.apply_update(self)`: the write is queued, not pushed, because 4.7.2's server refuses `update_set_role`/`update_set_value` outside that notification and prints an engine error for each call. A published node is an `A11yContent` (a `Control` whose own accessibility update writes the role `A11y.set_text` queues) and carries its content in `accessibility_name`: that is the name a driver reads for a Control, while a `Label` reports its display text instead (content in a Label's `accessibility_name` published an empty name, measured 2026-11-13) and a bare `Control` keeps the container role AccessKit drops from the tree. Never carry the screen as Label text either: one full screen (221x78 = 17 315 chars) cost 992 ms of shaping (windowed, 2053x1382, measured 2026-11-11).
- Sidebar layout: the sidebar owns every persistent switcher (workspaces, profiles, panes) as vertical sections in its VBox - never add full-window top strips or overlays, they cover sidebar chrome (the window-mode dropdown sits at the sidebar's top). Sidebar content lives inside a `MarginContainer` (8px left/right ≈ scrollbar width, 6px vertical) so rows never touch the sidebar's edges. Every text-bearing sidebar button is built by `_make_sidebar_button(text, icon := "")`: a row label (`icon == ""`, `clip_text` + ellipsis so a long user-authored name cannot stretch the 164 px section) or a full-width icon+text action whose child `HBox` (icon `Label` + text `Label`, same font size) is centered with `ALIGNMENT_CENTER` and no sideways offset, plus an explicit `custom_minimum_size.y` on the textless icon+text Button (a textless Button does not size from its children and collapses). Section lists share one pattern: `SECTION_MAX_VISIBLE_ROWS` (5) caps visible rows; `_measured_section_height` sizes the scroll container from `get_combined_minimum_size()` (never hard-coded row heights - they drift from theme metrics and truncate the last row); `_apply_row_accent` marks the active row (`Palette.ACCENT_COLOR` + pressed look) and is used identically by workspace, profile, and pane rows. Active-row state: workspaces by index, profiles by name (cleared on `_do_reset` and on deleting the active profile), panes by `_tm.last_body` via `set_active_pane` (no list rebuild on focus change). The pane list absorbs leftover height via `SIZE_EXPAND_FILL`. The section headers are built by `Sidebar._add_section_header(host, id, header_name, actions, scroll, expanding)`, which appends the section's own controls and then a fold toggle whose only state is `SettingsManager.is_sidebar_folded(id)` (`SIDEBAR_SECTIONS` is the closed id vocabulary, `cfg_sidebar_folded` the `user://settings.json` key, written by `set_sidebar_folded` without a `settings_changed` broadcast) - hiding the list's `ScrollContainer` is what frees its height, and a list refresh never touches the fold. A refresh whose model did not change rebuilds nothing: `update_workspace_list`/`update_profile_list` compare `_workspace_signature`/`_profile_signature` and call `_apply_*_state` (accents only) when it matches, and a new field a row shows must join that signature or the row goes stale. The pane list has no signature: `update_pane_list` runs `_sync_pane_rows`, which mutates from `_pane_rows` (body instance id -> row) - it adds a spawned pane's row, detaches a closed one in the same call, rewrites a renumbered label, and swaps a row's actions for its check/cross pair (`_apply_row_pending`) - because a pane row costs 7-10.4 ms and rebuilding the list made a spawn cost grow with the live pane count (closed 2026-11-14).
- A section whose header is glyph-only carries the shared Help affordance: `ui/section_help.gd` (`SectionHelp.attach(header, host, title, intro, rows_of)`) adds one question-mark `Button` (tooltip and accessible name "Help") that opens an `AppDialog` table of `{glyph, action, chord}` rows. The provider is called on press, never at attach time, because a chord is only spelled once the workspace has registered its bindings; `host` must be an unclipped Control (the sidebar sets `clip_contents`, so its popups are parented to the background rect) and a header whose text changes with state keeps `clip_text` set, or the renaming Label resizes the 164 px section. Any user-facing string that names a chord reads `ShortcutManager.chord(action)` - never a literal, and never the pane registry's own `shortcut` field.
- Profiles: named terminal-layout snapshots. `ProfileManager.get_all_profiles()` lists **user profiles first** - the two seeded defaults are prepended to `profiles`, followed by saved profiles - and **installed-plugin profiles second**. `res://profiles.default.json` is seed material, not a row source: `_load_defaults()` copies only `name`/`description`/`tiles`, `_seed_defaults_once()` prepends them once and writes `seeded_defaults: true` in `user://profiles.json`, and deleting a seeded row is permanent (the marker stops re-adding it). Both name no program, so first-run onboarding opens no dialog: Agent Workspace is terminal geometry, Knowledge Base is a wiki tile naming the bundled-vault token. Tool presets stay in plugin repos, and the two defaults are also published as `godot-pty/gpty-agent-workspace`/`gpty-knowledge-base`. Shipped files are never written back, and plugin profiles are not either - they belong to the plugin and vanish with it (their store records keep them out of `user://profiles.json`; the sidebar gives them no rename but a trash that calls `GptyTerminal.uninstall_plugin()`, sharing `gpty-plugin`'s store removal with `gpty plugin uninstall`; the tooltip names the plugin and pinned revision). Dedupe follows `add_profile`: a user profile keeps the bare name and a colliding plugin takes ` (n)`; among plugin profiles the first wins, and `_derive_plugin_profiles()` re-runs on every user add/rename/delete so the winner does not depend on arrival order. `find_user_profile(name)` is the only user-name lookup; `rename_profile(index, name, replace_existing)` with `true` deletes a same-named user profile after the sidebar's Replace Profile prompt, while a name held only by a plugin is not a replacement target. `plugin_profiles_source` and `plugin_uninstall_source` are the test seams. `refresh_plugin_profiles()` parses `GptyTerminal.installed_plugin_profiles()`, skips malformed entries, re-derives the block and emits `profiles_changed`; it runs at init, after an accepted install review (the deferred 2 s re-read), and on the `pluginsChanged` notice, so a CLI admin action is visible in a running GUI. Activation clears the workspace (`_reset()`) then rebuilds tiles (`_restore_into()`) from the sanitized profile tiles; the shipped file's entries are covered by `test_each_preset_tile_passes_sanitize_tile` and its program-free rule by `test_the_shipped_builtins_are_program_free`. A profile row offers two destinations and keeps them separate: the label activates in the active workspace (`_do_profile_activate`, which asks before replacing panes) and the trailing `Icons.NEW_WORKSPACE` glyph opens it in a workspace of its own (`_do_activate(profile, ask_running, open_in_new)` → `_create_workspace_for_profile`: named after the profile through `WorkspaceStore.unique_name` (a second one gets " 2"), inheriting the active workspace's cwd, switched to before the restore, refused at `MAX_WORKSPACES` before the trust prompt, and with no replace confirmation because nothing live is lost). The Workspace Trust dialog carries `open_in_new` through, so an approval cannot redirect the click to the other destination; the two sidebar signals (`request_profile`, `request_profile_in_new_workspace`) are emitted by their own gesture and never both. The profiles section ends with a catalog hint row (`_make_catalog_hint_row`, `CatalogHintBtn`) that opens the plugin registry.
- Attachment IDs: persist `attachment_id` (`[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}`) on panes. Companion panes (Reasoning) attach by this stable id, not ephemeral labels like `T1`. `pane_label` is reassigned on restore and must not be used as a saved link. It is also the **public IPC id**: every pane has one (auto-generated `pane-XXXXXXXX` via `PaneTypes.generate_attachment_id()` when none was saved - `PaneBody.apply_settings` is the choke point), `newPane` returns it and `listPanes` reports it as `id` alongside the display `label`. A Pane Settings rename retargets the followers in that pane's own workspace (`Workspace._retarget_companions` calls each follower's `retarget_source`), so a companion never keeps an id its terminal no longer has; a pane whose link should survive a rename implements `retarget_source` rather than resetting on every `apply_settings`. IPC pane targeting accepts either the `id` or a `label`, resolved by `Workspace._resolve_pane_target`: an `attachment_id` always resolves (ids are globally unique across workspaces); a label resolves only when exactly one pane carries it, and a label several workspaces share (`T1` in each, since labels restart per workspace) is **refused** with an error naming every candidate's workspace and attachment id - never resolved to whichever workspace happens to be active, because an agent working in one workspace must not act on another workspace's pane by accident. `listPanes` and `broadcast` stay inside the active workspace. Restoring a tile set (a workspace restore, or the same profile activated in a second workspace) resolves every id **before** any body exists: `_resolve_tile_ids` renames duplicates against the panes already live in other workspaces and against earlier tiles (first one keeps a repeated id), rewrites the set's `source_attachment_id` references through the old→new map so a Reasoning pane follows the terminal restored beside it, and copies the user-owned `PaneEnvStore` entry to the new id (the entry still belongs to the logical pane id the first instance holds).
- JSON → typed arrays: `JSON.parse()` returns untyped `Array`. Assignment to `Array[Dictionary]` fails at runtime. Always iterate and build the typed array element-by-element: `for item in raw: if item is Dictionary: typed.append(item)`.
- Private members: underscore prefix (`_cell_w`, `_settings_panel`)
- Config vars: `_cfg_` prefix (`_cfg_cursor_shape`)
- Persistence: Managers extend `BasePersistenceManager` - provides `_read_file(path)` / `_write_file(path, data)` for JSON stores and `_read_text(path)` / `_write_text(path, text)` for text assets, and sets `PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS`. Subclasses override `_on_init()` instead of `_ready()`. Loads read through the typed accessors (`_as_int`/`_as_bool`/`_as_array`/…) rather than a raw `d.get(key, default)` assigned to a typed variable: GDScript raises on a wrong-typed JSON value, which aborts the loader and drops every key after it (and the next save writes that reduced state back). Never inline `FileAccess.open()` - use `_read_file`/`_write_file` for JSON stores and `_read_text`/`_write_text` for text assets. Writes go to a sibling temp file and are renamed into place: `FileAccess.WRITE` truncates the target as soon as it opens, and `_read_file` reads a truncated file as empty, so an in-place write that fails costs the entire store. That temp name is random (`_temp_suffix()`, 64 bits) and the file is created 0600 (`STORE_UNIX_MODE`): `FileAccess.open(..., WRITE)` **follows a symlink**, so a fixed `<store>.tmp` let anything able to write in `user://` point the next save at a file of its own choosing. Do not go back to a predictable name, and do not drop the explicit mode - the umask decides otherwise, and a 0644 store hands every pane environment and window geometry to any account that can read `user://`.
- Godot paths vs real paths: `String.is_absolute_path()` is true for `res://` and `user://` as well as a filesystem path (measured on 4.7.2), so it is not the guard at a boundary that leaves Godot. `FileAccess`, `DirAccess` and `DirAccess.*_absolute` accept the schemes; Rust (`std::path`, a PTY `cwd`), FFmpeg and a desktop handler do not — and a scheme that slips through fails one layer later with a message about the layer, not the setting (v0.7.1's knowledge base resolved to `user://knowledge/<hash>` and failed as "not an absolute path" inside the vault index). Use `BasePersistenceManager.is_real_absolute_path()` wherever a data value must be a real absolute path, `BasePersistenceManager.sanitize_absolute_dir(raw, max)` for a *directory* value (a store entry or a `dir_path` setting — that check plus the length cap and the control-byte refusal, in one place for every store and the settings table), and `BasePersistenceManager.real_path()` to turn a scheme into the directory it names. `FileAccess.file_exists()` stays the regular-file gate; it answers only the path-type question.
- Directory layout: Scripts are grouped by role: `autoloads/` (shared managers and the persistence base), `terminal/` (core terminal), `ui/` (sidebar, settings, toast), `panes/` (specialty pane types). `project.godot` autoload paths and `preload()`/`load()` calls use the full `res://scenes/<dir>/<file>.gd` path.
- Pane settings from a file are a closed table: `PaneTypes.settings_schema(type)` lists every key a pane type accepts with a rule (`text` with an optional `values` closed set, `backend`, `int`/`float` with a range, `bool`, `color`, `id`, `tags`, `argv`, `shell`, `font_path`, `dir_path`, `scheme_path`) and `file: false` for keys only the app may set (env, scheme paths, the three chrome colors). `PaneTypes.sanitize_tile` runs it with `SOURCE_FILE` - unknown and app-only keys are dropped and `Workspace._restore_into` reports them once - and `PaneBody.apply_settings` runs it again with `SOURCE_RUNTIME`; it is the only assignment path - a pane's own `apply_settings` runs its live side effects (a repaint, an audio apply, a session reset, a status row) and never re-sanitizes a key the table already decided, so a rule changes in one place; `test_pane_settings.gd::test_a_refused_setting_value_leaves_each_panes_property_alone` holds every override to that (the old `_set_typed` assigned *any* exported String/int/float/bool, which is how a layout chose a font path). The control surface runs the same table with a third source, `SOURCE_IPC` (`paneSet`, `new-pane --setting`), which also refuses a rule marked `ipc: false`: a pane's `type`/`attachment_id`, `rows`/`cols`, the user's own env (`shell_env`) and Inspector aim, and the wiki's `graph`/`open_note`. A refused key answers `-32602` naming every one and nothing is applied, and `paneSettings` publishes the table (`kind`, `min`/`max`, `values`, `file`, `ipc`) so the vocabulary is discoverable rather than duplicated in the CLI. A new pane property that must survive a layout needs a rule, and `test_pane_settings.gd::test_every_pane_type_accepts_the_settings_it_saves` fails when one is missing. Data paths never reach a resource loader: a `.tres` with an embedded GDScript runs during `load()`, so `TerminalFonts` builds a font from bytes (absolute regular file, extension gate, 32 MiB cap, magic + face check) and only the bundled `res://` constants go through `load()` (an export carries their imported `.fontdata`, not the source `.ttf`); a color scheme is a capped `TextRead`. `font_size` is clamped to `PaneTypes.FONT_SIZE_MIN/MAX`, which the pane panel's spinbox also uses. A terminal tile's `launch` is the spawn-time key: one shell line, accepted from a file, expanded through the user's configured shell by `PaneTypes.spawn_argv` at `TerminalPane._start_child_if_ready` (the only `start_shell` call site). A saved launch tile carries the line alone — a launch line is spawn-time state, like `rows`/`cols`, and a settings edit never applies it to the child already running. A rule that carries `values` refuses a member outside it at every source, so no pane re-derives a closed vocabulary at apply time; `kind: "backend"` is the one canonicalizing rule - an alias folds into `BackendChoice.KINDS` and an unknown name is kept for the panel's `Custom:` row - and `pane-settings` publishes `values` for both.
- Settings pipeline: `cfg_*` → `SettingsManager.save_settings()` → `user://settings.json`. Read-only rows are allowed (not every row is a setting): the Terminal tab's "On disk:" label reports what scrollback costs, from the static FFI `GptyTerminal.history_store_stats()` → `gpty_core::history::store_size_on_disk()` (the store file plus SQLite's `-wal`/`-shm` siblings). It cannot be derived from `History lines` - the store is bounded by rows *and* bytes, so the real footprint depends on how long the lines were - and it is refreshed on `NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED` rather than once, because the panel outlives a visit while scrollback keeps growing. To add a new setting: (1) add a `cfg_*` var, (2) add the UI control to the owning tab and its reset lambda, (3) if a terminal consumes it, add the key to `SettingsManager.apply_to_terminal()`. `TerminalManager.spawn_pane()` and `Workspace._on_settings_changed()` call that automatically, so no other wiring is needed; a window/chrome-only value is applied by `Workspace._on_settings_changed()` itself (`WindowChrome.apply_opacity` is the instance). A setting only chrome owns takes a third shape: its own control writes the value through a manager method that calls `_save_settings_file()` directly and emits nothing, because `settings_changed` re-applies terminal settings to every pane in every workspace and such a setting changes no pane (`set_sidebar_folded` is the instance). `save_settings()` stays the announcing writer for every real settings save. Pane-local settings that are NOT terminal settings (e.g. `cfg_reasoning_max_turns`, `cfg_reasoning_max_turn_bytes`) are read by the pane from `SettingsManager` at `_ready` with clamps - changes apply to panes created afterward; no `apply_to_terminal` wiring.
- First-run shell: `SettingsManager.default_shell_command()` - `/bin/bash` on Unix, `%COMSPEC%` (falling back to `cmd.exe`) on Windows. The Windows branch exists because a POSIX path is not absolute there and `validate_executable` refuses it, so every pane of a fresh Windows install failed to start. `pane-run` picks the "run this and exit" flag from the shell family with `PaneTypes.shell_run_args()` (`/c` for `cmd.exe`, `-c` otherwise) - the pane API runs through the user's configured shell, so the flag cannot be hard-coded.
- Terminal spawning: `TerminalManager.spawn_pane()` (builds the body and auto-splits) and `create_body()` (a body for `_restore_into`'s own geometry) are the two constructors; a *live* pane only ever arrives through `Workspace._spawn_pane_into`, which is what `newPane`, `paneRun`, the palette, the sidebar, a `request_pane` and a profile activation all call. A terminal's child is **not** started by `_ready`: `TerminalPane._start_child_if_ready` is the one `start_shell` call site, and it runs on the first size the pane is drawn at (`_grid_for_size`, shared with the resize debounce, which opens the pty at that size). `Workspace._prime_restored_workspaces` is the caller that is not a draw: one restored workspace per frame after the launch frame, passing the rect the tile will be drawn at as `size_hint`, so a workspace that has never been shown still has its programs running - the pane's own size wins once the container has sorted it. So a new spawn path has to let `Workspace._apply_layout` position the tile (`PaneBody.mark_tile_laid_out`) - a body added without going through it has no child, by design - and every pane that must know its drawn size waits for that hook instead of reading `size` in `_ready`. The corollary for the control surface: a pane-creating IPC answer is only true once the child exists, so `WorkspaceIpcHandlers.dispatch_request` holds any answer carrying a `pane_id` through `Workspace._hold_pane_answer` until the pane reports its start — `TerminalPane.child_started` (answer the document) or `child_start_failed` (answer `start_shell`'s sentence, toast it, close the tile) — and a new pane type that starts asynchronously must emit the same pair rather than answering a claim it cannot keep.
- Pane ceiling: `Workspace.MAX_LIVE_PANES` (96) bounds live panes for the whole window - every workspace, because a pane in a workspace that has been shown keeps its PTY, child process and grid while the workspace is hidden, and a restored pane starts holding a slot the moment its tile exists (its child starts while the workspace is still hidden - the launch primer lays the restored set out and starts its children one workspace per frame) - and `Workspace._pane_ceiling_refusal()` is the one decision that says no, carrying the limit in its text. Two creation paths consult it: `_spawn_pane_into` (nothing is built when it refuses; `_live_pane_room()` is the shared room check), and `_restore_into` (a layout, profile or workspace store restores what fits and toasts `Restored N of M panes.` plus that same text). A new pane-creation path that skips it reintroduces the unbounded spawn the ceiling closed; the constant's doc comment carries the measurement behind the number.
- Layout Constraints: The tiling grid relies on Godot `Control` nodes. Prefer using Godot's built-in Size Flags (Expand/Fill) inside containers (`HBoxContainer`/`VBoxContainer`) over manual pixel math. When manual math is absolutely required (like terminal cell reflows), hook into `_notification(NOTIFICATION_RESIZED)`.
- Pane activation & keyboard routing: clicking any pane (body, titlebar, or inner widget) makes it the active pane - workspace `_input` hit-tests tile wrappers with `event.position` (raw input, because inner RichTextLabels/ScrollContainers consume clicks before `_unhandled_input` ever fires). Only terminals take keyboard focus: activating a non-terminal pane releases the previous focus owner so keystrokes stop flowing to the terminal the user just left (read-only panes swallow keys by design - uniform click-to-activate, no fall-through; the one deliberate exception is the wiki pane's Escape-to-list, which reads the input stage and scopes itself to its own focus owner, traps in `pitfalls.md`). That rule lives in exactly one place, `Workspace.activate_pane(body)` (records `last_body` in the body's own workspace, then `_take_focus()` for a terminal and a focus release otherwise) - the three activation paths (click, sidebar row, IPC `focusPane`) all call it, because the copies had already drifted: `focusPane` called `grab_focus()` unconditionally, so focusing a read-only pane raised an engine error and activated nothing while still answering `success: true`. A focusable child (Inspector input) re-resolves its owning pane each frame in `_refresh_status_bar` via `_body_of_focus_owner`. Profile activation must end with `_apply_active_workspace_view()` - the same refresh path as workspace switching - or restored wrappers stay unlaid-out and the sidebar pane list stale. That refresh is also where a workspace with no remembered active pane resolves one: launch, a restored workspace never visited, and a profile rebuild all leave `last_body` null, because it is only set by a click, a spawn, or a focus event. `_fallback_active_body()` picks the first terminal (only terminals take keyboard focus), falling back to the first pane so a read-only workspace still has an active row, and the result goes through `activate_pane` like every other path - without it the first keystroke after launch reached nothing until the user clicked a pane (UX-01).
- Overlay keyboard ownership: the four workspace overlays (Settings, Pane Settings, the command palette, the concept graph editor) extend `OverlayPanel` and own the keyboard while visible. `Workspace._keyboard_overlay()` is the one predicate, in stacking order (palette, concept editor, settings, pane settings), and Escape is handled in `Workspace._input` - before GUI - because a focused terminal consumes every key in `_gui_input` and would turn Escape into the raw ESC byte its child expects; no overlay may handle Escape in `_unhandled_input` (all four copies were dead while a terminal held focus). An overlay is shown with `open()` (never a bare `visible = true`): it remembers the focus owner and focuses a control inside (`_initial_focus()` or the first reachable descendant), so a typed character lands in the overlay instead of the shell. `close()` hides it and emits `keyboard_released` only when it still owned the keyboard, so a click that already moved focus is never overridden; the workspace then focuses the overlay underneath (the concept editor over Settings; when that overlay's remembered control is gone it takes a control again through `grab_keyboard()`, never leaving the keyboard to the terminal behind a visible overlay) or the active pane. While an overlay is open, `_activate_pane_under_mouse` does nothing: the raw stage runs before GUI picking, so without that rule a click on a panel would re-focus the pane behind it. A new overlay joins `OverlayPanel` and `_keyboard_overlay()`; `test_overlay_focus.gd` is the contract test (typing never reaches the PTY, Escape closes without writing the ESC byte, focus returns). `ShortcutManager` asks `overlay_owns_keyboard` (injected by `Workspace` from `_keyboard_overlay()`) before it acts; `register(..., survives_overlay = true)` is only for window actions, so a refused chord is consumed instead of spawning or resetting behind the panel. The palette's entries are data (`ui/palette_model.gd`); its rows are `FOCUS_NONE` buttons under one field, the arrow keys move a `UiTheme.SELECTED_ROW` cursor, and a row's chord is `ShortcutManager.chord(action)` - never a repeated literal.
- Pane chrome is a keyboard toolbar: a pane's title-bar buttons are `FOCUS_ALL` with an explicit `focus_next`/`focus_previous` ring (`TerminalManager._wire_chrome_keyboard`), so Tab moves through the three controls and wraps instead of leaking into the next tile, and the body's own `focus_next` points at the first of them. There are three, not five - **pane settings**, the **actions menu**, **close** - because the type list alone used to cost a whole button (122 px of bar reserved, 74 now). `TerminalManager.show_pane_actions_popup` is the one definition of what a pane can do: minimize/restore, **Swap pane**, and **Switch pane type**, which opens the eight types in a second popup with their Phosphor icon and the current one radio-checked; both the workspace rows and the pane actions build native items through `ui/menu_items.gd` (`MenuItems.add`/`add_radio`), built per open and freed on close. The sidebar's pane row opens the same builder, so the two surfaces cannot list different actions or disagree about a pane's type, and choosing the current type is a no-op (`swap_pane` does allow a same-type swap, which would silently rebuild the pane). A focused terminal consumes Tab for its child, so the way in is the `Ctrl+Shift+E` shortcut (`Workspace._focus_active_pane_chrome`, which does nothing while an overlay owns the keyboard) and the way out is Escape (`Workspace._escape_pane_chrome`). A chrome action that leaves the pane on screen hands the keyboard back (`TerminalManager._return_focus_to_body`): a mouse click focuses the clicked button, and a focused button swallows the next keystroke. A terminal takes the keyboard itself; another pane may name its own entry point (`PaneBody.keyboard_entry` - a wiki pane with an open note aims at its buffer, not at a top-row action), and a pane without one gets its first reachable control (`KeyboardFocus.first_reachable`, the same walk an overlay uses on open). Read Escape at an input stage with a focus-owner check, never in `_gui_input` - on 4.7.2 `_gui_input` is delivered to the focused control only and does not bubble to ancestors (measured: a focused Button under an `outer.gui_input` delivered nothing to the outer control).
- Pane surfaces are shared, not per-pane: `PaneBody.CONTENT_INSET` (6 px) is the margin every text pane keeps from the tile's own 1 px border, applied with `PaneBody._fill_content(root)` - not a `MarginContainer` wrapper, which would move node paths the panes and tests already address - and the panes whose surface is its own pixels edge to edge (the terminal grid, whose inner padding is its own setting, and the media video) do not call it. `PaneBody.empty_state(content, glyph, title, hint, font_px)` is the one "nothing to show" surface (centred hero glyph, title, and a sentence naming the fix; the title clips at a 200 px minimum so file-supplied text cannot widen the pane): media, the code viewer and the file tree use it, and a pane that owns its wording rewrites the returned `{host, title, hint}`. `PaneBody.empty_state_font(title, hint, font_px)` re-applies the pane's size to those two lines when it changes; every pane that owns an empty-state surface calls it from `_recompute_cell_metrics`. The wiki pane's single centred sentence is a deliberate exception - its toolbar stays live above it and its messages are one-line diagnostics.
- Pane scroll chevrons are one widget: `ui/scroll_hints.gd` (`ScrollHints.attach(pane, region[, up_name, down_name])`) overlays the two 24x24 mouse-only chevrons on a pane, and the pane binds it to its own scroller - `bind_bar(bar)` for a `ScrollBar` (a `ScrollContainer`, `TextEdit`, `CodeEdit` or `RichTextLabel`), `bind_tree(tree)` for a `Tree`, `bind_custom(can_up, can_down, to_top, to_bottom)` for a surface with no `Range` behind it (the terminal grid). Each chevron is visible only while its direction has content (a body that fits its viewport shows neither), the pair is inset past a bound scrollbar's column (the terminal keeps its 6 px corner), and the widget syncs itself on the scroller's signals - `sync()` is the pane's call only where the binding has none (a `Tree`'s items, the terminal's offset). A new scrolling pane attaches the widget instead of building its own button.
- Every chrome toolbar is a keyboard ring entered by a chord: `KeyboardFocus.reachable_children(row)` picks the row's stops and `KeyboardFocus.ring(...)` wires `focus_next`/`focus_previous`, so Tab wraps inside the bar instead of leaking into the next tile. A focused terminal or `CodeEdit` keeps Tab for its child, so a chord is the way in and Escape is the way out, one level per press: the window's own bar (`Ctrl+Shift+A` → `WindowChrome.focus_controls`, Escape → `_escape_window_chrome` → `_return_focus_to_body`), a pane's own action row (`Ctrl+Shift+L` → `PaneBody.focus_toolbar`, Escape → `Workspace._escape_pane_toolbar` → `leave_toolbar`), and the wiki note toolbar (`Ctrl+Shift+K` → `WikiPane.focus_note_toolbar`, Escape → the same shared step; `WikiPane._wire_note_toolbar` still builds that row from the same pair). A view pane joins by assigning `PaneBody._action_bar` (`CodeViewerPane` rings Reload/the view toggle from `_refresh_view`, `CliViewPane` Restart/Stop from `_sync_buttons`) and overriding `keyboard_entry()` with the surface a reader continues in - the base `leave_toolbar()` returns there and never back into the bar, and a pane whose buffer is not on screen (wiki `preview`) answers Back instead of null. Chords that resolve "the pane" do it from the focus owner and only then fall back to `last_body` - `last_body` alone was measured wrong, because a wiki pane opened from its own list kept the startup terminal as the active pane, so the chord did nothing from the very buffer it exists for - and they are inert while an overlay owns the keyboard. Two rules the engine forces, both in `pitfalls.md`: a button that becomes disabled must also lose its focus mode, and a ring rebuilt from what is on screen must be allowed to shrink to one member (`KeyboardFocus.ring` then clears both paths instead of writing a `"."` self-path). `Workspace._input` is the one Escape ladder - overlay, pane chrome, window bar, pane toolbar - and each step is scoped to its own focus owner.
- The link graph is the same pattern one surface over: each presentation makes the canvas and its actions one ring with the canvas first (`VaultGraphCanvas` is the shared contract; `VaultGraphView` and `VaultGraph3D` build their own chrome and ring), so Tab cycles the map's own controls and never leaks into the sidebar. Each view draws its own focus frame and crosshair (a custom-drawn Control has no stylebox to do it), arrows pan, `+`/`-` zoom about the centre, and Enter acts on `cursor_hit()` - the node under the crosshair, else the edge under it - so the keyboard and the pointer share one `VaultGraphModel.hit_test`/`hit_test_edge` answer instead of a second navigation model (the 3D view projects the bodies to screen positions first; it does not add a physics raycast). Labels are a placement problem, not a per-node draw: each view's `label_placements` orders candidates by what the user is aiming at then by degree, `VaultGraphModel.cull_labels` drops any box that would print over an accepted one, and `fit_to_view` reserves the widest label so the fitted map's right-hand labels stay inside the view - without that, a 52-note vault prints its titles on top of each other (measured, and the row that closed it).
- List cursors and mouse-only declarations live in the same module: `KeyboardFocus.next_index(current, count, delta)` is the one clamped cursor step (the ends are stops, and `-1` means nothing is selected yet), used by the command palette's rows and by the search strip's History results; and `KeyboardFocus.declare_mouse_only(control, reason)` records why a `FOCUS_NONE` control leaves its action to a chord or to a field - `mouse_only_reason` reads it back, and `scripts/ui-capture --audit-focus` prints a declared control with that reason and counts only undeclared ones as `unaccounted`. A new mouse-only button in the app's own chrome declares one, or the audit reports it as an oversight.
- Capture Bridge: Rust never calls into Godot. GDScript polls the backend from `_process()` - `drain_concept_events()` for completed captures and `drain_agent_events()` for Tier 1 agent state.
- Agent-state observation contract: `PaneBody.agent_state_source_id()` names the terminal a pane observes by stable `attachment_id` (a terminal returns its own id - the tiered tracker it reads *is* that terminal's state; empty = observes nothing, the base default) and `PaneBody.on_agent_state_changed(state)` receives that terminal's state. `workspace.gd` is the only dispatcher: `TerminalPane.agent_state_changed` (emitted from the slow poll on a real transition) calls `_dispatch_agent_state`, and a per-frame `_prime_new_pane_observers` scan delivers the current state once, to the new pane alone, through `_tell_observer` - any pane-entry route (spawn, restore, swap, a future pane SDK), a follower whose terminal appears later (retried), and a pane re-pointed at a different source (the stored record is the source it was primed for plus the state it was last told), all without re-priming a settled pane. A change dispatch reaches only panes already settled for that source - delivering to an unsettled one would make the scan's entry the duplicate - and `_tell_observer` drops a value the observer already holds, the dispatcher-side mirror of the terminal's own `_badge_state` rule, so no observer hears the same state twice whichever path carried it. Panes are found through the `panes` group, so hidden workspaces keep observing their own; the source terminal is resolved **inside the observer's own workspace** (`_workspace_for_body` then `_terminal_for_agent_state`), so a companion left pointing at another workspace's id observes nothing instead of that terminal. Agent events follow the same rule: `_route_agent_events` groups receivers by workspace and delivers only inside the emitting terminal's own (`_poll_agent_events` is just the FFI drain). The titlebar badge is the first implementation and runs *through* this path (`TerminalPane.on_agent_state_changed` applies it), not beside it: the hook also records the delivery (`_badge_state` is what the pane was last told), and the slow poll reports only deltas against it - its first read before any delivery is adopted silently, so the entry prime stays the single delivery of the spawn state instead of the poll re-announcing it as a change. Display only: a Tier 2 declaration is spoofable by anything that prints and Tier 3 is a heuristic, so a hook must never feed a decision, an action, a capture, or IPC. The badge itself is `ui/agent_badge.gd` (`AgentBadge`): the control owns the state table, the tint role, the tooltip and the accessible name, and its own animation clock, so `TerminalPane._apply_badge` only hands it the state. `working` is painted - a filled 2 px ring with a moving notch - because the font's spinner shapes are thin arcs that measured at half its siblings' ink at badge size, while the other three states stay Phosphor glyphs; a state that needs a new silhouette is a row in `STATES` and, if it is drawn, a glyph in `icons.gd`.

- Pane status contract: `PaneBody.status_document() -> Variant` is the generic `paneStatus` hook (null when the pane has no primitives). `TerminalPane` returns its process/grid document unchanged; `MediaPane` returns `{kind,file,state,position_us,duration_us,paused,loop,volume_db,muted}` while a file is open. `ipc_handlers.gd` uses the hook for both the aggregate (a pane without primitives keeps `status: null` rather than disappearing) and a targeted request (a generic "no status primitives" error, never "not found"). Any future pane that has observable state implements the override; do not add a per-type branch in the IPC handler.
- Deferred IPC answers: a routed method that cannot answer inside the drain loop books its request id on the workspace and answers later, never by blocking. Three methods do: `paneWait` (`_pending_waits`, answered by `_poll_pending_waits`), `pluginInstall` (`_pending_plugin_reviews`, answered by the review dialog) and `paneView --graph` (`_pending_graph_answers`, answered from the pane's `graph_built` signal, connected `CONNECT_ONE_SHOT`). Each books in `WorkspaceIpcHandlers.dispatch_request`, which is the only place that holds the request id — so its branch lives there, at one tab, and its validation stays inline in that branch because `mcp.rs` parses the branches from source as a method set and `wire.rs` reads the `params.get("…")` keys in them. Each has a deadline sweep in `Workspace._process` that answers before the Rust edge's fallback (the graph's fires `GRAPH_ANSWER_MARGIN_MS` early), so a caller reads the handler's sentence instead of a generic timeout. The work itself never runs on the frame: a computation that scales with data is a `WorkerThreadPool` task polled from `_process` (`WikiPane._poll_graph_build`, whose task writes one output slot and touches no node or autoload), and the pane reports the outcome through a signal.
- Close contract: `PaneBody.request_close(answer)` asks before a pane is destroyed, and `PaneBody.has_unsaved_state()` is its state half. `answer` receives a bool - `true` proceeds with the teardown, `false` cancels the whole action - and it may arrive **deferred** (the wiki pane opens a Save/Discard/Cancel dialog), so a caller passes a continuation, never destroys the pane itself, and must honour the bool it gets back (a continuation that ignores it turns a Cancel into a go-ahead - measured: the leave button closed the note it had just been told to keep). The base answers `true` at once, so a pane with nothing to lose never asks. Every destruction path goes through it: `Workspace._kill`/`_kill_now` (the titlebar X, the sidebar's close button, `Ctrl+Shift+W`, the palette, IPC `killPane`), `_swap_pane` (the old body dies), `_reset`/`_do_reset`/`_do_activate` (reset, profile activation) and `_close_workspace`/`_restore`, plus `request_quit()` - the app's only quit path, reached from the window manager's close request (`auto_accept_quit` is off), the titlebar's close button and the Rust shutdown flag (`daemon stop`, a refused socket bind) - which walks every pane of every workspace through the same ask (a Cancel cancels the quit; `quit_action` is the seam the tests replace, and the `_quit_asking` flag is cleared on both answers so a canceled quit can be asked again). `_ask_close_then(bodies, next, declined, ask_running, action, qualify_entries)` is the one walk, in two phases: stopping **running processes** is the action's hazard, so `_ask_running_then` asks once for the whole set - `PaneBody.has_running_work()` - and the consent text is the caller's action phrase plus the busy/total pane counts (`running_ask_intro`) and one line per busy pane naming its label and `PaneBody.display_name()` (`running_ask_entry`), qualified by its workspace unless the action phrase already named it (`qualify_entries`) - and only then does each pane answer for work only it can describe (the wiki's Save/Discard/Cancel) through `request_close`; a bulk close of sixteen terminals must not raise sixteen dialogs. A refusal at either phase stops the walk, so panes it had not reached are never asked. `TerminalPane.has_running_work()` reads the status document's `foreground_job`: Unix is exact (`portable-pty`'s `process_group_leader()`/`tcgetpgrp` on the master compared with the spawned child, so `cmd &` does not count and a pane whose configured program *is* the child reports none), while Windows/ConPTY has no foreground-group notion and answers `null`, which the pane must treat as busy while the shell runs - the conservative fallback. The sample is exact only for a live task: `running` is `exit_code.is_none() && task_alive` (`engine.rs`), so a pane whose I/O task ended while its child survived reports idle — that pane closes nothing by itself, and the status document's `child_alive` (the task's last `try_wait` answer) is what makes it ask, since teardown still SIGKILLs the surviving process group. `TerminalPane.running_work_from_status` is that decision in one pure function, unit-tested against every document state (`tests/unit/test_terminal_running_work.gd`). `_kill`/`_swap_pane` route through the same two-phase walk, so a titlebar X, `Ctrl+Shift+W`, the palette, a type swap and a workspace close all ask the same way. A caller that cannot answer a dialog - IPC - must not ask: it checks `has_unsaved_state()` and refuses with an error naming the pane (`killPane`, `profileLoad`, the rule `profileLoad` already applied to an untrusted profile). Stopping processes is not refused, because naming a kill or a load is consent to it: `killPane` calls the `_kill_now` primitive and `profileLoad` activates with `ask_running: false`.

- Pane request contract: panes never spawn panes. A body that needs another pane emits `PaneBody.request_pane(type, settings)`; the workspace connects it in `_attach_pane_into` (so every entry route - spawn, restore, swap - carries it) and answers through `_spawn_pane_into` followed by `activate_pane`, holding `type` to `PaneTypes.ALL` so the spawn surface stays closed. The same choke point wires `body.title_changed` to `TerminalManager.set_title_label` for **every** type - a rename is not a terminal-only feature, and it arrives from the pane settings panel and from `paneSet`, so a connection made only in `spawn_pane`'s terminal branch left a renamed viewer's title bar stale. The workspace may answer with an existing pane: a `code_viewer` request for a file some viewer in that workspace already shows is focused and not duplicated (a viewer's scroll, selection and rendered/source mode belong to its document, so silently repointing one is rejected; a second view is a deliberate second viewer), which is why an emitter must not assume its request created anything and why the viewer needs the explicit Reload action. The file tree's `open_in` is per-tree state (`viewer` default, `system` optional), saved in the tile like `root_path`; the origin owns the choice rather than a global setting.

gPTY is a graphical PTY foundation with an observability layer. It does **not** recreate agent TUIs, scrape PTY output for agent semantics, or host the user's interactive OMP/Claude/Gemini session.

| Surface | Role |
|---------|------|
| Terminal | User launches `omp` (or any CLI) normally. The CLI owns its TUI, auth, tools, and permissions. |
| Inspector | Private, tool-free, iterative Q&A. Owns one in-memory `GptyAi` session; backends: `omp` (private `omp --mode rpc --no-session --no-tools --no-extensions --no-skills --no-rules`), `mock`, or `cli` (subprocess NDJSON bridge - a configured adapter command, argv never shell-evaluated, documented hooks only). Does not attach to the terminal's agent process. |
| Reasoning | Passive view of documented reasoning/lifecycle events from **one** terminal in its own workspace, selected by `source_attachment_id`. Never starts jobs or accepts concept captures. Turn history is an in-memory accordion for the terminal's current agent session only. |
| `@gpty/omp-events` | Explicitly installed OMP extension. Dormant unless its configuration is complete: `GPTY_EVENT_PROTOCOL` = `1`, `GPTY_EVENT_SOCKET`, `GPTY_EVENT_CAPABILITY` and `GPTY_TERMINAL_SESSION_ID` (`transport.js`'s `readConfiguration`). Forwards bounded session/turn/tool metadata plus `thinking_delta` text only, **coalesced** (one event per 16 ms / ≤8 KiB UTF-8, split on code points). |

- Inspector and Reasoning are **different sessions**. The shipped "Agent Workspace" profile opens Terminal + Inspector + Reasoning; only Reasoning is attached to the terminal.
- Event delivery is **workspace-scoped**. The workspace resolves the emitting PTY by its FFI `terminal_session_id` and fans the envelope out only to receivers in that terminal's own workspace (`Workspace._route_agent_events`); a hidden workspace still receives its own events. Activating the same profile in a second workspace reuses its logical ids, so `_restore_into` pre-resolves the duplicate terminal's id and rewrites the Reasoning pane's `source_attachment_id` before either body exists — a Reasoning pane can never show another workspace's stream. A **Pane Settings rename** of a terminal is retargeted the same way in that terminal's own workspace (`settings_applied` → `Workspace._retarget_companions` → `ReasoningPane.retarget_source`): a follower opts in by implementing `retarget_source`, which keeps the bound session and turns because the terminal never restarted — `apply_settings` stays the path for a *different* source and resets them.
- A **pane move** (`movePane`; the pane menu's Move to workspace) keeps the link whole: the transaction moves a terminal together with the panes in its own workspace whose `source_attachment_id` names it, so a Reasoning pane cannot be left behind by its own terminal; a follower moved on its own keeps the id and observes nothing until it is co-located again, which the move warns about.
- Reasoning history is session-scoped RAM (collapsed previous turns, live turn streaming). Closing the pane, changing `source_attachment_id`, or binding a new `omp_session_id` drops it. Do not write thinking text or OMP session IDs into layout/profile JSON.
- **The event listener runs on every platform.** Workspace control IPC works on Windows (named pipes); the event listener serves `\\.\pipe\gpty-events` there and `gpty-events.sock` on Unix, and per-PTY `GPTY_EVENT_*` injection happens on both. The shipped `@gpty/omp-events` extension needs no platform branch to reach either one: `net.connect(path)` opens a Unix socket for a socket path and a named pipe for a pipe path, and the only branch is validation (`validateSocket` says a Windows path must be a `\\.\pipe\` name, answered from the path alone because a pipe cannot be `stat`ed). `scripts/smoke_pane_api.py` runs the extension inside a real pane and asserts the pane reports Tier 1 `working`, so the chain - env injection, transport, capability check, translation, drain - is observed live on the platform running the smoke (Linux locally, `windows-smoke` in CI).
- `GptyAi` is instance-owned: `session_open` / `session_prompt` / `session_poll` / `session_cancel` / `session_close`. There is no process-global subscriber bus. Polled envelopes carry `session_id`, `turn_id`, `run_id`, `sequence`, `channel`.
- Reasoning caps are user settings (Settings → Reasoning tab): `cfg_reasoning_max_turns` (clamped 1–64, default 16) and `cfg_reasoning_max_turn_bytes` (clamped 4 KiB–1 MiB, default 64 KiB). `reasoning_pane.gd` reads them at `_ready` into `max_turns`/`max_turn_bytes` (not consts). When truncating accumulated raw Markdown at the cap, re-close an odd number of ``` fences (`_close_open_fences`) - an unclosed fence re-renders the tail as code. The cap is **visible**: the first time a turn reaches it the view gets a source notice (`set_source_notice`) saying later reasoning is not shown, and `truncated`/`text_bytes` ride in the turn record. Appends are O(delta), not O(turn): the byte count is incremental and a delta that arrives after the cap returns before any concatenation or UTF-8 re-encoding (the old path paid two full `to_utf8_buffer()` copies per dropped delta - 486 ms for one 64 KiB capped turn, now 31 ms; `godot/tests/bench/reasoning_bench.gd`).
- Reasoning streaming is four rules that must not regress: (a) **only the changed turn renders** - `_refresh_turn_layout` syncs fold heights and never calls `set_markdown`; re-rendering every turn on every delta re-parsed the whole accordion and cleared any selection; (b) **one deferred layout refresh per frame**, not per delta (a burst of 200 deltas used to enqueue 200 walks of every turn); (c) **a held selection pauses the coalesced render** (`MarkdownView._apply_pending` restarts its timer while `get_selected_text() != ""`; `render_now` for explicit acts is not deferred); (d) **the live turn follows the bottom by intent** - `_follow_live` is cleared when the user scrolls away from the bottom and re-armed when they return (or a new turn starts), and the scrollbar's `changed` signal re-scrolls after the layout that follows a render. A distance test taken at scroll time is not enough: content grows by whole lines between renders, so the write clamps at the previous bottom and the follow stops. `reasoning_bench.gd` measures the append/render split (64 KiB: 14 ms append, 11 ms render; 256 KiB: 120/41; 256 KiB into a 64 KiB cap: 31/10, against 486 ms for the old capped path). `GPTY_REASONING_DEBUG=1` prints one line a second - deltas/bytes in, renders/render-ms out, turn/cap state, and `GptyTerminal.omp_event_stats()`'s accepted/rejected/queued counters - which is how a lossy input stream is told apart from a slow renderer. The status line is a selectable `RichTextLabel` with the context menu, and every `MarkdownView` enables selection + the Copy menu.
- The accordion **never assigns a minimum width** to a turn view. A `custom_minimum_size.x` there propagates through the fold, the turn list and the horizontal-scroll-disabled `ScrollContainer`, and an anchored parent clamps to its combined minimum, so a narrowing pane kept the old layout and never re-wrapped (fixed 2026-11-17). The container owns the width; `_sync_fold_height` assigns only the height and re-runs from the view's `resized` signal.
- Inspector aim is **user-owned state, never file state** (v0.7.1): `PaneTypes.INSPECTOR_SETTINGS` marks `system_prompt`, `auto_run` and `accept_concept_captures` `file: false`, and `_get_layout_state` does not save them, so a profile, layout or workspace file cannot point the pane at a prompt or turn auto-send on - a shared profile plus a routing concept would otherwise send captured output to a model with no gesture. The user's own values live in `PaneInspectorStore` (`user://pane_inspector.json`, the `PaneEnvStore` pattern: id-pattern keys, typed reads, caps, one bad entry costs itself), written only by the pane settings panel's `settings_applied` handler and overlaid at attach by `PaneBody.apply_user_state` (`InspectorPane` overrides it). The control surface is held to the same line: `paneSet`/`new-pane --setting` run the table with `SOURCE_IPC`, which marks those three keys `ipc: false`, so a socket caller is refused (`-32602`) instead of aiming a live pane at a prompt that would not survive a restart and would leave no record the user could revoke. That runs after `_ensure_unique_attachment_id`, so every entry route - spawn, restore, type swap - applies the record for the id the pane actually carries; a user rename moves the entry, a duplicate-id collision copies it, clearing the prompt and both switches removes it, and closing the pane removes it in `_kill_now` (restart, profile activation, close-all, workspace close and layout restore reset the manager directly, so the aim survives those). A restored pane therefore comes back on the user's own aim, and its first auto-send is still a gesture made in the panel. Do NOT save the keys into a layout or re-add a file path for them - either reopens the hole.
- Do not add Claude/Gemini/Antigravity adapters that read OAuth tokens, call private endpoints, or parse undocumented TUI output. Future adapters may use only that CLI's documented hooks/extensions, with a fresh terms review.

Curated traps, subtle engine behaviors, and invariants for Godot 4.7+ and GDScript development.

## Theming, Styling & Colors

- **Pressed-state text color ignores `font_color`:** A toggle-mode `Button` resolves text from `font_pressed_color`, which falls back to the theme default and silently ignores `font_color`. Use a type variation role (e.g., `UiTheme.ACCENT_BUTTON`), which defines `font_color`, `font_hover_color`, `font_pressed_color`, and `font_focus_color` together in the theme.
- **ScrollBar thickness is derived from content margins:** Godot derives `ScrollBar` thickness from the track stylebox's content margins plus padding constants (`VScrollBar.padding_left`/`padding_right`), while the grabber stylebox margins only determine thumb minimum length. An empty track (`StyleBoxEmpty`) creates a 0 px bar with no column reserved. Geometry is theme-owned (`UiTokens.SCROLLBAR_THICKNESS`/`SCROLLBAR_INSET`/`SCROLLBAR_MIN_THUMB`).
- **Embedded Window frame uses default theme:** `Window/embedded_border` and `embedded_unfocused_border` have no effect in Godot 4.7.2. An `AcceptDialog` lays out every direct child Control over the same content rect (requiring a single root `VBoxContainer`), and its internal `dialog_text` keeps rendering until hidden. `AppDialog` builds borderless modals with custom headers.
- **A per-surface `modulate` is not a translucent window:** `Window.transparent`/`transparent_bg` plus a `Workspace.modulate` alpha makes every stacked surface blend again instead of fading the finished window - the terminal's row backgrounds, its ground and the window ground compounded to framebuffer alpha **0.992** at a 70 % setting (measured 2026-11-20 on 4.7.2). A whole-window alpha is one post-pass: `godot/shaders/window_opacity.gdshader` samples a `BackBufferCopy` placed above every app surface, and `render_mode blend_disabled` writes the sample renormalised to the setting's alpha; `Workspace.apply_window_alpha` hides the copy and the veil at 100 %, so an opaque window pays nothing. Embedded dialogs, file pickers and popup menus draw after the canvas and stay opaque. Where `DisplayServer.is_window_transparency_available()` is false - the X11 driver a Wayland desktop runs, unless it is started with `--display-driver wayland` - the Settings row is still shown, disabled, with `SettingsPanel.opacity_hint`'s reason beside it: hiding the row read as a feature that was never shipped.
- **Window transparency needs `transparent_bg` and a real display to prove it:** with it off, a written 0.5 alpha read back **0.333** (the channel is not 8-bit); the headless display server refuses `Window.transparent` even when it is set directly, so a GUT test asserts the viewport/veil half and the window flag is proven on a headed run. `project.godot` must also set `display/window/per_pixel_transparency/allowed`, or the engine answers `is_window_transparency_available()` false even on a renderer that supports it.
- **The boot splash is drawn before the palette exists:** the engine paints `application/boot_splash/image` before any script or autoload, so the frame cannot read `user://settings.json`, `UiPalette.active()` or the UI scale. It is one fixed picture: `project.godot` pins `bg_color` and the art's edges to the dark `UiPalette.DARK["SURFACE"]` (`#202128`) and `test_boot_splash.gd` fails when the image, corners, colour or `stretch_mode` drift. A theme-following launch is a first-frame overlay, not a second splash; prove the engine's frame with `scripts/screenshot-gpty`, because `scripts/ui-capture` only sees the app viewport after the splash.
- **A CanvasItem material applies to every draw command of that item, not to the item as a whole:** the terminal's grid is one canvas of per-row bands, glyph runs and rects, so a `ShaderMaterial` there runs once per command with the font atlas as `TEXTURE` and each rect's tint in `COLOR` - a CRT material on the grid treats glyphs as textures and loses every rect's colour (measured on the orphan `crt.gdshader`, whose `COLOR = texture(TEXTURE, uv)` made a tinted overlay opaque white). A pane-scale effect gets its own single-command layer instead: `PaneEffects` owns the material and the buffer, `Layer.EFFECT` is one `draw_rect` or one `draw_texture_rect`, and the pane skips its own ground and the row runs at the default background while that layer is active. A `TIME`-driven effect also belongs in a half-resolution `SubViewport` at 30 Hz - full-resolution per-frame shader work is the expensive half (0.29 ms/frame at 1080p and 1.02 ms at 4K for a 4-octave FBM tree, testing.md) - and `phase` as a uniform rather than `TIME` keeps captures repeatable. An additive term is what makes a comb visible on a black ground; multiplying alone changes nothing there.
- **Palette reads in initializers freeze mode:** An `@export var c: Color = UiPalette.active().X` evaluates once at definition time and freezes whichever theme mode was active at construction. Read colors at draw time or use `Theme` type variations. `scripts/check-theme-tokens` fails class-body `UiPalette.active()` reads and `add_theme_color_override`.
- **Ancestor theme resolves only after entering the tree:** A script probe setting `host.theme = UiTheme.build()` and checking `get_theme_stylebox("panel")` in the same frame gets Godot's default theme. Await one `process_frame` first for variation lookup to resolve.
- **Phosphor glyph `Label` instantiation cost:** In Godot 4.7.2, `add_child` of a `Label` carrying a Phosphor PUA codepoint costs 3.3–3.5 ms (vs. 0.09 ms for ASCII), and re-assigning `text` on an attached label costs ~0.00 ms. Update labels and glyphs in place; avoid recreation during workspace or tab switching.

## Node Hierarchy, Sizing & Viewports

- **`extends Node` cannot render `Control` children:** Only `Control` nodes render child `Control`s (`Label`, `Button`, etc.). A `Label` parented to a plain `Node` is completely invisible. Containers must extend `Control`.
- **Textless Buttons collapse without explicit minimum width/height:** Godot does not derive a `Button`'s minimum size from child Controls. A button that carries an icon+text `HBox` instead of native `text` needs an explicit `custom_minimum_size.y`.
- **Width floor inside scroll children freezes layout:** Setting `custom_minimum_size.x` on a `RichTextLabel` inside a horizontal-scroll-disabled `ScrollContainer` propagates upward and prevents shrinking. The container must own width; sync only height from `get_content_height()` and re-run on `resized`.
- **`TabContainer` owns its internal `TabBar`'s theme items:** The engine copies the `TabContainer`'s tab styleboxes, font colours and font size onto the internal `TabBar` as overrides; entries registered on `TabBar` alone leave the live bar on the engine default (10 px a side plus 1 px borders, 20 px per tab). Set the tab box and font colours on **both** types - `UiTheme` shares the same `StyleBox` objects - and remember the default `side_margin` indents the bar 8 px on the left (zero it when the card already pads). A tab hidden by an overflow reports a zero-based rect from `get_tab_rect()`; calculate total width by summing rect widths sequentially.
- **`Tree` does not expand on double-click by default:** `TreeItem` defaults to `collapsed = false`, and double-clicking emits `item_activated` without auto-toggling. Code that populates rows on first activation and immediately toggles `collapsed` collapses the newly populated folder.
- **3D `SubViewport` in a pane:** Sizing is `(0, 0)` on the frame the first graph is shown; units-per-pixel calculations must use the Control's height as a fallback. An `ImmediateMesh` surface is committed only on `surface_end()`. Clear `SubViewportContainer` visibility pauses (`_hidden_paused`) on the visible branch.
- **Reparenting fires `_exit_tree`:** `Node.reparent()` removes and re-adds the node. Subsystems that stop backends on tree exit (`cli_view`, `media`, `inspector`) must check `PaneBody.backend_preserved` across workspace moves.

## Focus, Keyboard & Input Handling

- **Focus traversal visits disabled buttons:** `find_next_valid_focus()` filters `FOCUS_NONE` and invisibility, but not `disabled`. A toolbar whose buttons disable must set `focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE` on disabled items, or Tab navigation will land on them.
- **Input bubbling in Godot 4.7.2:** `_gui_input` does not bubble to ancestors. An input-stage handler (`_input`) with `gui_get_focus_owner()` checks is required to handle global shortcuts like Escape without relying on container bubbling.
- **Terminal consumes keyboard:** A focused `TerminalPane` consumes all keystrokes in `_handle_keyboard`. Overlays must capture keyboard ownership on open, and handle Escape before GUI input.
- **Z-Index does not affect Control picking:** Godot GUI mouse picking checks reverse tree order (last sibling first), ignoring `z_index`. Overlays must call `move_child(overlay, -1)` on open to ensure they receive clicks ahead of earlier siblings.
- **Tooltip mouse filters:** Viewport tooltip lookup skips controls whose `mouse_filter` is `IGNORE` (the default for `Label` and `RichTextLabel`). Controls showing tooltips must set `mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` or `PASS`.

## GDScript Syntax, Lifecycles & Typing

- **No NUL character in strings:** A `\u0000` literal decodes as `\uFFFD` and triggers unexpected NUL character errors at load time. Never use NUL characters for string splitting or composite map keys; use nested dictionaries or structured objects.
- **`:=` inference fails on untyped Variant:** `var x := ws._palette._field` produces a parse error because reading a property on a `Variant` base yields `Variant`. Explicitly type the variable: `var x: LineEdit = ws._palette._field`.
- **Typed arrays (`Array[T]`):** A typed parameter `func f(arr: Array[Control])` rejects a plain `Array` at call sites. Furthermore, `Array[Dictionary]` rejects across the Rust GDExtension boundary; always pass untyped `Array` to Rust.
- **String format operator `%` with arrays:** `"...: %s" % changed` where `changed` is an `Array` treats the array as the format argument list. If the string has only one `%s`, it raises a format error for arrays with >1 element. Wrap with `% str(changed)` or pass explicit tuples.
- **Default arguments evaluate at script load:** `func f(x := some_var)` captures `some_var` at definition time, not call time. Use sentinel defaults (`func f(x := -1)`) and resolve dynamic values in the function body.
- **Reference cycles in `RefCounted`:** If object A stores object B and object B stores object A, neither is freed on exit. Use `WeakRef` on the owned child and bind methods directly instead of capturing parent instances in closures.
- **Autoload callable references:** Publishing an inline closure `ShortcutManager.overlay_owns_keyboard = func(): ...` captures the enclosing node. When the node is freed, the callable points to dead memory. Reset callbacks in `_exit_tree()`.
- **A control must not free the row it lives in from its own signal:** a picker's `item_selected` handler that rebuilds its container and calls `free()` on the old row crashes the engine with `Object ... was freed or unreferenced while a signal is being emitted from it` (measured 2026-11-21 on 4.7.2, the reactive-effects cue picker). Defer the rebuild (`_sync_reactive_rows.call_deferred()`); if the rebuild must land in the same frame, free with `queue_free()` and tolerate one frame of stale rows.

Traps and invariants across Linux, Windows, macOS, continuous integration runners, build scripts, and headless execution.

## Platform Parity & Packaging

- **Linux user namespaces and overflowuid:** In rootless Podman, Docker, Flatpak, or user namespaces where root is unmapped, system binaries (`/bin/sh`, `/usr/bin/env`) map to overflowuid 65534 (`nobody`). Path validation must permit `overflow_uid` alongside UID `me` and `0` - **but only where the kernel really substitutes it**: `pty::unmapped_owner_uid` reads `/proc/sys/fs/overflowuid` (default 65534) and accepts it only when that UID is outside `/proc/self/uid_map`, so a host with the identity map (`0 0 4294967295`) accepts nothing new and an unreadable `/proc` fails closed. The rule lives once, in `pty::validate_executable_file`; `validate_untrusted_executable` adds the no-writable-ancestor walk for paths saved data chose, while `validate_gui_binary`/`validate_omp_binary` keep only the file rule (`GPTY_GUI`/`GPTY_OMP` are the user's own choice and macOS's `/Applications` is group-writable). `crates/gpty-core/tests/userns_executable.rs` re-execs itself under `unshare -Ur` and proves a 65534-owned system binary is accepted. Do not add an overflow arm to the socket-path or peer-credential checks: those compare against this process exactly.
- **Windows process DACL hardening:** On Windows, gPTY withholds `PROCESS_VM_READ` from same-user processes to prevent unprivileged token snooping. Profilers and debuggers must run with elevated permissions or use `GPTY_ALLOW_DEBUG=1`.
- **macOS bundle naming and discovery:** On macOS, the application bundle is named `gPTY.app`, while the command-line interface binary is `gpty`. GUI binary discovery checks inside the bundle and standard application directories.
- **macOS Mach-O minimum deployment target:** Mixing object files or dynamic libraries built against different deployment targets can silently raise the minimum supported macOS version. `scripts/check-macos-minos` validates Mach-O slices against the 10.13 (x86_64) / 11.0 (arm64) deployment floor.
- **BSD `mode_t` types:** `libc::mode_t` is `u16` on BSD systems and `u32` on Linux. Raw casts like `fchmod(fd, want as libc::mode_t)` ensure cross-platform compatibility across UNIX targets.

## CI Runners, Caching & Build Hygiene

- **Runner image cache isolation:** CI caches compiled shared libraries (such as FFmpeg) and Cargo build artifacts. Caches must not be shared across incompatible OS images (e.g. `ubuntu-22.04` and `ubuntu-24.04`), as newer GLIBC symbol versions (such as `GLIBC_2.38`) break binary compatibility on older base images.
- **Self-modifying shell script execution:** Modifying a shell script (such as `scripts/ci-check`) while it is running causes bash to read offset blocks and execute corrupted commands. Always allow a test run to complete before saving edits to runner scripts.
- **Shell function exit status:** Under `set -e`, a shell function is judged by its final command. Ending a cleanup helper on `[ -n "$TMP" ] && rm -rf "$TMP"` causes the entire script to exit 1 if `$TMP` is unset. Conclude step functions with an explicit `return 0`.
- **Stable PATH symlinks vs. extract folders:** Creating a PATH symlink directly into an extracted release directory breaks when the directory is purged or updated. `scripts/install-cli` installs binaries behind a stable link (`~/.local/opt/gpty/current`).
- **Sandboxed launches and operator credentials:** Launching test harnesses or screenshot scripts from an existing terminal pane can leak `GPTY_SECRET` into child processes. Sandbox runners (`scripts/ui-sandbox`) must explicitly unset credential environment variables.

## Headless Execution Boundaries

- **Zero-size viewports:** Running Godot with `--headless` initializes the root viewport to 0×0 (or 64×64 for `-s` script probes). Layout calculations, divider positions, and responsive UI adapters cannot be validated under headless execution; use windowed capture probes (`scripts/ui-capture`).
- **Missing display drivers and hover events:** Headless execution runs without a window display driver. `Viewport.gui_get_hovered_control()` returns `null`, tooltips never trigger, and `frame_post_draw` notifications never fire. Automated UI tests should assert control properties (`mouse_filter`, `tooltip_text`) rather than simulating pointer hovers.

Traps and patterns for Rust, GDExtension (`gdext`), FFI boundaries, concurrency, and persistent storage.

## GDExtension Boundary & gdext

- **Parameter type marshaling:** In `gdext`, only `GString`, `bool`, and `i64` are reliably marshaled as direct input parameters in `#[func]` methods. Passing `Array<Variant>`, `Dictionary`, or bare `Variant` can silently fail (the GDScript call succeeds while the Rust method body never executes). Serialize complex structured payloads to JSON strings and deserialize with `serde_json`.
- **Typed arrays across FFI:** Passing a GDScript typed array like `Array[Dictionary]` to a Rust `Array<Variant>` parameter fails at runtime with type mismatch errors. Keep arrays untyped across the boundary.
- **Renamed exports break at runtime:** Renaming an exported `#[func]` is syntactically valid in GDScript but fails at runtime when the method is invoked. `scripts/check-ffi-surface` cross-checks all calls against the exported GDExtension surface.
- **Library pinning on exit:** Unloading the GDExtension shared library (`dlclose` or `FreeLibrary`) while background tokio worker or PTY reader threads are still running causes immediate segmentation faults. `pin_library()` pins the mapping using `RTLD_NODELETE` on Unix and `GetModuleHandleExW` on Windows.
- **Rebuilding maps and SIGBUS:** Overwriting a mapped `.so` in place with `cp` causes running processes to crash with `SIGBUS` ("Misaligned address error"). `scripts/build` installs extension libraries by staging to a `.new` temporary file and performing an atomic rename over the target path.

## Concurrency, Threads & Tokio

- **SceneTree is strictly single-threaded:** Never invoke Godot engine methods, emit signals, or mutate nodes from background tokio tasks or worker threads. Queue updates in bounded thread-safe channels for GDScript to poll on `_process()`, or invoke `call_deferred()`.
- **Short-lived TermGrid locks:** `TermGrid` is shared across threads via `Arc<Mutex<TermGrid>>`. Acquire the lock briefly to copy cell damage or push input, and release it immediately. Holding the lock during blocking I/O freezes the rendering thread.
- **`std::sync::Mutex` and poisoning:** Use `std::sync::Mutex` throughout. A poisoned lock indicates a thread panic; log and report via `gpty_core::lock::lock_or_warn(mutex, "what")` rather than using bare unwraps or silent ignores.
- **`tokio::pin!` + `reset()` for timeouts:** Re-arming timeouts inside capture loops should use `tokio::pin!(sleep)` and `sleep.as_mut().reset(deadline)` rather than recreating timer instances in every `select!` iteration.
- **`tokio::select!` on closed channels:** When an `mpsc::Receiver` returns `None`, `tokio::select!` disables that branch but continues spinning on remaining branches, pegging CPU at 100%. Bind the receiver explicitly and break when the channel closes.
- **Task handles detach on drop:** Dropping a `tokio::task::JoinHandle` does not abort the task; it continues running in the background. Explicitly call `handle.abort()` in `Drop` implementations when child tasks must terminate.
- **CLI single-thread runtime:** The CLI binary runs on `#[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]`. CLI commands execute single requests and exit immediately; multi-threaded worker pools add process startup overhead and introduce teardown exit races.

## Storage, SQLite & Persistence

- **Process-wide write serialization:** Multiple SQLite writer threads across panes competing for the same database file cause busy timeouts and dropped batches. `store::write_guard` provides process-wide write serialization.
- **Damaged database recovery:** A corrupted database file that begins with SQLite page bytes but lacks a valid schema causes SQLite recovery to fail. `store::open_with_recovery` detects corrupt databases, moves them to `<path>.corrupt`, and initializes fresh, clean stores.
- **Forward-compatible store readers:** Readers for JSON configuration stores (`plugins.json`, etc.) must ignore unknown sibling keys rather than failing as corrupt. Closed validation rules belong on manifest checkers and writers, not on store deserializers.
- **Owner-only file permissions:** Stores containing terminal scrollback, settings, or encryption secrets must be created and repaired to 0700 for directories and 0600 for files using `gpty_core::owner_only`.

Traps and invariants across PTY emulation, ANSI parsing, VTE escape processing, grid layout, and child process lifecycles.

## PTY Spawning & Process Lifecycles

- **`portable_pty` `$HOME` fallback behavior:** `CommandBuilder::as_command()` resolves directory paths with `cwd.filter(is_dir).unwrap_or(home)`. If `$HOME` points to a deleted or non-existent path, spawns fail with `No such file or directory (os error 2)` naming the *binary* (e.g. `/bin/bash`) even when the binary exists and is executable.
- **Teardown via `Drop`:** Every Rust structure wrapping a child process (`portable_pty::Child`) or dedicated reader thread must implement `Drop` to call `.kill()` and abort reader tasks. Without explicit teardown, closing panes in Godot leaves orphaned shell processes and background threads.
- **PTY child working directory:** A child process spawned from the GDExtension without an explicit `cwd` inherits the Godot project directory, not the user's terminal launch directory. Always resolve and supply the active workspace directory explicitly.
- **Exit detection on Windows (ConPTY):** ConPTY keeps the PTY pipe open after the child process exits. Relying solely on pipe EOF causes panes to report `running: true` indefinitely. Exit detection requires polling `try_wait` alongside pipe reads.
- **Non-blocking input writes:** PTY input is backpressured through bounded channels (`STDIN_QUEUE_CAP` to `WRITER_QUEUE_CHUNKS`). Writing to the PTY must be non-blocking; blocking in the write path leaves raw-mode children unkillable when they cease reading stdin.
- **A pty write's success is not delivery:** a raw-mode Linux master write absorbs megabytes into the tty flip buffers before it blocks, and the line discipline discards what a non-reading child never consumes while `write` still returns the full count. So a test cannot infer "the input queue filled" from counted `send_text` successes - an 18 MiB burst was swallowed with no error and only `READY` on the grid, while a fresh probe blocked after ~11 KiB; saturation depends on the flip-buffer state earlier output left behind (measured 2026-11-21). Test a queue cap at its ingress instead: send the burst without yielding, so nothing drains and the cap is what refuses.

## Grid Synchronization, Rendering & Sizing

- **SGR 7 inverse video color swap:** ANSI SGR 7 swaps both foreground and background colors. Do the swap once at the grid presentation boundary (`CellInfo::paint_colors`). Bash readline wraps bracketed paste echos in SGR 7; swapping only text color paints glyphs with their own background, rendering them invisible.
- **Selection lives in grid space:** Text selection coordinates must be maintained in grid buffer lines (`alacritty_terminal::Term::selection`), not in viewport screen coordinates. Output scrolling and window resizing rotate the grid; viewport-based selections desynchronize immediately.
- **Transient pane sizes collapse grids:** During layout churn (splits, spawns), panels briefly report tiny pixel sizes (~38×40 px, or 4×2 cells). If passed to `resize_grid()`, the grid collapses and rewraps destructively. Skip resizing when pixel dimensions fall below the minimum grid threshold (`TerminalPane._grid_for_size`).
- **Resize rate-limiting & debouncing:** Firing SIGWINCH on every frame during window drag overwhelms child processes. Debounce `_on_resize` calls in GDScript and avoid redundant SIGWINCH signals if calculated rows and columns have not changed.
- **Raw-byte buffering for grid replay:** Never buffer parsed plain text for terminal replay. The ANSI state machine requires raw byte streams with escape sequences preserved.

## Terminal Protocols & Key Handling

- **Terminal query replies (`Event::PtyWrite`):** `alacritty_terminal` emits `Event::PtyWrite` in response to terminal status queries (such as DSR cursor position requests `ESC[6n`). gPTY must forward these reply bytes back to the child PTY. Dropping them breaks interactive TUIs (e.g., OMP, lazydocker) after window resizes.
- **Alt key combos:** For Alt+letter combinations, the keymap expects the frontend layer to prepend `\x1b` (ESC) in the `_key_to_text` fallback path.
- **Mouse mode reporting:** Mouse reporting mode bits (`get_mouse_mode`) are the source of truth for whether the child owns the pointer. The frontend encodes SGR (DECSET 1006) or legacy X10 mouse packets accordingly. Shift-clicking bypasses mouse reporting to allow host text selection.
- **Ctrl+V passthrough:** `Ctrl+V` must reach the child shell as literal `^V` (for readline quoted-insert and vim visual-block). Terminal paste must always be bound to `Ctrl+Shift+V`.

## By defect class

### one-fact-two-copies

- `tokio::pin!` + `reset()` for capture timeouts: Use `tokio::pin!(sleep)` and `sleep.as_mut().reset(deadline)` to re-arm a timeout without recreating it each iteration. One `select!` branch, no code duplication.

- SGR 7 swaps BOTH cell colors, not just the glyph: an inverse cell's text is painted from `bg` and its background from `fg`. Do the swap once, at the presentation boundary - `CellInfo::paint_colors` in `gpty-core` is what `get_grid_updates_packed` packs, so the cache a pane draws from is **paint-ready** and `_draw_cells` must never re-derive it.
