Swapping only the text color paints the glyph in its own background, and this is the common case, not an exotic one: bash's readline wraps the echo of every bracketed paste in `ESC[7m`/`ESC[27m` (measured under a real PTY), so pasted text read as blank cells with the cursor advancing, until the next arrow key made readline repaint the line unhighlighted. `godot/tests/integration/test_inverse_paint.gd` pins the cache's paint-ready colors (and fails on the raw-color packer); `inverse_cells_expose_swapped_paint_colors` pins the rule itself.

- Pressed-state text color: a pressed (toggle-mode) Button resolves text from `font_pressed_color`, which falls back to the theme default and silently ignores `font_color` - the active-row accent rendered black until all three states were overridden. The fix is a colour role, not an override: `_apply_row_accent` names `UiTheme.ACCENT_BUTTON`, whose type variation sets `font_color`/`font_hover_color`/`font_pressed_color`/`font_focus_color` in the theme (an override would pin the palette the row was built under, and a new pressed role needs all four colours or the accent vanishes exactly when the row is active).

- A `ScrollBar`'s thickness is not a property: Godot 4.7.2 derives it from the track stylebox's content margins plus the type's padding constants (`VScrollBar.padding_left`/`padding_right`, `HScrollBar.padding_top`/`padding_bottom`), while the grabber stylebox's margins only set the thumb's minimum length (`ScrollBar::get_minimum_size`). An empty track (`StyleBoxEmpty`) is therefore a 0 px bar - nothing drawn, nothing draggable, and no column reserved, because `ScrollContainer` subtracts the bar's minimum from its content. The geometry is theme-owned (`UiTokens.SCROLLBAR_THICKNESS`/`SCROLLBAR_INSET`/`SCROLLBAR_MIN_THUMB` consumed by `UiTheme.build`, pinned by `test_ui_theme.gd`); a widget-level override would be a second source of truth. A stylebox's content margins ARE its minimum size, so an all-zero box collapses any control that sizes from it.

- The layout grid has exactly **one** definition: `PaneTypes.GRID`/`PaneTypes.MIN_TILE`, read by the drag math, `PaneTypes.sanitize_tile`'s default, and `workspace.gd._apply_layout`. A second copy drifted once (the layout divided by 12 while the tiles were in 60), which clamped every restored pane to a sliver and drew it several times the grid - panes outside the visible area, from a one-line constant change. Never re-declare it locally; the tiles on a divider are the ones whose saved span *ends* on the line and the ones whose span *starts* on it (`TileDrag._tiles_on_divider`), never a neighbour matched by equal extents - a full-height pane flanked by two stacked ones has no equal-extent neighbour at all.

- An embedded `Window`'s frame and title band are painted from **Godot's own default theme**, not
  from a `Theme` set on a Control ancestor: `Window/embedded_border` (and
  `embedded_unfocused_border`) had no effect on 4.7.2 - a magenta `StyleBoxFlat` produced no
  pixels, and merely defining the item took the band from the default grey to unpainted, leaving
  the pane behind showing through. `StyleBox.expand_margin_top` on `AcceptDialog/panel` cannot
  cover it either, because the window's canvas clips drawing to the window rect. `AppDialog`
  therefore builds modals `borderless` with its own header. Two more things that follow from the
  same layout rule: an `AcceptDialog` lays out **every** direct child Control over the same content
  rect (two children overlap, so one `VBoxContainer` is the only workable structure), and its
  internal `dialog_text` label keeps rendering whatever you add until it is hidden - `AppDialog`
  hides it and keeps `dialog_text` as the string so tests and `body_of` agree.

- A renamed or unmarshaled `#[func]` breaks GDScript at runtime, not at parse time: the call is syntactically valid and fails only in the pane that exercises it. `scripts/check-ffi-surface` (run by `ci-check`) cross-checks every call on a GDExtension handle against the exported surface - name and arity. A `#[func]` is attributed to the class its enclosing `#[godot_api] impl` block names (primary or `#[godot_api(secondary)]`, which is how one class is implemented across files), and a `#[func]` outside such a block is reported - the old rule took the first `struct` in the file, so a class split across files would have quietly lost every moved method from the checked surface. It is fail-closed: a Godot-inherited member it does not know about (`has_method` is allowlisted) is reported, so add it to `INHERITED_MEMBERS` deliberately rather than widening the check. The same walk reads the crate's own prose - `crates/gpty-gdext/README.md` and its `///` comments - where a backticked `name(...)` must be an export, a plain `fn` in the crate, or a reasoned `DOC_ALLOWED_NAMES` entry: the reference is what a caller reads before writing the first call, and a name that exists nowhere (three prose mentions of `get_grid_rows()`, a method no version of the class ever had) costs the same round trip as a renamed export. One parsing limit: the arity splitter does not know string literals, so a `#[func]` call whose string argument contains a comma (`set_palette(",".join(...))`) reads as two arguments and fails the gate on a correct call - assign the string to a local first (the v0.9.4 roadmap row owns the fix).

- A file reader's closed key set is a second copy of rules its consumers already own, and it fails as *corruption*: `plugins.json`'s reader refused an unknown key at every level, so a store written by a newer release made `gpty plugin list|enable|disable|uninstall` report an intact file as corrupt (`unknown key 'concepts'` from a v0.7-era writer on a v0.5.5 CLI, then `grid_unit` in v0.8.4 - the same class twice). The reader's rule is now one policy in `crates/gpty-plugin/src/store.rs`: an unknown sibling key is ignored at every level because nothing reads it (a tile goes through `PaneTypes.sanitize_settings`, a concept through `gpty_core::concept::concepts_from_json`, which ignores what it does not know), while a required field, a type, a shape, a cap and the id/revision formats are refused - a rename still fails through its required-field check. A record that genuinely does not match is `StoreError::mismatched`, which names the release skew (`run the CLI and the GUI from the same release`) instead of the file, and the writer keeps the closed vocabulary it emits (`validate_concepts` holds the manifest's `CONCEPT_KEYS`). Before closing a reader's key set, ask what a *newer* writer of the same file does to it; refusal is only right for the fields the reader depends on.

### missed-call-site

- A child spawned from the GDExtension without an explicit cwd inherits the GUI's working directory, and that is the Godot *project* directory (`godot --path <dir>` chdirs there), not where the user launched the app: measured 2026-11-06 while recording a demo - `gpty new-pane -t cli_view -c git --arg log` listed gPTY's own history while the same `git log` in a terminal pane listed the sandbox repo's four commits, because `CliProcess::spawn` (`crates/gpty-core/src/cli.rs`) takes no cwd while terminals go through `PtyHandle::spawn_with_cwd` (`pty.rs:409`) with the workspace directory. A new spawn path passes the workspace directory (the v0.8 row *A pane can choose its own directory, with the workspace directory as the fallback* owns the resolution) instead of relying on inheritance; `scripts/record-demo` compensates with `git -C "$HOME"` until that lands.

- Reparenting a pane fires a teardown notification: `Node.reparent()` (or `add_child` onto another parent) removes and re-adds the node, so `_exit_tree` runs. `cli_view`, `media` and `inspector` stop their backend there (`_cli.stop`, `_stop_backend`, `_close_session`), so a cross-workspace move must set `PaneBody.backend_preserved` around the reparent and those three hooks check it; `TerminalPane`'s hook only flushes history and needs no guard. A pane moved this way keeps its body and its GDExtension object (the Rust side tears down in `Drop`, not on tree exit), so the PTY session id and scrollback survive - `Workspace._move_panes_into` owns the transaction.

- Typed arrays break Rust FFI: gdext `Array<Variant>` parameters reject GDScript's `Array[Dictionary]` at runtime ("expected array of type Untyped, got Builtin(DICTIONARY)"). Always pass untyped `Array` across the FFI boundary. Prefer `func f(arr: Array)` over `func f(arr: Array[Dictionary])` when the array originates from or goes to Rust.

- Godot typed Arrays: `Array[T]` won't accept plain `Array`. If you type a parameter, check all call sites use matching types (`var x: Array[Control] = []`).

- GDScript `:=` cannot infer through an untyped handle: `var x := ws._palette._field` is a parse error ("Cannot infer the type of \"x\" variable because the value doesn't have a set type"), because a property read on an untyped (`Variant`) base yields `Variant` - and the suite reports it as a `Parse Error` that aborts the whole GUT run, not as a failing test. The integration tests reach through untyped `Workspace` handles all the time, so annotate the target (`var x: LineEdit = ws._palette._field`) rather than falling back to `=`; the error names the variable, not the handle.

- Alt key handling: For Alt+letter combos, the Rust keymap returns `None`, expecting the GDScript layer to prepend `\x1b` (ESC). `_handle_keyboard` does this in the `_key_to_text` fallback path.

- Resize cascades from layout changes: When panes are added/removed, remaining terminals receive multiple `NOTIFICATION_RESIZED` events in rapid succession. Even when calculated rows×cols are identical, each `resize_grid()` call triggers a full grid re-wrap and sync, producing a visible "scrolling through history" animation. Fix: `TermGrid::resize()` must return early if dimensions are unchanged. Also apply a pixel-level check in the GDScript debounce to avoid redundant calls.

- Transient pane sizes collapse the grid: during split/spawn layout churn, panes transiently report ~38×40 px (4×2 cells). Applying that rewraps the grid to 2×4 - the terminal looks dead. `terminal_pane.gd` must skip resize when the size cannot hold the minimum grid (`TerminalPane._grid_for_size` returns `Vector2i.ZERO`: fewer than 8 cols or 3 rows) at BOTH event and apply time, and must recompute dims from the CURRENT size when the debounce fires. `resize_grid` (gdext) must also no-op when dims are unchanged (no redundant SIGWINCH). The same helper is the one birth-size threshold: a pane's child is spawned on the first laid-out size (never on the container's minimum), `_grid_for_size` is shared by that spawn and the debounce, a tile the grid has never positioned (`PaneBody.mark_tile_laid_out`, driven by `Workspace._apply_layout`) spawns nothing, and a tile too small to hold the minimum grid still gets a shell at the pane's configured `rows`/`cols` - which is all those fields mean now: `apply_settings` never resizes a live grid.

- Textless Buttons collapse: Godot does not derive a Button's minimum size from child Controls. A Button that carries an icon+text HBox instead of its own `text` needs an explicit `custom_minimum_size.y` (see `_make_sidebar_button`'s icon+text branch) or it squashes to nothing and overlaps the next VBox row.

- Pane targeting over IPC is resolved by `Workspace._resolve_pane_target` only: an `attachment_id` is matched across every workspace first (ids are unique), a label resolves only when exactly one pane carries it, and a label two workspaces share is refused with the candidates named. Never reintroduce active-workspace-first label lookup - it delivered an agent's command to another workspace's pane with no error.

- `gpty --json` prints the JSON-RPC envelope on stdout **and** exits 1 when the response carries an error: `format_response`/`check_error` print first, then fail, so stdout stays parseable and the exit status is the success signal a script branches on (`error.code` carries the kind; a verb with a string sub-kind adds `error.data.code`). The custom-output commands (`list-panes`, `profile list`, the all-panes `pane-status`) call `check_error` after their own output rather than re-deciding the rule. The MCP server is separate: it builds its own in-band JSON-RPC errors.

- CLI auto-spawn policy: only `new-pane` and `profile load` may start a GUI, and `--no-daemon` refuses even those (`main.rs::may_autospawn`, exhaustive so a new subcommand must choose a side). Every other command reaches the GUI through its own call and, when nothing is listening, prints `no gpty GUI is running (start one with \`gpty daemon start\`)` and exits 1 - the classification is `daemon::is_not_running` over `ClientError::Connection(NotFound | ConnectionRefused)` in the error chain, so a refused insecure path keeps its own message. `daemon start` is the explicit spawner (it refuses under `--no-daemon`), `daemon stop` with nothing running is an idempotent no-op, and `daemon status` can never create what it checks. The MCP server never auto-spawns - its `daemon-start` tool is the bootstrap, and a tool call that finds no GUI answers with the same hint plus "call the daemon-start tool first". A GUI that cannot start reports its own stderr (captured to a private temp file, removed once it answers) instead of waiting out the timeout with the reason discarded; a spawn happens only when the probe says the endpoint is genuinely empty (a listener that does not answer is waited out, never duplicated).

- A control that animates on its **own** clock is not frozen by stopping its pane: the agent badge (`ui/agent_badge.gd`) advances its phase in its own `_process`, so `_apply_agent_states` re-applies the state (which pins the phase to 0) *and* calls `badge.set_process(false)` - stopping the pane alone left two runs of the same state differing, which `scripts/ui-capture-check` reports as a pixel mismatch. A state that gains a self-animating control needs both lines, or its image stops repeating. `ShortcutGuide` is the other instance: `_pin_empty_guide` calls its `pin_animation()`, which resets phase/step and stops its own `_process`.

- A `TabContainer` takes the font size of the `TabBar` it creates from the **container's** theme item, not from `TabBar`'s: the engine builds the internal bar with a `font_size` override copied from `TabContainer`, so `set_font_size(..., "TabBar", n)` alone leaves the live bar at the theme's `default_font_size` (measured on 4.7.2: 13 px in the theme, 12 px on screen). Set both. And a tab hidden by an overflow answers `get_tab_rect(i)` with a zero-based rect (measured: tab 6 read 0..56 on a bar whose tabs ended at 464), so a "the tabs fit" guard has to read the rects as one contiguous row - `position.x` equals the running end - and sum their widths; a per-tab `end.x <= bar.size.x` check passes while the last tab sits behind the overflow dropdown.

### silent-failure

- A sandboxed GUI inherits the operator's own control credential, and its panes do not: launching `scripts/record-demo` from an agent pane carried `GPTY_SECRET` into the app, so it demanded the secret while every `gpty` call typed *inside* the clip (a pane's shell has it stripped) was refused `GUI requires GPTY_SECRET authentication` - and the run still encoded a clip, exited 0 and looked finished. A scripted launch must clear it (`scripts/ui-sandbox` does; `record-demo` now `unset`s it), and a capture's exit status is not evidence that its pane commands ran - read a frame before trusting the asset (measured 2026-11-16).

- Locking: `std::sync::Mutex` throughout; a poisoned lock means *skip this work and keep the app running*, so report it through `gpty_core::lock::lock_or_warn(mutex, "what")` rather than a bare `if let Ok(..) = m.lock()` - the first occurrence of each lock then shows up in the log (a silently frozen pane used to be indistinguishable from an idle one). Do NOT add `parking_lot` (the dead `gpty-ipc` dependency was removed in v0.5.4): with no poisoning at all, "a thread died holding this lock" becomes invisible instead of reported. `gpty-ai` is the exception - it does not depend on `gpty-core` and turns poisoning into a `Result` error at its own boundary.

- Core diagnostics do reach the GUI now: `diagnostics.rs` installs a `log` bridge at `InitStage::Core` that forwards `warn`+ records whose target starts with `gpty` to `godot_warn!`/`godot_error!` (dependency targets stay out, and `info`/`debug` are dropped - a diagnostic meant to be seen must be `warn` or above). Do not call `godot_warn!` from `gpty-core`/`gpty-ai`: those crates must not depend on gdext, so their message goes through `log` and the bridge carries it. 

- PTY spawns inherit portable-pty's `$HOME` fallback: `CommandBuilder::as_command()` resolves the child's directory with `self.cwd.filter(is_dir).unwrap_or(home)` and then applies it through `current_dir`, so a `$HOME` that names no directory turns *every* spawn into `No such file or directory (os error 2)` **with the program's name in the message** - `/bin/bash` looked missing while it ran fine (measured 2026-11-04: a test environment carried a deleted `HOME`, and the whole GDScript suite reported 13 spawn failures for a shell that existed). Two consequences worth remembering: an absent cwd does not mean "inherit gpty's own", it means `$HOME`; and `get_home_dir` falls back to `getpwuid` only when `$HOME` is unset, never when it is set and missing. Judge a spawn ENOENT by the *directory*, not the program - `env -i HOME=<a real directory> …` reproduces or clears it in one run. The product fix is queued as the first v0.9.1 row.

- A Godot `String` cannot hold U+0000: a `\u0000` escape in source and `String.chr(0)` both read back as U+FFFD, with `Unicode parsing error ... Unexpected NUL character` on stderr (measured on 4.7.2) - six times for `vault_graph_model.gd`, which used a NUL separator for composite edge keys and emitted it on every script load. Never use NUL as a key separator or value sentinel: `String.contains`/`find` of one can never succeed, and a key built with one is silently a U+FFFD key that can collide with a path containing that glyph; the graph model keys pairs with a nested `{a: {b: pair}}` map instead. A sanitizer that drops control characters therefore never *sees* a NUL, and a test that puts one in a literal is testing the engine, not the sanitizer - build the case from BEL (`\u0007`), TAB, LF, CR and DEL, which do survive.

- `extends Node` won't render `Control` children: Only `Control` nodes can render child `Control`s (Labels, Buttons, etc.). If you add a Label to a plain `Node`, it's invisible. Use `extends Control` for UI containers and set `z_index` for layering.

- `continue` in `for` does not skip trailing code: A `continue` inside a `for` loop only skips the current iteration - code BELOW the loop still executes. Use `break` + a boolean flag to conditionally skip post-loop grid feeding.

- Concept matching on PTY output: `ConceptMatcher::match_line` tests every line against the enabled concepts (first match wins) on both the PTY-output path and the typed-input path; `concept::match_line` is its ungated decision loop (same verdict, no prefilter) and stays the function the precedence/condition tests exercise. The match's return value MUST be used to `session.begin(name, target, deadline)` - ignoring it (`let _ = match_line(...)`) silently disables capture, which looks exactly like "concepts do nothing".

- Tab completion triggers concept matches: Bash reprints the prompt and partial command when showing autocomplete candidates. This reprinted line has no trailing `\n`, so `LineParser` never emits it. Tab completion never triggers concept matching.

- Raw-byte buffering for grid replay: Never buffer parsed lines for later grid replay - the alacritty_terminal ANSI state machine needs raw bytes with escape sequences intact. Buffer `Vec<Vec<u8>>` (chunks), replay with `feed_grid(board, chunk)`.

- Emulator PTY replies: alacritty_terminal emits `Event::PtyWrite` for terminal queries (DSR cursor-position `ESC[6n` → `ESC[row;colR`, mode reports). gPTY's event proxy MUST queue these and the engine MUST write them to the child PTY (`TermGrid::drain_replies()` drained each loop iteration). Dropping them breaks TUIs that query the cursor after SIGWINCH - the OMP TUI re-anchors its transcript and appears to "scroll through history" on every resize, while vim/btop (which never query) are unaffected. Never drop non-`Title` events.

- Consume the event socket's answer: the extension's `sendOne` opens one connection per event, writes, half-closes - and must read the reply. A `net.Socket` reaches `end`/`close` only once its readable side is consumed; left paused it never closed, so every event in the forwarder's pump waited out `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS` (measured 2026-11-14 against the running server: 4.0 events/s on Node 26.13.1 and Bun 1.4.4, instead of ~4 800 and 5 769 with `socket.resume()`). Reasoning deltas flush every 16 ms, so a thinking turn outran the channel, the 128-slot outbox dropped its oldest chunks, and the Reasoning pane and the agent badge ran seconds behind the session while `omp.agent.settled` sat at the back of the backlog. The fix discards the bytes (the channel stays fire-and-forget); the regression test is a socket double that closes only after its bytes are read, and any new one-shot writer on `gpty-events.sock` has the same rule.

- `stream=thinking` observers are not job owners: after migration they become Reasoning panes and must keep `can_receive_content() == false`. Acknowledging a capture without starting analysis discards terminal output.

- **A `gpty` on PATH is a stable link, never a download directory.** A symlink into an extracted release dir breaks silently when that dir is cleaned up: `ls ~/.local/bin/gpty` shows the link, `execvp` finds nothing, and an MCP client reports `Executable not found in $PATH: "gpty"` - the message a *missing* binary prints, which sends the reader to PATH order instead of to the link. `scripts/install-cli` owns the layout that avoids it (`~/.local/opt/gpty/<version>`, `current` pointing at one of them, `~/.local/bin/gpty` and `gpty-gui` linked through `current`) and `--check` prints every `gpty` on PATH in the order `execvp` walks it.

- gdext `#[func]` parameter types: ONLY `GString`, `bool`, and `i64` are reliably marshaled as input parameters. `Array<Variant>`, `Dictionary`, and bare `Variant` all silently fail - the GDScript call succeeds but the Rust body never executes. Workaround: serialize complex data to JSON in GDScript (`JSON.stringify()`), pass as `GString`, deserialize in Rust with `serde_json::from_str`.

- GDScript typed parameters are a batch-wide failure at the IPC edge: `sanitize_tags(raw: Array)` raised a call error when a caller sent `"tags": "a,b"`, and one raise inside a handler arm aborts the drain loop (`WorkspaceIpcHandlers.dispatch_request`, called from `_poll_ipc_requests`) - every request already drained is then unanswered and each caller waits out its timeout (no try/catch to contain it). A helper that takes a value *from a request* stays untyped and degrades to an empty result (`sanitize_tags` now mirrors `sanitize_shell_args`); the JSON-type refusal belongs at the edge, where it costs one `-32602`. Keep the typing for internal callers, where the value is already known.

- A per-request read bound must not wrap the IPC server's reader in a second `BufReader`: `handle_frame` serves every newline-framed request on a connection until EOF, and the extra buffer swallows the start of the next pipelined frame when it is dropped. Bound the read with `take` on the existing `BufReader` instead; an over-bound frame answers `-32600` and closes the connection because the stream is no longer frame-aligned, while a parse error answers `-32700` and the batch continues.

- A bounded external tool is not a fallback: `timeout 20 ffmpeg …` written as a bare command under `set -e` aborts the script on the timeout's status 124, so the guard meant to prevent a hang produces a silent exit with empty stderr instead of handing over to the next backend (measured 2026-11-06 in `scripts/screenshot-gpty`: ffmpeg's `x11grab -window_id` attached to nothing on this XWayland session and printed nothing, while ImageMagick's `import` captured the same window immediately). Put the call where a failure is a value - inside an `if`, or with `|| true` - delete the stale partial output, and try the next backend; `SCREENSHOT_CAPTURE=ffmpeg|import` pins one when you know which can grab.

### unbounded

- `tokio::select!` None branches: When a channel returns `None` (closed), `select!` disables that branch but keeps polling others instantly - causing 100% CPU. Bind to a variable first (`msg = rx.recv()`), then `let Ok(v) = msg else { break; }`.

- PTY output is backpressured, never dropped: `pty_rx` is `mpsc::channel(pty::OUTPUT_QUEUE_CHUNKS)` (256 chunks ≈ 1 MiB per pane) and the reader thread blocks in `blocking_send` when it fills, so a flooding child (`yes`, `cat /dev/urandom`) waits on the kernel PTY buffer instead of growing the process - with an unbounded queue it measured +70 MiB/s in the GUI and 2.2 GiB in 20 s in a bare harness. Do NOT make the channel unbounded again, and never "unstick" a full queue with `try_send`/drop: these bytes carry ANSI state (SGR, cursor moves, `ESC[` sequences), so a dropped chunk desynchronises the grid. The reader thread stops only when the pane is gone (receiver dropped) or the child exits.

- Rendering Performance: GDScript `_draw` is slow when calling `draw_rect`/`draw_string` character-by-character. Avoid generating heavy data structures (like `Dictionary`) per-cell across the FFI boundary. Prefer packing data into flat arrays (`PackedByteArray`, `PackedInt32Array`) in Rust, and batch rendering into glyph runs - consecutive same-attribute cells merged into one draw call; per-line batching is the floor, not the ceiling. Do NOT re-propose a custom GPU texture pipeline (fontdue glyph atlas / instanced quads) without new evidence: Godot already GPU-composites canvas items, the bottleneck is CPU-side command generation, and fontdue would duplicate Godot's existing glyph atlasing. The instanced-quad renderer is evidence-gated in ROADMAP Future - revisit only if render batching plus flood rate-limiting still shows frame-time pain.

- Godot's 2D canvas does not occlusion-cull: a shader on a full-window rect pays its fragment cost for every pixel even where opaque panes cover it, so a background effect's price follows the rect it draws, not the area the user can see. Scope it by rect (its own `SubViewport`, half resolution, its own frame rate) and never assume the covered area is free.

- A 3D `SubViewport` shown inside a pane has three traps the vault map paid for: its `size` is still `(0, 0)` on the frame the first graph is shown, so a units-per-pixel derived from it (with a 1 px fallback) makes world-space link quads thousands of units wide and covers the pane - use the Control's own height as the second source and rebuild after the deferred fit. An `ImmediateMesh` surface is not committed until `surface_end()`; without it every test that reads the recorded vertices passes while nothing draws. And a 3D `Environment` background/fog is a different colour path from the 2D palette: `fog_light_energy < 1` dims the whole ground, and a dark surface colour renders near-black - paint the palette background in the 2D Control and give the SubViewport a transparent background (`BG_CLEAR_COLOR` + `transparent_bg`), so both themes match the pane exactly. `VaultGraph3D` is the reference.

- The Markdown renderer's **form** is a rule, not a style: it never emits `[ul]`/`[ol]`, because Godot lays a list out superlinearly in its item count and a preview pays that on every update - measured on the Godot 4.7.2 binary: 38915 ms to shape 1.7 MiB of two-item lists (146705 ms for a real 1 MiB note) against 819 ms for that same rendered text with the tags stripped, and 0.5–1.3 s for every other construct (headings, quotes, inline code, links, tables). Each item is therefore a `• `/`N. ` line inside one `[indent]` per list (a nested list opens its own), which renders identically (screenshot-checked side by side) and keeps the layout linear; the numbering is the renderer's own, which is also how a list starting at 3 renders `3.`. Reintroducing a list tag is a freeze measured in minutes, not a fidelity tweak. Cost model, measured with `godot/tests/bench/markdown_bench.gd` (and `cargo test -p gpty-gdext --lib probe_render_cost` for the Rust half alone) in release: a preview update is render 48 / 50 / 101 ms plus shape 261 / 486 / 973 ms for 256 KiB / 512 KiB / 1 MiB - the shape pass is the dominant term, so nothing may make it superlinear again.

- A live preview renders on **settle**, never on the streaming throttle: `MarkdownView.set_markdown_settled` restarts its timer on every call (`settle_delay`, 0.4 s), so a typing run queues no render at all and one lands when the user stops - `set_markdown`'s non-restarting throttle stays for streams (Reasoning, Inspector) and `render_now` for explicit acts (opening a note, a mode switch, a save). The wiki pane's `_on_editor_changed` must call the settle form; the throttle there was the original item's bug (a 75 ms cadence re-rendering and re-shaping a large note under the typist's fingers).

- A Phosphor glyph `Label` costs ~3.5 ms to enter the tree, which makes free-and-recreate row UIs far more expensive than their control count suggests: measured on 4.7.2 X11 (2026-11-09), `add_child` of a `Label` whose text is a PUA codepoint with the bundled Phosphor font override is 3.3-3.5 ms, the same Label with ASCII text is 0.09 ms, the same glyph left in `Button.text` (the pre-v0.8.0 icon shape) is 3.4 ms, the glyph with no font override (system fallback search) is 6.6-8.0 ms, and re-assigning `Label.text` on an attached Label is 0.00 ms - the cost is per element and is not cached across Labels. So a row carrying two icon buttons costs 7 ms to rebuild, and `Workspace._switch_workspace` spends 62 of its 74 ms freeing and recreating the sidebar's three lists (v0.8.3 row *The sidebar rebuilds every list on a workspace switch, 62 of 74 ms*). Update a row's label and glyphs in place; create rows only when the set of rows changes. A capture harness cannot see this - it is synchronous GDScript, not a draw - and neither can headless.

- PTY input is backpressured in two bounded stages, never one: the engine's `STDIN_QUEUE_CAP` (256 messages) feeds the writer thread's `WRITER_QUEUE_CHUNKS` (16 chunks). Do NOT make either unbounded, and do NOT block in `PtyHandle::send`: a full writer queue answers `WouldBlock` and the task retries after a 1 ms async sleep, so a pane close can still abort the task and drop the handle that kills the child. Blocking a tokio worker in the send leaves a raw-mode child that stopped reading unkillable (measured 2026-11-15: the test hung past 60 s until the send became non-blocking). Canonical-mode PTYs discard the excess instead of blocking, so the test child must run `stty raw` to reproduce the queue at all.

### stale-state

- A `SubViewport` visibility pause must be cleared on the visible branch, not merely re-requested: `VaultGraph3D._pause_for_hidden()` sets `_hidden_paused` and `UPDATE_DISABLED`; when a settled map was shown again, `_request_render()` still saw the flag and kept the viewport disabled, and `_resume_from_hidden()` (the only clearer) was reached only from a physics frame that is off while settled. The `SubViewportContainer` kept the pre-switch map as a static background (reported 2026-11-18 after a workspace switch; the settled visible branch now calls `_resume_from_hidden()`). Every pause flag needs its visible branch to clear it; a settled viewport needs `UPDATE_ONCE`. Regression: `test_a_settled_view_repaints_after_hiding` (`godot/tests/integration/test_vault_graph_3d.gd`). Audited 2026-11-18: `vault_graph_3d.gd` is the only app-owned `SubViewport` (`rg -n "SubViewport|render_target_update_mode|UPDATE_DISABLED" godot/scenes --glob '!addons/**'` also matches only a comment in `vault_graph_canvas.gd`); `docs_viewer.gd`, `settings_panel.gd`, `shortcut_guide.gd` and `vault_graph_view.gd` have `NOTIFICATION_VISIBILITY_CHANGED` handlers but own no render target, and `agent_badge.gd` only toggles `set_process`. Any future app `SubViewport` gets the same hide→show test.

- GDExtension rebuilds: After changing `#[func]` signatures or adding methods, `cargo build -p gpty-gdext` and fully restart Godot. Keep `godot/bin/libgpty_gdext.linux.x86_64.so` as a symlink to `../../target/debug/libgpty_gdext.so` so the editor sees Cargo output. A release build of the editor (e.g. 4.7.2 stable) does not accept `linux.debug.*` feature keys. `./scripts/build` overwrites the symlink with a release copy.

- GDScript default params: Evaluated at definition time, not call time. `func f(x := some_var)` captures the value of `some_var` when the script loads. Use `func f(x := -1)` and check `if x < 0: x = some_var` inside the body for runtime-evaluated defaults.

- `std::sync::Once` poisoning: if the closure passed to `Once::call_once` panics, the `Once` is permanently poisoned - all subsequent calls panic too. For lazy init that spawns fallible work, use `AtomicBool::swap(true, Relaxed)` or `Mutex<Option<...>>` instead.

- Pane labels: `_next_label` takes `max(existing numeric suffix) + 1` - closing the newest pane reuses its number, middle gaps are never filled (T1,T3 → next is T4). Do not reintroduce monotonic counters.

- Terminal selection lives in the **grid**, not in viewport rows: `GptyTerminal.selection_start/extend/clear` drive `alacritty_terminal::Term::selection`, which alacritty rotates whenever output scrolls the screen (and on resize). A screen-space selection (the pane's old `_sel_start/_sel_end`) stayed on whatever text scrolled under it; `get_selection_text` reads grid rows, so a selection scrolled out of view still copies in full. Do not re-derive the anchor from `display_offset` arithmetic in GDScript - grid line indices shift with every scroll, so only the term's own selection keeps its text; `get_selection_cells` is just the drawing projection for the current offset.

- Godot's AccessKit adapter (4.7.2) has three traps that decide whether published content reaches AT-SPI. An element's name is a **snapshot taken when it was created** (measured 2026-11-05), so dynamic content is a replacement node per change (`A11y.publish`, one at a time), never an edit, and the name must be set before `add_child`. A `Label`'s AT-SPI name is its **display text**, not `accessibility_name` (measured 2026-11-13: the terminal's published slot showed an empty name with the content in `accessibility_name`, and the same string in `Label.text` showed up as the name), so the content node is `A11yContent`: a `Control` whose own `NOTIFICATION_ACCESSIBILITY_UPDATE` writes the role `A11y.set_text` queues. Never a `Label` (it would shape the whole screen: 992 ms for 221x78, measured 2026-11-11) and never a bare `Control` (it keeps the container role, which AccessKit drops from the tree). The role/value writes are legal only inside that notification; `update_set_role` reaches AT-SPI while `update_set_value` does not (`Text.GetText` answers `""` for a screen the app pushed, measured 2026-11-13). A `PaneBody`'s own children were not observed in the tree on 4.7.2, which is why the publish host is the tile's title bar.

- Font-size changes reach a pane through `PaneBody`'s `font_size` setter, which calls `_recompute_cell_metrics()` for **every** type; a repeated value is a no-op, because the settings panel re-sends the whole dict on each keystroke. A view pane's override re-applies its own theme font-size overrides (and invalidates any height it cached at the old font) and must tolerate null widgets: a spawn applies the saved settings before `_ready` runs. `PaneBody.empty_state_font(title, hint, font_px)` keeps an empty state's two lines on that same size (the title one step above the body text). The terminal's override guards on `_font`, which `_ready` loads.

- A **width floor inside a scroll child freezes the layout it was measured at**. `custom_minimum_size.x` on a `RichTextLabel` in a `FoldableContainer` inside a horizontal-scroll-disabled `ScrollContainer` propagates upward - that ScrollContainer's own minimum width is its child's minimum - and an anchored parent clamps to its combined minimum, so a shrinking pane keeps the old width and autowrap never re-runs. The container owns width; sync only the height from `get_content_height()` and re-run it from the view's `resized` signal. Measured on 4.7.2: a 420 -> 220 px Reasoning pane stayed 400 px wide until `_sync_fold_height` stopped writing `custom_minimum_size.x` (`godot/scenes/panes/reasoning_pane.gd`).

- A palette read in an initialiser is evaluated **once**: an `@export var c: Color = UiPalette.active().X` compiles and freezes whichever mode was active at construction, so a later switch never reaches that widget (the `const` form does not compile, which is how a missed site announces itself). Read at draw time, or name a `Theme` type variation; the census that keeps this true is `scripts/check-theme-tokens` (run by `ci-check`), which fails an `add_theme_color_override` and a class-body `UiPalette.active()` read.

- A theme set on an ancestor resolves for a child only after the child is in the tree and a frame has run: a `-s` probe that sets `host.theme = UiTheme.build()`, adds the child and calls `get_theme_stylebox("panel")` in the same frame gets **Godot's default theme** - whose `PanelContainer`/`ScrollContainer` boxes are plausible enough (a 60 %-opaque `Color(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.6)` panel) to read as "the variation did not resolve", which is the wrong conclusion for a `set_type_variation` role. Await one `process_frame` first; measured 2026-11-09 while checking that `UiTheme.RAISED_PANEL` resolves on a `ScrollContainer` (it does: the variation's `panel` item wins by name, whatever the base class).

- A `TreeItem` starts with `collapsed == false`, and `Tree` never expands or collapses on a double-click by itself - `item_activated` is only a signal. So code that lists a folder's children on first activation and then toggles `collapsed` folds the folder it just filled: the first double-click shows the arrow and a second one is needed to see the rows (measured on 4.7.2, 2026-11-14; `FileTreePane`). Populate, leave/force `collapsed = false`, and toggle only on an activation that already had rows.

### race

- Scrollback is write-behind, never written from the terminal path: `TermGrid::store_line` only updates `recent_lines` (which `waitForOutput` polls each frame and must see immediately) and calls `PaneHistory::push`, which queues the line for a per-pane writer thread. Do NOT call into SQLite from the grid (the grid mutex is what the UI renders under) and do NOT make the queue unbounded: it is bounded by the store's own retention window (row cap + 1 KiB-per-row byte cap), so a line it drops under flood is one `enforce_cap` deletes on the next commit - the retained scrollback stays contiguous. One writer per history file at a time **for the whole process** (`store::write_guard`): every pane's writer owns its own connection to the same file, and SQLite's write lock plus a busy handler that does not queue fairly let N panes starve one another - measured with a probe over one file, 8 unserialized writers dropped 7 batches and 16 dropped 15, all with `database is locked` (the same message `windows-smoke` showed), while the guarded version dropped none and committed *faster* (32.8k rows/s at 8 writers against 26.1k, since a dropped batch is wasted work) for ~5% against a single writer. The guard is always the innermost lock (taken inside a store method while a caller may hold the pane's store mutex), so the order cannot invert, and a poisoned guard proceeds *unserialized* rather than skipping the write: the busy timeout is then the backstop for another process on the same file. The trade is staleness: a search can miss the last `FLUSH_INTERVAL` (200 ms) of output, and anything buffered when a process dies without teardown (SIGKILL, `daemon stop`'s `process::exit`) is lost. On a normal quit `TerminalPane._exit_tree()` calls `flush_history`, which is the only hook that can live there: the GDExtension class's own `exit_tree` virtual was probed and never fires, while GDScript's does.

- Rebuilding kills whatever has the file mapped: a GUI dies with SIGBUS when a file it has mapped is written in place, and both writers now install by rename. `scripts/build` writes the library as `$LIB_DST.new` and renames it over `godot/bin/libgpty_gdext*.so` (the old in-place `cp` killed a `godot --path godot` with "Misaligned address error", measured 2026-11-13, twice, each taking every pane in it), and the export goes to `dist/.stage.XXXXXX` on `dist/`'s own filesystem and installs every entry with `install_atomic` - a file renamed over the old name, a directory renamed aside first and the old one removed - so a running `dist/gpty` keeps every inode it mapped and a failed export leaves the previous build intact. Stage inside the destination's filesystem: a cross-filesystem `mv` degrades to copy+unlink and the guarantee is gone. When a GUI dies with SIGBUS, check what was rebuilt under it before hunting a code bug.

- Resize Rate Limiting: Firing SIGWINCH heavily on every frame during window drag will overwhelm the child PTY process. Always debounce or rate-limit terminal `_on_resize` events before passing them to the backend. The **first** laid-out size is not a resize: `TerminalPane._start_child_if_ready` spawns the child at it (`start_shell`'s `rows`/`cols`, which open the pty sized), so the debounce never resizes a child by its own creation and a program that snapshots its size at startup reads the settled size.

- Empty grid cache: `_grid_offset()`/`_mouse_to_cell()` run on mouse events before the first grid sync - guard `_cell_cache.is_empty()` or the editor pauses on a script error and the app appears frozen.

- Pages deploy traps (v0.8.1): `actions/upload-pages-artifact` can report success before `/actions/runs/<id>/artifacts` lists the artifact - run 42688595589's deploy answered `Found 0 artifact(s)` 0.39 s after `Finalizing artifact upload` while it was the only live run - so a deploy polls the artifact list (30 × 2 s) for exactly one `github-pages` artifact instead of trusting the upload. `gh run rerun --failed` on a job that uploads adds a second `github-pages` artifact to the same run, and `deploy-pages` then refuses it (`Artifact count is 2`), which is why the upload and the deploy are separate jobs. Workflow-level `concurrency` serializes whole runs: `group: pages` with `cancel-in-progress: false` makes a second docs push wait, queued with no job started, until the first run finishes.

- **A gate script edited while it runs reports nonsense**: bash reads a script in blocks, so a write to `scripts/ci-check` (or any long gate) mid-run can make it execute shifted lines - measured 2026-11-14, a full `ci-check` that had passed every step through GUT died with `line 677: -p: command not found`, where line 677 is an `ln -sf` whose text contains no such word, and a clean-shell re-run of the *same* file passed end to end. Treat a gate that stops with an impossible command name at a plausible-looking line as evidence the file changed underneath it: check `git status`/`git diff` for the script, then re-run it before debugging the line. The inverse also bites - a run started *before* someone else's edit proves nothing about the tree you are about to commit.

- Concept push startup race: GDExtension classes aren't registered when autoloads initialize, so `ConceptManager._on_init()` defers its push via `call_deferred("_push_to_rust")`, and `workspace.gd` repeats it after `await create_timer(2.0)` as the fallback. There is no FFI object to own: `set_global_concepts`/`get_global_concepts` are **static** (the engine's concept set is process-wide), so the push is a plain `GptyTerminal.set_global_concepts(...)` guarded by `ClassDB.class_exists` - the old `ClassDB.instantiate("GptyTerminal")` vehicle leaked one ObjectDB entry per push, and a `GptyTerminal.new()` during autoload init would have been a zombie whose `#[func]` methods silently no-op. `ConceptManager` is also the single subscriber to its own `concepts_changed` (the store owns the push; a per-workspace connect both duplicated the push per workspace and collided across `Workspace` instances with Godot's "signal is already connected"), and `_push_to_rust` is the one entry point - the copy in `workspace.gd` that scanned tiles only to borrow a terminal's instance is gone.

- CLI runtime shape: `crates/gpty-cli/src/main.rs` runs on `#[tokio::main(flavor = "current_thread")]`. Every command is one request in a process that exits as soon as it has an answer, and nothing in the CLI or `gpty-ipc` uses `spawn_blocking`, `block_in_place` or `tokio::process`, so the multi-thread flavor's workers bought no parallelism - they were the only concurrency around `process::exit`, the plausible shape behind the single Windows `STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION` (`0xC0000374`) the smoke saw on an `inject` that printed nothing (v0.7.0). A worker pool adds startup cost (measured on Linux: 300 `gpty version` runs went from 1.04 s to 0.60 s) and an exit race to a one-request CLI; do not switch it back without evidence. The smoke's CLI teardown stress step (100 throwaway `pane-status` processes ≈ 200 connections) is the amplifier if it ever needs reproducing.

- `first_pipe_instance` must stay unspent until a create *succeeds*: the flag is what makes a failed create on an owned name answer `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED` rather than silently attaching to another process's pipe, so consuming it before the call (a `swap(false)` on the old field) spends the claim on an attempt. A transient failure then leaves every later instance non-first, a racing process owns the name, and a restarted GUI attaches to it instead of refusing. `IpcServer::create_with` loads the claim, creates, and records success only on `Ok`; its test drives that three-step sequence without a pipe, and the `rust-windows` job runs it because the arm is `#[cfg(windows)]`.

- A non-blocking media `seek` must keep `poll_video`/`poll_audio` **draining** while it is pending, not return early: the worker blocks in `send_bounded` on a full output queue and only reaches its command check once there is room, so a poll that stops consuming the moment a seek is in flight deadlocks the seek against a merely busy decoder. The caller claims a serial the worker publishes as the applied epoch; frames queued under the old epoch are consumed and dropped, never delivered, and `MediaSession::seek` returns once the command is queued (measured: 1 µs with the decoder parked, where the old acknowledgement wait hit its 5 s deadline and returned an error).

### lifecycle

- `Drop` impl for external resources: Any Rust struct holding a child process (`portable_pty::Child`) or I/O thread MUST implement `Drop` to call `.kill()`. Otherwise closing a terminal in Godot orphans the shell process and reader thread.

- The GDExtension must stay mapped while its threads live: it owns the tokio runtime's workers, one PTY reader per pane, and one history writer per pane, so Godot's unload of the library (`dlclose` at exit) used to free code those threads were executing - SIGSEGV in a `tokio-rt-worker` on a quit during IPC activity. `pin_library()` pins the mapping at `InitStage::Core` with `RTLD_NODELETE` (a reference `dlclose` cannot drop) on Unix, and on Windows with `GetModuleHandleExW` + `GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_PIN | ..._FROM_ADDRESS` (Godot calls `FreeLibrary` there; the address of the function itself names the module, so nothing depends on the DLL's file name - raw `extern "system"` + `#[link(name = "kernel32")]`, no `windows-sys` dependency). Do NOT remove it, and do not "fix" a shutdown crash by going back to `process::exit` - that skips the teardown the quit exists to run. The Windows branch is compile-verified by `ci-check`'s xwin/clang-cl step and CI's `rust-windows` job; its runtime is covered by the queued Windows smoke item.

- GraphEdit owns internal children (the connection layer, minimap container, popups): rebuilding a canvas by clearing `get_children()` deletes them and every later interaction logs `connections_layer is missing`. Remove only `GraphElement` children (`ConceptGraphEditor._rebuild_canvas_ui`). Its floating chrome (zoom buttons, view menu, minimap toggle) is viewport-anchored at the canvas origin and covers the first node's title at the default scroll offset - the editor disables that chrome and keeps zoom on ctrl+wheel.

- `tokio::task::JoinHandle` drop detaches: dropping a `JoinHandle` does NOT abort the task - it keeps running until it exits naturally. For explicit cleanup (e.g., in a `Drop` impl), call `handle.abort()`.

- Inspector close must tear down its OMP child: call `session_cancel` + `session_close` from `_exit_tree()`. Dropping a Godot node without closing the session leaves `omp` running.

- A lambda published into an autoload slot outlives the node that created it: `ShortcutManager.overlay_owns_keyboard = func(): return _keyboard_overlay() != null` kept pointing at a freed `Workspace`, and because the address was reused the next key press resolved the closure's `self` to an unrelated `ProbedPane` and raised `Nonexistent function '_keyboard_overlay' in base 'Control (ProbedPane)'` - `Callable.is_valid()` reported the callable as fine. Whatever node publishes a predicate or callback into an autoload puts the neutral lambda back in `_exit_tree()` (`Workspace` does), and a GUT suite that frees a workspace and then presses a key depends on that reset, not on the pointer happening to be dead.

- A `RefCounted` owner and the object it owns must not reference each other: `TerminalManager` stored `TileDrag.new(self)` while `TileDrag` stored `_tm`, and a hook lambda that captured the manager was itself stored on the manager. Neither cycle is ever collected - every exit leaked one manager + drag per workspace, `terminal_manager.gd`/`tile_drag.gd` stayed "resources still in use", and two managers' worth of lambdas outlived the `Workspace` script (measured 2026-11-09: 13 instances, 85 StringNames). The same leak fired on every closed workspace tab, because `_teardown_workspaces` drops extra managers. Shape that stays free: the owned helper reaches its owner through a `WeakRef` behind a getter-only property, and callbacks are bound methods (`on_open_pane_settings` takes `(manager, body)`) rather than closures over the owner. Regression tests: `test_terminal_manager.gd` (dropping a manager frees its drag; wiring a `Workspace` then freeing it leaves no reference).

### input-ownership

- Godot's focus traversal does not skip a disabled `BaseButton`: `find_next_valid_focus()` (and so Tab) filters only `FOCUS_NONE` and invisibility, while `KeyboardFocus.reachable_children` also filters `disabled` - so a toolbar whose buttons enable and disable must set `focus_mode = Control.FOCUS_NONE` on the disabled ones (`CliViewPane._sync_buttons` does) or a rebuilt ring still walks onto them. For the same reason a ring rebuilt from what is on screen must be allowed to shrink: `KeyboardFocus.ring` clears `focus_next`/`focus_previous` for a one-member list, because the paths a larger ring left behind keep pointing at the member that left it. Measured on 4.7.2: `--audit-focus cli-view-content` listed a just-exited run's disabled `StopButton` in the ring until both rules landed.

- Terminal paint granularity: Godot rebuilds a CanvasItem's **whole** command list on any `queue_redraw()`, and a control's own `_draw` runs before its children's, so a partial grid repaint needs child items. `TerminalPane` paints one background band and one text band per row (a `Layer` Node2D), then an overlay for the cursor, scrollback indicator, selection and search highlights; a partial sync queues only the rows its damage covers (`_painted_rows` records them, `draw_bench`'s `avg_rows` prints it, a full repaint queues every row). Three traps, all measured 2026-11-13: (1) the bands must sit at the origin and take the grid offset in the **pen** - `draw_string` picks its glyph raster from the position argument, not from the composed item transform, so a per-band `position` repainted every glyph with a different antialiasing (73 000 pixels in the draw-bench PNG); (2) every background band must stay before every text band - folding them into one band per row draws row r's text under row r+1's background, which clips a descender that overhangs its row. The tree order itself is the third trap: place the bands with **two** `move_child` passes (all backgrounds, then all texts), because an interleaved pass leaves every text band after the pane's chrome whenever the strip sits between the groups - `move_child` shifts the not-yet-placed siblings, and a probe pane with no strip hides it entirely (only the staged `search` capture showed the grid painting over the strip). `_draw_ms` is now a float sum of the bands a frame actually drew, so the budget above reads a one-row update as one row. A test of damage locality must not assert that the repainted rows are the cursor's: ConPTY rewrites the rows it relays, so one typed line there damaged rows 0, 3, 4 and 6 with the cursor on row 6 (measured on Windows CI 2026-11-13, and the Unix-shaped assertion is what turned that run red). The platform-neutral direction is text-changed => repainted: diff the cache's rows across the sync and require every changed row among `_painted_rows`, plus a small bound on the total.

- Scrollback vs. PageUp/Down: `terminal_pane.gd:_handle_keyboard` intercepts PageUp/Down for scrollback navigation. These never reach the PTY, so programs like `less` or `vim` cannot receive them. Users must use alternative keys (`b`/`f` in `less`, `Ctrl+B`/`Ctrl+F` in vim). The pane search bar is on `Ctrl+Shift+F`; plain `Ctrl+F` is never intercepted, so it reaches the PTY (and the documented vim workaround works).

- Ctrl+V passthrough: `Ctrl+V` MUST reach the shell as a literal `^V` (readline quoted-insert, vim visual-block). Paste is `Ctrl+Shift+V` only - never bind plain `Ctrl+V` to paste.

- A tooltip needs a hover target: the viewport's tooltip lookup skips a control whose `mouse_filter` is `IGNORE`, and `Label`/`RichTextLabel` default to that - so a `tooltip_text` set on a plain label is unreadable however good the sentence is (`SettingsPanel._make_concept_row`'s provenance, the Terminal tab's on-disk path, the concept editor's error list all shipped that way until v0.8.3). Set `mouse_filter = Control.MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` with the tooltip; `PASS` is enough for a custom-`_draw` control (`AgentBadge`), and a `Button`/`OptionButton` is a hover target already. `test_settings_panel.gd` walks the built panel and fails a tooltip-bearing `Label` that ignores the mouse.

- Container ancestors skip gui_input propagation: clicks on pane bodies never reach a wrapper's `gui_input` (proven by probe). Pane activation therefore lives in the workspace's raw `_input` with wrapper hit-testing, not in per-wrapper signal wiring.

- `z_index` is rendering-only for Control input: Godot 4 GUI picking uses REVERSE TREE ORDER (last sibling first), ignoring z_index. A full-rect overlay with z_index=100 that is NOT the last child draws on top but is dead to clicks - later-added siblings (workspace grids, sidebar, status bar) eat its input. Every overlay (pane settings popup, global settings panel, palette) must `move_child(overlay, -1)` when opened so it is topmost for both picking and rendering. The z bump is still required for RENDERING when grids are added after the overlay.

- `_gui_input` does not bubble to ancestors on Godot 4.7.2 (measured): a focused `Button` inside a `Control` whose `gui_input` was connected delivered the key to the button alone, with `mouse_filter` STOP or IGNORE on either side. A container cannot see its children's keys that way, which is why the wiki pane's Escape is read in `_input` and scoped by `gui_get_focus_owner()` (`is_ancestor_of`), and why pane-chrome Escape lives in `Workspace._escape_pane_chrome`. `_unhandled_input` also works only when no child consumes the key (a `TerminalPane` accepts every key it sees), so an input-stage handler plus a focus-owner check is the form that does not depend on what the focused widget does with the event.

- Escape never reaches an overlay's `_unhandled_input` while a terminal has focus: a focused `TerminalPane` consumes every key in `_handle_keyboard` (its fall-through path calls `accept_event()`) after sending the mapped bytes to the child - measured 2026-11-03: Escape left Settings and Pane Settings open and wrote a raw ESC to the shell, and typing with Settings open reached the prompt (`x`). Overlay Escape is handled in `Workspace._input` now, before GUI input, and each overlay takes the keyboard on open (GDScript page, "Overlay keyboard ownership"); do not move it back into an overlay's `_unhandled_input`, and do not show an overlay with a bare `visible = true` - that path leaves the keyboard on the pane behind it. The related `LineEdit` trap is still live for any focused text field: Escape leaves editing mode (`is_editing()` becomes false), after which Enter stops emitting `text_submitted` - the palette it used to reach looked alive but was dead, which is why the input stage, not the field, owns Escape.

- Terminal mouse reporting: the grid's mouse-mode bits (`GptyTerminal.get_mouse_mode`, `gpty_core::term::MOUSE_MODE_*`) are the single source of truth for whether the child owns the mouse. The pane forwards only what the enabled modes cover (DECSET 1000 click, 1002 drag, 1003 any-motion), encodes SGR when 1006 is set and the legacy X10 form otherwise, and must leave selection/scrollback untouched when the bits are zero. `Shift` bypasses reporting (xterm's convention) so text selection stays reachable - removing that traps the user in any full-screen app that grabs the mouse.

- Divider resize is the **handle layer's**, not a pane's: one control per divider-line segment, owned by `DividerHandles` inside the workspace grid. The layer must stay the grid's topmost child (`_attach_pane_into` moves it back after adding a wrapper) because Godot picks the last sibling first and the handles must sit over the panes they separate; a handle takes the pointer (`MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` + HSIZE/VSIZE) only when `TerminalManager.divider_limits` reports travel, so a single pane and a divider pinned at `MIN_TILE` show an arrow and start nothing. It cannot live inside a wrapper: a `PanelContainer` fits every child into its content rect, so a strip there covers only the inside of the 1 px stylebox border - two neighbours left those 2 px dead - and the handle's `mouse_default_cursor_shape` is what puts the resize cursor on hover, whereas an imperative `DisplayServer.cursor_set_shape` is overwritten by the hovered control's default and only flashes. The drag itself is driven from `workspace._input` (`drive_edge_drag`) because the motion right after a press on the band is already over the pane body, which would otherwise read it as a text selection.

### untrusted-input

- A store file can be page-structured and still not be a database: the reported `user://history.db` (2026-11-10) was 56,938,496 bytes whose every 4096-byte page began with a SQLite b-tree page-type byte (`0d`/`0a`/`05`/`02`), yet it held no `SQLite format 3` header and no `CREATE TABLE` cell anywhere - so `file` called it `data`, the first `PRAGMA` returned `file is not a database (26)`, and `sqlite3 .recover` failed with the same sentence, because recovery walks the schema page and that file's schema page was gone. Check for the 16-byte magic (`head -c 16`) and for the schema text before deciding a store is a database with a bad row; pages without a schema are unrecoverable, not merely unreadable by one tool. `store::open_with_recovery` now moves such a file and its `-wal`/`-shm` siblings (siblings first) to `<path>.corrupt` and opens a fresh store, one warning per process instead of one per pane and under the write guard so concurrent opens move it once; `HistoryStore::open` and `VaultStore::open` both go through it, so the scrollback database and the vault index recover as `history.db.corrupt` and `vaults.db.corrupt` instead of ending that store until the file is deleted by hand.

- Restore ordering and env authority: the env chain is three deliberate steps, in order - `_restore_into` strips any `shell_env` a file carries (legacy tiles; a toast names what was dropped - never adopt it into the store, that would launder a hostile file's payload into the trusted map), `SettingsManager.apply_to_terminal` sets the user's global, and `TerminalPane._ready` overlays `PaneEnvStore.env_for(attachment_id)` last (the id is final there: uniqueness renames run before the wrapper enters the tree). Do NOT re-add file env to any step of that chain, and do NOT write `PaneEnvStore` from anywhere but the pane settings UI path (`workspace.gd`'s `settings_applied` handler, which also re-keys the entry when the pane's id changes).

- Do not scrape agent TUIs: PTY bytes are presentation, not structured events. Semantic observability comes only from documented OMP/Claude/Gemini hooks or extensions. Regex concepts remain valid for ordinary shell output (e.g. `cat` → code viewer).

- Data paths never reach `load()`: a `.tres` whose sub-resource is a GDScript executes during `load()` (a `.tres` typed as a font was enough - `ResourceLoader.exists()` is true for it). `TerminalFonts` is the font boundary (bytes, absolute path, extension + magic + face checks) and `PaneTypes.settings_schema` is the closed settings table; `PaneBody.apply_settings` is the only generic assignment path. A new key added to a pane's `_get_layout_state` without a table rule silently stops surviving restore - `test_pane_settings.gd::test_every_pane_type_accepts_the_settings_it_saves` fails instead.

- Event vs control sockets: `ompEvent` lives on `gpty-events.sock`. Putting it on the control socket would require giving the extension `GPTY_SECRET` (workspace control) or weakening auth. Keep them separate.

- Event capability is per-PTY: unregister on spawn failure and `Drop`. A capability for terminal A must never be accepted for terminal B. Compare capabilities in constant time.

- Pane file sinks (`code_viewer`, `file_tree`, `wiki`): `FileAccess.file_exists()` is a **regular-file** check on Godot 4.7.2 (measured: false for directories, character devices and FIFOs - even reached through a symlink - true for regular files and symlinks to them) and `FileAccess.get_size()` returns -1 for anything non-regular, so that pair is the type gate and a FIFO never reaches `FileAccess.open()` (which would block the GUI thread until a writer appears). The read guard is `TextRead.read_prefix` - one definition every reading pane calls: absolute paths only, that regular-file gate, a `TextRead.DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB) cap (the reader is the GUI thread and the path can come from an untrusted layout/profile), and a torn UTF-8 tail decoded by hand, because cutting at the cap often lands inside a sequence. `code_viewer` and `file_tree` call it directly; the wiki pane's note view calls `GptyTerminal.vault_note_read`, which applies the same cap, the same regular-file gate and the same torn-tail drop in `gpty_core::vault` - and its editor is the pane set's only writer, through `GptyTerminal.vault_note_write` on an explicit save and `vault_note_create`/`vault_note_rename`/`vault_note_delete` on their explicit actions (the vault bullets above have the rules - including the crash-recovery copy that sits beside the save and never touches a vault). `file_tree` never hands a bare name to the system: activating a path `ViewableFiles` names opens it in a `code_viewer` pane through the panes-never-spawn-panes request (below; the per-tree `open_in` setting can leave every file on the system path), while anything else validates an absolute path, builds the one `file://` URI itself (scheme allowlist - a basename cannot contain `/`, so no scheme can be injected), and asks for confirmation, because a downloaded `.desktop` file is *run* by the mime handler. The table is an allowlist with no content sniff - `ViewableFiles.viewer_for` decides from the lowercased extension or an exact extensionless name, so a binary is never decoded as text - and the viewer's **Reload** action exists because opening the same file again focuses the existing pane instead of re-reading it; a routed capture clears `file_path`, so a viewer now showing capture text can never be mistaken for the file's pane. Godot 4's `CodeEdit` has `add_comment_delimiter(start, end, line_only)`, NOT `add_comment_string` - the latter raised a script error that silently aborted `load_file` before `_refresh_view()`.

- The media pane (`media`, `MediaFiles` + `MediaPane`): a local-file sink under the same trust stance as the text panes, with one sharper hazard - a path handed to `ResourceLoader.load` would load whatever a file-supplied tile named (a `.gd` or `.tscn` behind a media extension is code), so `MediaFiles` is a **closed extension table** and both streams go through `GptyMedia` (see below): video as RGBA frames, audio as PCM pushed into an `AudioStreamGenerator`. `check` is the one path gate (absolute, `FileAccess.file_exists`'s regular-file check, unknown formats refused before a decoder), and `load_media` re-runs it every time because the path can come from `workspaces.json`/a profile; a refusal clears `file_path` and explains itself in the pane (no toast, no `push_error` - a bad path is a caller's question, and GUT counts engine errors). Remote/URL streaming is deliberately absent (its own trust boundary, queued in v0.7.0), and project schemes (`res://`/`user://`) are refused with the non-absolute paths. **Video is the Rust backend**: `VIDEO_EXTENSIONS` covers `ogv/mp4/m4v/mov/mkv/webm/avi/ts/m2ts`, a video session opens both streams (the pane drains audio too; an unconsumed queue is backpressure and would stall the other stream), frames are drained only while a small PTS-ordered backlog has room and presented against the media clock below - the backend's bounded queue is the backpressure, because a fixed drain count followed by "keep the newest four" discarded frames that were due (the decoder decodes a whole clip in milliseconds, so the picture froze on the first frame while audio advanced); stale frames are dropped only when a newer one is waiting, and without audio the clock starts on the first frame's own PTS (a stream whose timeline does not begin at zero would otherwise be held as "in the future"), and the surface is a `TextureRect` with aspect-preserving center stretch. **Audio is the same backend**: `AUDIO_EXTENSIONS` covers `ogg/oga/opus/mp3/wav/flac/m4a/aac`, decoded f32 is pushed into an `AudioStreamGenerator` (48 kHz stereo, 0.2 s buffer), and the generator starts on the first real chunk so `get_playback_position()` and the media PTS share an origin. Chunks are held in a bounded 32-chunk local lead and drained from the backend even when the generator is full - leaving that queue full would block the worker, which also decodes video. With audio running the video clock is `get_playback_position()` mapped from the first chunk's PTS (20 ms tolerance, 150 ms catch-up); without audio it is the monotonic start clock. Volume (`-40..6 dB`) and mute (`-80 dB`) are pane settings saved in the tile. Two PCM facts are pinned: `pcm_u8` is in the component set, and a frame with an unspecified channel layout must be normalized **on the frame**, not only on the resampler (swresample otherwise answers `InputChanged`). **Transport:** a bottom bar offers Play/Pause, an `HSlider` seek, elapsed/total and Loop. Pause pauses the generator and freezes the clock (video-only offsets `_clock_start_us` on resume); seek goes through the backend's queued seek and then drops local frame/audio queues, stops the audio player and releases the generator playback (its `clear_buffer` refuses while the playback is active - paused included - and `play()` instantiates a fresh, empty generator playback, so dropping the reference is what discards the samples), and resets the clock epoch; loop seeks to 0 at EOF (the worker survives it) and is saved in layout state, while Play on a finished non-looping file restarts from zero. The slider marks `_seeking` so the position update does not fight the drag. The backend's format policy is this table at the edge plus `components.txt`/the Rust allowlists (see the Rust media bullet), and it refuses a file it cannot decode before any decoder starts. The file tree routes a supported media file through `request_pane` exactly as it routes text (`ViewableFiles` first, then `MediaFiles.pane_for`), and a same-path request focuses the media pane already holding it (two would double the sound and the decode work) - the viewer's dedupe rule, not a new policy. The pane accepts no routed content; its transport state is reported through `status_document()` (see the pane status contract).

- `FileAccess.set_unix_permissions` follows a symlink, so a bare `chmod` on a store path a link occupies changes the *link's target* - a file outside gPTY's stores. Every mode repair goes through `gpty_core::owner_only` (`O_NOFOLLOW` open, `fstat` the descriptor, `fchmod` it), never a second `chmod` call site; the stores, the vault's recovery directory and the log directory all use it.

- FFmpeg must never open a media path: its `file` protocol calls `open(2)` with plain `O_RDONLY`, so a FIFO swapped in after `validate_path`'s stat blocks the decode worker uninterruptibly - no interrupt callback fires inside a blocked syscall, and `MediaSession::drop` joins that worker, so the Godot thread waits with it - bounded since v0.7.1 (`CLOSE_TIMEOUT_MS`, 2 s, after which the thread is abandoned with its FFmpeg contexts), but the blocked syscall is still the bug: the close bound only keeps one stuck decoder from freezing the pane close and the window quit. `gpty-media/src/source.rs` opens the descriptor itself (`O_NONBLOCK | O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC`, `fstat`-verified, a symlink resolved once) and hands FFmpeg a custom `AVIOContext` (`AVFMT_FLAG_CUSTOM_IO`) with the path as a probe hint only; a path-based open back in the crate fails `tests/binding_rules.rs`.

### gate-lies

- A new `class_name` that annotates a field or a parameter with `TerminalManager` makes the global class registry compile `terminal_manager.gd` while it registers classes - before the autoloads exist - and `terminal_manager.gd` reads `SettingsManager` in `spawn`, so that compile fails and *every* `TerminalManager.new()` becomes `Nonexistent function 'new' in base 'GDScript'`: a `godot -s` launch (the capture harness, `scripts/ui-capture`) then runs with a Nil manager in every workspace, while GUT - which compiles the app's own scenes first - keeps passing. `divider_handles.gd` holds its manager untyped for exactly this reason; a new class that needs one should do the same, or take it as an untyped parameter.

- GDScript's `%` on a String is the **format operator**, and an Array on its right is the *argument list*, not one value: `"...: %s" % changed` with `changed = ["pane_name", "font_size"]` raises `String formatting error: not all arguments converted during string formatting` at that line, which GUT records as an unexpected engine error - a red gate next to an assertion that actually passed. Wrap the value (`% str(changed)`) or write one specifier per value (`% [a, b]`). A Dictionary or a String on the right is formatted as a single value, which is why `% answer` is fine; an Array of one element silently formats and two or more raise, so the trap only shows up as a test's list grows. Measured 2026-11-14.

- A regression test that hands the value under test **straight into the fixed function** passes on the unfixed tree. Measured 2026-11-15: `test_a_profile_written_in_a_coarser_unit_activates_the_same_shares` first built `{"grid_unit": 12, …}` inline and passed it to `_do_activate`, which already honoured a declared unit - the defect was that no *producer* wrote the field, so the assertion held before and after the fix. Route the test through the producer (`ProfileManager.refresh_plugin_profiles` from the store JSON, then `find_profile`) so the missing write is what fails, and check the new test is red on the pre-fix tree (`git stash` the source only) before trusting it. The same shape catches a guard whose *consumer* was never broken: assert the producer's output, not only the geometry the consumer computes from a hand-built input.

- A shell function is only as green as its **last** command: `run_tooling_scripts` ended on `[ -n "$TMP" ] && rm -rf "$TMP"`, which is false whenever the variable is unset, so the function returned 1 after every check inside it had passed - and under `set -e` the gate exited there, printing a clean step list and no final verdict. The pre-commit hook then refused the commit with no message of its own. End a step function with `return 0` (or an `if` whose condition may be false) and judge a gate by its last line, not by the absence of a failure: `ci-check` prints "All checks passed" only after the final step. Measured 2026-11-13, a commit aborted after ten PASS lines.

- CLI `gpty version` is local-only: it prints the CLI's own crate version and exits without touching IPC. It cannot probe a running GUI. Use `gpty daemon status` or `list-panes` to test connectivity/auth.

- SSH commit signing needs the key registered as a **Signing Key**, not only for authentication: with `user.signingkey` at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub`, `gpg.format=ssh` and `commit.gpgsign=true`, a commit is signed locally (`git verify-commit` reports Good once `gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile` names the key), but GitHub answers `commit.verification.reason = unknown_key` and the protected-branch signature rule is still bypassed. Add the same public key at Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key with **Key type: Signing Key**; the default `gh` token cannot do it (`admin:ssh_signing_key` is not in its scopes).

### doc-drift

- The preview path has its own cap, and it is **the same number**: `GptyMarkdown.render` cuts its input at `MAX_MARKDOWN_BYTES`, which is `TextRead.DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` and `gpty_core::vault::MAX_NOTE_BYTES` (1 MiB) - `crates/gpty-gdext/src/markdown.rs`'s `the_input_cap_is_the_read_cap_the_panes_apply` reads the GDScript declaration and fails if they ever drift, because a pane that shows a note at its read cap has to render all of it, or its own "showing the first 1 MiB" claim is a lie about a view that stopped sooner. The cut is never silent: the render answer is JSON - `{text, truncated, shown, size}`, the same shape a read answers (`shown`/`size` are bytes of the source) - and `MarkdownView` is the one place a reader is told, as a banner **above** the body: its own numbers when the renderer's cap bit (a pasted buffer, a routed capture, a long model turn), and `set_source_notice` for a cut the *caller* made. A pane must pass its read-cap notice that way rather than appending it to the source: a note at the read cap is at the renderer's cap too, so an appended notice is the first thing the cut would drop - which is exactly the case the notice exists for. The text panes keep their own notice at the end of the text they hold (`TextRead.truncation_notice`, now a bare sentence the caller places).

- A roadmap row may cite a gitignored working note only **by path, never `path:line`**: `scripts/docs-check` resolves every backticked `path:line` citation against `git ls-files`, so `TEMP/<note>.md:12` is reported as a citation to a missing file and turns CI red, while a bare `TEMP/<note>.md` is not a citation at all and passes. Measured 2026-11-15 while queueing the OSC 7501 rows.

### platform-parity

- Pane exit detection needs two signals, not one: `pty_rx` closing (Unix EOF when the child exits) **and** a `CHILD_POLL_MS` (200 ms) `try_wait` poll whose result starts an `EXIT_DRAIN_QUIET_MS` (500 ms) quiet window before the task ends. Waiting for EOF alone is not enough - ConPTY keeps the pty pipe open after the child exits, so on Windows every pane whose command finished reported `running: true` with no exit code (`paneStatus`/`paneRun`'s whole contract), and on Unix a SIGHUP-immune descendant holding the pty does the same (the kernel only HUPes the foreground group when the session leader exits). The quiet window is what keeps ending early from truncating output the pty still holds: any output re-arms it. `try_wait` does not consume the status - std caches it on Unix and Windows reads the exit code - so the teardown's own poll still returns the same answer. `a_shell_that_exits_while_the_pty_is_held_open_is_still_reported` pins it (it fails on a no-op mutation, 10 s timeout). A task that ends *without* recording an exit code is the third case, and the one that used to lie: nothing awaits the `JoinHandle`, so a panic inside the task left the pane reporting `running: true` forever and hung every consumer that waits for exit. `SpawnedTerminal::task_finished()` is the only thing that notices it, `running` is `exit_code.is_none() && !task_finished()`, and the document carries `exit_reason` (`exited`, `task_ended`, or `null` while running). `SpawnedTerminal::status_json` builds that document in core - the pane API's promise and the tested artifact are the same bytes. The document also carries `foreground_job`: the same 200 ms poll samples the PTY's foreground process group (`tcgetpgrp` on Unix, exact; `null` on Windows/ConPTY, which cannot tell), and the GUI's close confirmation is its only consumer - a background job does not count, so `sleep 600 &` never blocks a close while a typed `sleep 600` does. The comparison is against the direct child's pid, so a pane whose *command* is the busy program (`command: "sh", args: ["-c", "sleep 600"]`) answers `foreground_job: false` exactly like a background job - to stage a busy pane in a test or capture, type the command into an interactive shell (that is what `ui_capture.gd`'s `running-work` state does). Its second field, `child_alive`, exists because `running: false` (a waiter must stop) and "no process a close would kill" (the close guard must ask) are different questions: it is the task's last `try_wait` answer, set true where the child is spawned and false at the reap, so a pane whose task died while its child survived still says the process exists. Do not fold it back into `running` - that reintroduces the wait-forever bug above.

- Release bundles carry the pinned FFmpeg runtime: the GDExtension has an `$ORIGIN` (Linux) / `@loader_path` (macOS) rpath, so `scripts/bundle-media` is the one packer - `linux`/`windows` copy the shared libraries and an `ldd` check refuses an unresolved bundle, `macos-libs` lipos the two per-arch builds into universal dylibs and ad-hoc signs them (the macOS FFmpeg build uses `--install-name-dir=@rpath` so the GDExtension records relocatable names), and `macos-zip` injects those pre-signed libraries into the exported `.app` on the Linux export job. Every bundled dylib and GDExtension slice is checked against the app's declared 10.13 (x86_64) / 11.0 (arm64) floor by `scripts/check-macos-minos` after lipo: a newer runner SDK default silently raises it. `macos_libs` lipos only canonical files and recreates the alias symlinks, so the bundle carries one copy per library instead of a real copy per alias. `scripts/build` uses the same helper.
