## Added

- **`cli_view` panes.** A pane type that runs a program plus argv - never a shell string - and streams its merged stdout and stderr into the pane body as plain text: no PTY, no stdin, no ANSI interpretation, so no sequence from the child can move a cursor or change what is drawn. Spawnable from the CLI (`gpty new-pane --type cli_view --command prog --arg …`), the palette, and profile or plugin tiles (which pass the Workspace Trust gate, because naming a program is what the gate is for). The child is held to the same `validate_program` rule as a terminal's and stripped of `GPTY_SECRET`/`GPTY_SOCKET`/the event capability; the pane keeps the stream after the child exits and reports the exit through the same status document as a terminal. This is the v1 plugin UI: a plugin's `[[profiles]]` can render a status command in a pane without a Godot SDK.
- **Plugin manifests, and a validator that is the shipped parser.** `gpty-plugin.toml` declares `id` (`owner/name`, immutable while the repo exists), `name`, `version`, `min_gpty_version`, `platforms`, `build`/`startup` argv, and five array-of-table sections: actions (≤64), events (≤64), link handlers (≤16), concepts (≤128) and profiles (≤64 profiles × ≤64 tiles). Validation keeps the same posture as every other untrusted-input path: size and count caps, a closed key set, argv never a shell string, tiles that mirror `PaneTypes.sanitize_tile` with rejection instead of clamping, actions limited to the published CLI surface (the same derivation the 19 MCP tools come from), events limited to the event-socket vocabulary, and every concept round-tripped through the engine's own parser - a trigger the Rust `regex` crate cannot compile (a PCRE2 lookbehind, say) rejects the manifest rather than being silently dropped. `gpty plugin validate <path>` runs it offline (`--json`, exit 1 on rejection), so a plugin repo's CI can check a manifest before anyone installs it. The first-party tool layouts live one repo per tool under the `godot-pty` org.
- **Plugin install, review, and lifecycle.** `gpty plugin install <owner>/<repo>[@ref]` clones with git argv into a staging dir, parses and gates the manifest (the id must equal the install target, the platform must be declared, `min_gpty_version` must not exceed the CLI), and then asks a human: the summary is sent to the GUI, which lists every action, event, link handler, concept and profile the plugin declares - including the programs each profile would run - beside the ref you asked for and the revision it resolved to. Declining, disconnecting, or having no GUI means nothing installs, and the CLI's deadline for that answer is 300 s rather than the usual 5, carried with the request so the dialog closes itself when the request dies. On acceptance the content moves to `<data_dir>/plugins/<id>`, per-plugin `config`/`state`/`logs` directories are created, and the record - including the validated profiles - lands in `state_dir()/plugins.json` with the revision pinned to a commit SHA, so a moved tag is a new revision and re-reviews. `list`, `enable`, `disable`, `uninstall`, `logs` and `run <id> <action>` manage the store; an admin action notifies a running GUI (never starts one) so its profile list has caught up before the command returns.
- **Profile layouts now come from plugins.** The shipped tool layouts - herdr, lazygit, nvim, claude, OMP - left `godot/profiles.default.json` for those plugin repos, so `Agent Workspace` is the only built-in and a first run opens no dialog. Installed plugins' profiles appear in the sidebar between the built-ins and the user's own, with their provenance in the tooltip (plugin id and pinned revision), no delete or rename affordance, and the ` (n)` dedupe re-derived whenever a user profile takes or frees a name - a collision used to resolve to the *plugin's* row for the rest of the session, so clicking the user's row activated the plugin's profile. `layout list` and `layout load` see them, a plugin approved at its pinned revision activates without re-asking (a newer revision re-prompts), and a catalog hint row appears while no plugin profile is installed. Shipped files are never written back: a plugin profile vanishes with its plugin.
- **A plugin registry, and a page that lists it.** `godot-pty/gpty-plugins` is the canonical index - `registry.json` plus `validate.py`, a closed key set per entry, checked weekly against every listed repo's manifest at HEAD so a vanished or renamed repo is noticed - and the docs site renders it at `/plugins/`, fetched at build time with a committed snapshot as the offline fallback (the build warns when it falls back, so a stale page is visible). The registry is display data: nothing in it executes, and `gpty plugin install` never consults it.
- **Agent state is part of the pane contract.** `PaneBody.agent_state_source_id()` names the terminal a pane observes by stable `attachment_id`, and `on_agent_state_changed(state)` receives that terminal's state; `workspace.gd` is the only dispatcher - it delivers on real transitions and primes every new observer, including a follower whose terminal appears later or one re-pointed at a different source, without re-priming settled panes. The titlebar badge is the first implementation and runs *through* this path rather than beside it. Display only: a Tier 2 declaration is spoofable by anything that prints and Tier 3 is a heuristic, so state never feeds a decision, an action, a capture or IPC.
- **Workspace Trust remembers.** `TrustedStore` (`user://trusted.json`) short-circuits the gate for what was already approved: a shipped built-in at this app version, a tile whose exact spawn plan (`program` + argv) an approval covers, or a plugin at its pinned revision. A new version or revision re-prompts, content that arrived any other way (user-authored profiles, layout files) keeps asking, and only the trust dialogs' confirm paths write the record. `layout load` over IPC keeps refusing an untrusted profile - a caller cannot answer a dialog, and naming a profile is not consent to what the file asks for.
- **A pane's environment belongs to the user, not to a file.** Restore strips any `shell_env` a saved tile carries (with a toast naming what was dropped) instead of adopting it, and per-pane env lives in `user://pane_env.json`, keyed by `attachment_id`, written only by the pane settings UI and overlaid last at spawn. Profiles lose the ability to carry env by design - a profile that needs one points at the shell rc, or asks the user to set it once - which closes the path where a downloaded layout handed a pane its `PATH` or a `PROMPT_COMMAND`.
- **A clock in the status bar**, beside the version; the window-mode readout moved off it (the sidebar owns that switcher).

## Changed

- **The AUR recipe follows the 0.5.4 bundle layout.** It installs the CLI and the GUI side by side (`/usr/lib/gpty/{gpty,gpty-gui,gpty-gui.pck,libgpty_gdext.linux.x86_64.so}`, both on `PATH`), points the desktop entry at `gpty-gui`, installs the icon from `godot/icon.png`, and takes the tarball hash from the release's `SHA256SUMS` asset.

## Fixed

- **A locked history store no longer drops the batch it was committing.** Two panes committing at once could make SQLite return `SQLITE_BUSY` past the 5 s `busy_timeout`, and the writer logged the failure and dropped the batch - scrollback that the store's own retention window would have kept. The writer now waits for the lock (bounded by the pane's own task) and commits. Measured before the fix: 7 of 15 batches dropped under contention; 0 of 15 after.
- **`gpty new-pane --pane-type code_viewer` failed** (and so did `file_tree` and `cli_view`). `PaneType` serialized kebab-case (`code-viewer`) while every other surface - the GUI's `PaneTypes.ALL`, the CLI's accepted names, the manifest validator, the docs - used `code_viewer`, so a multi-word type reached the GUI as a key it does not know. The enum now has one spelling in both directions (`Serialize` writes `as_str()`, `Deserialize` goes through `parse()`), the CLI's and the validator's lists are derived from `PaneType::ALL`, and a test parses `PaneTypes.ALL` out of the GUI source and compares key for key - the previous count-only checks would have passed a rename on either side.
- **Windows concept matching was dead.** ConPTY renders line breaks as cursor moves rather than LFs, and the discard-only line parser committed a line only on LF, so no output line ever reached the concept matcher - a shipped or user-defined trigger could not fire in a Windows pane. The parser now commits on the cursor-move breaks ConPTY emits (and still ignores a redraw), and the smoke asserts a routed `concept` event from real output on whichever platform runs it.
- **`gpty pane-wait --socket <path>`** ignored the flag - which is global on the CLI - and talked to the default socket. It reaches the resolved socket now, and the server's fallback honors `paneWait`'s own deadline instead of ending a long wait early.
- **A pane whose terminal task died looked like a running one.** Nothing awaited the task's `JoinHandle`, so a panic inside it - or a child that closed its pty and outlived the pane - left the status document reporting `running: true` with no exit code, forever, and every consumer that waits for an exit hung. Liveness is now part of the document (`exit_reason` is `exited`, `task_ended` or null while running), built in core so the pane API's promise and the tested artifact are the same bytes.
- **A failed `resize_grid` desynced a pane's size permanently.** The grid and the PTY are now resized as one transaction (`false` = refused, nothing moved, PTY included), the pane keeps its own dimensions in step with the backend, and a resize is applied from the size at debounce time rather than a stale one.
- **The concept push leaked a `GptyTerminal` per push.** `ConceptManager._push_to_rust` fabricated an instance through `ClassDB.instantiate("GptyTerminal")` as a vehicle for a call on a static accessor, growing `ObjectDB` on every settings save, concept toggle and editor save. The engine-global accessors are called statically now, and `scripts/check-ffi-surface` covers class-name calls too (61 → 90 checked call sites), which is what had let that call site go unverified.

## Added

- **Plugin concepts reach the engine.** A plugin's `[[concepts]]` - validated against the engine's own parser at install - were counted in the review and then dropped. They now travel the path profiles use: the store record carries the validated entries, the new static `GptyTerminal.installed_plugin_concepts()` shapes the enabled records, and `ConceptManager` merges them **between the shipped defaults and your own rules** (the order builtins/plugin/user uses for profiles). A name a shipped default or an earlier plugin holds is not stolen: the plugin yields with a ` (n)` suffix, so uninstall and re-install give the bare name back. A user toggle or edit *overlays* the plugin's rule by name - which is what makes the Settings toggle, edit and delete work on installed content - and a deleted plugin rule is written as a disabled overlay rather than removed from a file the plugin owns. The Settings list shows where a rule came from, the visual canvas stays scoped to the rules it can own (defaults and yours), and uninstall/disable drops the rules without a restart through the existing `pluginsChanged` refresh. The install review now names each rule and what it would do (capture ✓/notify-only, routing targets, ships-disabled) instead of printing a count. `[[events]]` and `[[link_handlers]]` remain declared and reviewed only - nothing consumes them yet, and both are execution paths whose delivery is its own trust decision (queued).

## Changed

- **The CLI starts a GUI only for commands a fresh one can satisfy.** `new-pane` and `layout load` still auto-start the workspace (unless `--no-daemon`); every other command - queries, pane-targeted mutations, `concept toggle`, and `daemon stop`/`status` - now fails with `no gpty GUI is running (start one with \`gpty daemon start\`)` and exit 1, instead of opening a window and then failing at the command's actual work (`gpty list-panes` used to launch the GUI it was trying to query). `gpty daemon start` is the explicit spawner, `gpty daemon stop` with nothing running is a no-op, and the MCP server never auto-starts a GUI: its `daemon-start` tool is the bootstrap, and other tool calls that find none say so. A GUI that cannot start - no display, missing libraries - now reports its own stderr immediately instead of waiting out the timeout in silence.
- **Declared-only manifest sections now say so in the install review.** A plugin's `[[events]]`, `[[link_handlers]]`, and `build`/`startup` are declarations gPTY never dispatches or runs; the review printed "Listens for:" and "not run at install", which implied delivery at some later point. The sections now read as the declarations they are - the plugin reads the event socket itself, the Markdown view opens only `http(s)`/`mailto` links and runs no handler, and neither build nor startup is executed - and `docs/content/plugins.md` states the model (a plugin that wants events subscribes to the event socket, whose path a program launched in a pane already has).
- **The five first-party plugin repos validate with the shipped validator.** Each repo's `validate.yml` installs `gpty` from the v0.5.5 commit (`cargo install --git … --rev 2f17459… --locked`; the SHA is the pin, a tag is mutable) and runs `gpty plugin validate .` - the same `parse_manifest` the install path runs - replacing the provisional inline `tomllib` + id script. Only the `id`-equals-repo assertion stays inline, because that is the install gate's contract and the validator cannot know which repo a manifest lives in.

## Fixed

- **A second gPTY window can no longer hijack the control socket.** `IpcServer::serve()` unlinked an existing socket after checking only that it was a socket owned by this UID, so a second instance took the path and orphaned the running one: both windows stayed up, every CLI command went to the newcomer, and the older workspace became unreachable with no message anywhere (measured: two processes, two listeners on `/run/user/1000/gpty.sock`, the older one's inode unlinked). The bind now probes the path first and refuses when a server answers - replacing only a socket nothing is listening on, so a restart after a crash still works - and the same rule covers the event socket and, on Windows, the named pipe (which previously spun on a taken name instead of refusing). A checkout that cannot serve asks itself to quit through the existing shutdown flag and says why in a toast instead of vanishing: a window without a pane API is worse than no window.
- **An agent-state observer hears a terminal's spawn state once.** The terminal's slow poll compared the engine's tiered state against a shadow that started empty, so the first poll after the workspace's entry delivery re-announced the spawn state as if it were a change - every follower's hook (and the titlebar badge) was told `idle` twice. The hook now records the delivery and the poll reports only deltas against it, which is the once-on-entry-plus-every-change contract `PaneBody.on_agent_state_changed` promises.
- **A stale CLI on `PATH` now says so.** The CLI and the GUI must come from the same release: an older `gpty` shadowing the bundle's CLI failed opaquely (`error: unrecognized subcommand 'plugin'` while the running GUI was 0.5.5, and its own `gpty version` is local-only by design). Every command that talks to a GUI now compares what it reports - IPC protocol first, then version, direction-aware - and prints one stderr warning naming both sides and the remedy; the check rides on probes the CLI already makes, a command that has not probed does one best-effort check (500 ms, never able to fail or gate it), and the MCP server warns the same way at startup. The protocol version also has one definition now (`gpty_ipc::protocol::PROTOCOL_VERSION`), shared by the server's `version` response, the CLI, and the About tab, which had a hardcoded `2.0`.
- **An agent-state observer is told a value once, whichever path carried it.** The entry scan broadcast the current state to every observer of a terminal, so attaching a second follower re-told the first a value it already held; and a follower that joined while a change was in flight heard the change before its entry, then the same value again from the scan. Each observer now carries `[source, last state]`: the scan's entry goes to the new pane alone, a change reaches only panes already settled for that source, and a repeat of the held value is dropped - the dispatcher-side mirror of the terminal's `_badge_state` rule. Three contract tests pin it (a change dispatched before the entry, a second follower attaching, a repeated dispatch).
- **`gpty daemon status --json` answers JSON on every path.** The running case printed the raw `version` response (parseable), but the not-running, busy, refused and auth paths printed prose - a script that probed with `--json` got unparseable output exactly when the probe mattered. Those paths now answer the shaped vocabulary the MCP `daemon-status` tool already used (`{"status": "not running"}`, `{"status": "busy"}`, `{"status": "error", "error": …}`), still with exit 1; the running shape is unchanged, because the live smoke parses `result.version` out of it.

## Added

- **The file tree opens text files in a viewer pane instead of the desktop.** Double-clicking a supported file (source, config, docs, `md`/`markdown`, `txt`/`log`/`diff`/`patch`, and the extensionless `Makefile`/`Dockerfile`/`LICENSE`/`Justfile`) now asks the workspace for a read-only `code_viewer` pane carrying that path; opening the same file again focuses the pane that already shows it instead of duplicating it, and a new **Reload** button re-reads it after a change on disk (an open never re-reads, because a viewer's scroll, selection and rendered/source mode belong to its document). Everything the closed `ViewableFiles` table does not name keeps the existing confirmation-then-system path, so binaries, images and a downloaded `.desktop` behave exactly as before, and the per-tree **Open files: Viewer pane | System application** setting (default Viewer) can leave even supported files on the system route. Panes still never spawn panes: the file tree emits `PaneBody.request_pane`, and the workspace - the only spawner - attaches and activates the result.
- **Agents can search and read the knowledge base through the pane API.** `gpty vault search <vault> <pattern>` and `gpty vault read <vault> <path>` - mirrored as the `vault-search` / `vault-read` MCP tools - expose the wiki's vault to anything driving the control socket, with nothing new to configure: the vault's absolute directory is the only handle. Search re-indexes first, so a note edited outside gPTY (Obsidian, an editor, another agent) is visible to the next query rather than waiting for a pane to reopen the vault; it answers `{results: [{path, title, snippet}], total, truncated}`, where `truncated` says the 2000-note walk cap made the index partial. Read answers the note document `{path, text, truncated, crlf, mtime, size}` under the note editor's own rules - the vault-relative `.md` vocabulary, the regular-file gate, and the 1 MiB display cut - and neither method writes to the vault. Both are answered natively in Rust on a blocking pool rather than through the GDScript dispatcher: a vault is a directory rather than workspace state, and a walk plus SQLite query must not stall the frame that polls the pane API. A refusal is a JSON-RPC error carrying the stable `NoteError` code (`not_found`, `bad_path`, `outside_vault`, …) in `data.code`. The commands are queries and never auto-spawn a GUI.
- **The wiki pane draws the vault's link graph.** A new **Graph** button shows the vault's own structure as a canvas - nodes are the indexed notes plus a ghost for every unresolved `[[target]]`, edges are their mentions aggregated per note pair (a mutual pair is one edge and is drawn double-headed when Arrows is on) - with logarithmic, clamped thickness so one chatty note cannot drown the drawing, and pan/zoom/drag plus a deterministic layout a **Relayout** button restores. Nothing is stored and nothing is written: the graph is queried from `vaults.db` on every visit (every note mutation already re-indexes), positions live only in the canvas for the session, so a drag survives a re-query, clicking a note opens it behind the same Save/Discard/Cancel ask as the list, and clicking a ghost runs the preview's own mention resolution - offer to create a missing note, report an ambiguous stem, never guess. The query caps itself at 10,000 edges per class and 2,000 ghosts and says "truncated" rather than drawing part of a vault as if it were all of it.
- **The link graph accepts declared weights.** Measured weight is only mentions - two notes can be deeply related and name each other once, or name-drop ten times and share nothing - so an edge's weight can now be declared: right-click an edge in the graph canvas, or use `gpty vault weight <vault> <src> <target> --weight N` (mirrored as the `vault-weight` MCP tool), to set or clear one number between 1 and 100. A declaration overrides the measured count for edge thickness, the **Relayout** springs and link-panel ordering - display only, never which edges exist, what a click reaches or any trust decision - and lives in the user-owned `user://link_weights.json`, not the rebuildable `vaults.db`: a schema bump that re-indexes the vault cannot erase authored work. The canvas sets both directions of the pair it draws, an agent writes exactly one directed pair, and declarations whose note left the vault are pruned lazily when a complete graph is shown (never from a truncated answer). A renamed note's declarations are not re-keyed yet - that is a queued item - so renaming a curated note currently loses its weights on the next graph view.
- **Wikilinks are indexed (the data half).** `[[note]]` mentions are now parsed as the index pass reads each note and stored as edges in `vaults.db`: one row per occurrence, with the line it was written on, resolved against the note set by stem - or by path when the target contains `/` - with exact case first, then a unique case-insensitive match, and a stem two notes share never silently picked. A fenced block, an inline code span or a backslash-escaped opener stays literal text, so a note documenting the syntax creates no edges. The edges are *maintained* rather than derived on the fly: an edited note rewrites its own, and any pass that adds or removes a note re-derives the vault's - a stub that appears resolves the links that pointed at it, and a vanished target leaves its occurrence behind as unresolved. The store schema moves to `user_version=2`, which rebuilds the derived tables instead of migrating them (the vault is the source of truth; the next pass re-reads it). `GptyTerminal.vault_links(vault, note)` answers a note's outgoing links, its backlinks (the same edges read in reverse) and its unresolved targets, with the candidates an ambiguous stem could not choose between. The pane's view of these edges - the link panel and following in place - is the pane half below.
- **The wiki pane creates, renames, and deletes notes.** The editor used to only touch notes that already existed; now a New note button on the list (default `Untitled.md`, a bare name gains `.md`) asks for a path and opens the empty note, Rename and Delete sit on the open note, and an unresolved `[[mention]]` - or its row in the link panel - offers to create exactly the note it names. An ambiguous stem never gets one: it stays a report, because creating either candidate would be a guess. The verbs are the vault module's, held to the save's rules: the path follows the walk's vocabulary, a create or rename may only target a directory that already exists inside the vault (never one symlinked out), and the destination is claimed with `create_new`, so an existing note answers `exists` and is never replaced - a collision re-opens the same question with the typed name. Rename moves the vault entry (a symlinked note moves as a link, its target untouched) and preserves the file's mtime/size, so the open buffer and its save stamp stay valid; a dirty buffer's recovery copy is re-keyed to the new path, and a confirmed Delete (which warns about unsaved work) drops it. Every verb re-indexes, so a new note is searchable at once and a moved one stops satisfying links that named its old stem - the link table's own `removed`/`added` re-resolution answers that, with no second bookkeeping.
- **Wikilinks are followed in the wiki pane (the pane half).** Mentions now render in the preview - `[[target]]`, `[[target|alias]]` and `[[target#heading]]` - with the alias as the label and the heading kept as text, and clicking one follows it **in place**, behind the same Save/Discard/Cancel ask a Back makes (no history stack: the notes list is the way back). The occurrence set is the index's own: the renderer reuses the parser that writes the `links` table, so a fenced block, an inline code span and an escaped opener stay literal, and each accepted mention is replaced through a sentinel before Markdown parsing, so emphasis, headings and tables around it are untouched and the label is never re-parsed. The destination comes from `GptyTerminal.vault_link_resolve` - the same resolution rules the index used, over the same note set - so a stem two notes share answers with its candidates instead of silently picking one, and a mention typed but not yet saved follows too. A new link panel under the note lists each outgoing occurrence with the line it was written on (`target · line 3`), each backlink the same way (`src · line 3`), and marks an unresolved target with the candidates an ambiguous stem could not choose between; resolved and backlink rows open their note in place, a missing target offers to create the note it names, an ambiguous one stays a report (creating either candidate would be a guess), and the panel is capped at 50 rows per section with the rest counted. Mentions are a wiki-pane vocabulary: `GptyMarkdown.render` takes a `wikilinks` flag that every other caller leaves off - Inspector, Reasoning and code previews keep literal `[[…]]` - only the renderer can emit the `gpty-note:` scheme (a document's own Markdown link still admits only http/https/mailto), and `MarkdownView` merely announces the click; it never opens anything.
- **Wikilink navigation lands where the link points.** A `[[note#heading]]` fragment was parsed but only kept as label text, so following a mention always landed at the top of the target note; it now rides the link's URL (percent-encoded, the literal `#` the one separator) into `note_link_clicked(target, fragment)`, and the pane scrolls to that heading once the note renders - exact text first, then case-insensitive, with a pure `MarkdownAnchors` scanner reading the source outside frontmatter and fenced code so a note documenting Markdown grows no anchors. The link panel carries the same navigation: an outgoing row shows and follows its fragment, and a backlink row opens the linking note at the mention's line (derived from the nearest heading above it) instead of stopping at the top. `vault_links` derives fragments from the stored body per occurrence, so `vaults.db` still stores edges only. A mention written inside a Markdown link's label or an image's alt now yields to that container and renders as plain label text - nested `[url]` tags left the click target undefined, and the outer link is what the author explicitly wrote. Display only: a fragment says where in the resolved note to scroll, never which note.
- **The wiki pane edits notes - live preview, explicit save.** A note opens into an editor beside the sanitized Markdown preview (Edit / Split / Preview, default Split), and the preview follows the *buffer* as you type, so unsaved work is what you see. Saving is an explicit act - the Save button or Ctrl+S - with unsaved changes marked and Save disabled while there are none; leaving a dirty note asks before discarding. The write goes through `GptyTerminal.vault_note_write`, the same module that defines what a note is, so an edit can only reach an existing note inside the vault: the path must be one the walk could have listed, the resolved file must stay under the vault root (a symlink out of the vault is refused, one to a sibling note is written through), the replacement is atomic and keeps the note's own mode, and a file that changed on disk since it was loaded is never overwritten without an explicit confirmation. CRLF endings survive an edit, a note past the 1 MiB read cap stays read-only (saving a truncated read would drop the rest), and every save re-indexes the vault, so the new text is searchable at once. The note read and write are documented in the gdext README; the toolbar names the open file.
- **Wiki pane type (v0.6.0 groundwork).** A seventh pane type, `wiki`, registered across the vocabulary (`PaneTypes.ALL`, the Rust `PaneType` enum, the type→body map) and therefore spawnable from the sidebar, the palette (`new wiki`), `gpty new-pane -t wiki`, and layout/profile restore. It opens a vault at an absolute directory path - validated at use exactly like `file_tree`'s root, so a file-supplied path is never trusted - and lists the vault's Markdown notes (recursive, hidden entries skipped, bounded in entries and depth). Activating a note renders it read-only through the sanitized Markdown pipeline; editing, the full-text index, wikilinks, the link graph and declared weights landed with their own items. The note read and the code viewer now share one guard, `TextRead.read_prefix` (absolute paths only, regular-file gate, 1 MiB cap, torn-UTF8-safe decode) - the security rule has a single definition.
- **Vault index: the wiki pane's notes are indexed with full-text search.** A new `gpty_core::vault` store (SQLite + FTS5, at `state_dir()/vaults.db` - never inside the vault, which stays plain `.md` files the app only reads) is now the one definition of what a note is and what searching one costs. The pane's list and its new search box both come from it: `vault_index` walks the vault, re-reads only the notes whose mtime or size changed, drops rows for deleted notes and answers the sorted list; `vault_search` returns best-rank hits with title and a body snippet, using the same query sanitizer as scrollback search and porter stemming (notes are prose, unlike terminal lines). Both are static `GptyTerminal` methods answering JSON, with `error` reserved for "the query could not run" so "no match" stays distinguishable from "not indexed". The store reuses the scrollback engine's hardening - WAL, `user_version` gating, external-content FTS5 with the three triggers, owner-only mode, one process-wide write lock - with its own `(vault + relative path)` key; a truncated walk never prunes, and index bodies are cut at 1 MiB with the torn UTF-8 tail dropped exactly where the reader cuts, so a hit can never name text the view does not show.

- **Unsaved wiki edits survive a crash.** The editor holds its buffer in memory and writes only on an explicit save, so until now every keystroke since the last save died with the process - and a SIGKILL, a crash or an outside kill has no close guard to ask about it. A dirty buffer is now snapshotted as a *recovery copy* outside the vault (`GptyTerminal.vault_scratch_write`; `state_dir()/scratch`, owner-only, atomic, keyed by the vault and the note path), refreshed at most every 1.5 s while the buffer stays dirty - a throttle, not a per-keystroke debounce, because a debounce that restarts on every keystroke never fires during a long typing run - and dropped the moment the buffer reaches the file or the user discards it. Reopening the note asks (**Restore** / **Discard** / Escape for "not now") and never applies anything on its own. The recovered buffer carries the stamp of the revision it was typed against, so a file that changed while gPTY was away still gets the existing conflict question before anything is written, and a copy whose record names another vault or note answers "no copy", so a stale file can never restore the wrong text. `vault_note_write` remains the only write that reaches a vault.

## Fixed

- **A note that mentions itself follows its own rename.** The "Update references?" pass deliberately skipped the renamed note - its buffer is the editor's - so a hub or index note whose text named its own old stem kept that one mention unresolved, and create-from-link would offer the old name back. The pane now passes its buffer's cleanliness to the pass: a clean buffer makes the note's own mentions candidates along with every other note's, the preview counts them, and the apply answers the rewritten text and fresh stamp (`renamed_note`), which the editor adopts in place - the buffer becomes what landed, stays clean, and a save right after does not see a stale stamp. A dirty buffer is still never written under: the pass excludes its note and updates only the other notes, so the unsaved edit stays exactly as typed. `vault_link_rewrite_preview` / `vault_link_rewrite` take the state as `include_renamed`.
- **Renaming a note keeps its declared link weights.** A declaration is keyed on vault-relative note paths, so a rename used to leave every authored weight naming the old path - and the next complete graph pruned those entries as a vanished note, silently erasing the curation. The wiki pane now re-keys both endpoints immediately after a successful rename (`LinkWeightsStore.rekey_note`, one write): declarations authored on the note, pointing at it, or naming it on both sides move with it, unrelated declarations are untouched, and a stale row already stored under the destination (a rename requires that note to be absent) merges with the moved one, which wins each shared target. The re-key runs before the optional "Update references?" question and is independent of its answer - a declaration is not a mention, so declining to respell other notes cannot discard the weights - while a refused or cancelled rename leaves the store exactly as it was. A note moved outside gPTY still looks like a delete to the index and is pruned; that limitation is queued.
- **`pane-status` without a pane now actually reports every pane's status.** The no-argument form is documented as the agent status list, but its `--json` branch printed the raw `listPanes` envelope - no `status` anywhere - and the default branch built the aggregate in the CLI by querying each pane, which meant the MCP `pane-status` tool (dispatching straight to `paneStatus`) could not answer its own no-argument form at all. The aggregate is now the API's: `paneStatus` with no target answers `{panes: [{pane_id, label, type, status}]}` for every tile, with `status: null` for non-terminal panes instead of dropping them, and both output modes render that one document (`--json` in the usual response envelope). The single-pane contract is otherwise unchanged, except that targeting a real non-terminal pane now says it "has no status (not a terminal)" rather than claiming it was not found. A GUT contract test drives the real handler for both shapes, and a CLI roundtrip pins that the no-pane mode sends one empty request rather than fanning out.
- **`--json` no longer reports a failed command as success.** `format_response` printed the JSON-RPC error envelope and returned `Ok`, so `gpty vault read … missing.md --json` exited 0 while the same command without the flag exited 1 - every IPC-backed command inherited it, which defeats the machine-readable mode for a script that branches on the exit status and contradicted v0.5.6's `daemon status --json` (shaped JSON **and** exit 1). The envelope is still printed first, so stdout stays parseable, and the command then fails on `resp.error` in both modes; the custom-output commands (`list-panes`, `layout list`, the all-panes `pane-status`) share one `check_error` rule instead of re-deciding it, and the all-panes path now reports the RPC refusal rather than its "no result" symptom. The live smoke asserts both halves - nonzero exit *and* the `not_found` code in `data.code`. The MCP server is unchanged: it builds its own in-band errors.
- **Held pane-API responses are no longer cut off at 30 s.** The control server wrapped the whole connection - request read, handler, response write - in one 30 s deadline, so a method whose answer is deliberately held died there no matter what it promised: `pane-wait --timeout-ms 60000` was unreachable past 30 s (the client read an empty socket while the GUI still held the wait) and the plugin install review could not outlive 30 s either, even though its dialog is designed to close itself at 300 s. The deadline is now split: reading the request and writing the response each keep a 30 s I/O bound (a stalled client still cannot hold a slot), while the handler dispatches under its own registered budget - 30 s by default, and fallback + 5 s for held answers (`paneWait` 75 s, `pluginInstall` 305 s), so the handler's own fallback answers first and the server budget only frees a wedged connection. An overrun now answers `-32000 handler timed out` instead of dropping the socket. Verified live against a headless GUI: `gpty pane-wait … --timeout-ms 33000` answered `{matched: false, timed_out: true}` at 33.0 s.
- **Pasted text no longer disappears while the shell highlights it.** Bash's readline echoes a bracketed paste inside `ESC[7m`/`ESC[27m` (inverse video), and the renderer swapped only the glyph color - the pasted characters were painted in the cell's own background color, so a paste read as blank cells with the cursor advancing past them, until the next arrow key made readline repaint the line unhighlighted (measured against bash 5.2 under a real PTY; the same opacity hit any inverse cell, not just a paste). `gpty_core` now resolves the swap once, in `CellInfo::paint_colors`, before the renderer-facing cache is packed, so the pane draws the colors it is handed - `fg` is always the glyph color and `bg` always its background - and pays no per-cell branch for it. `godot/tests/integration/test_inverse_paint.gd` drives a real child's `ESC[7m` output into the pane's cache and fails on the raw-color packer; `inverse_cells_expose_swapped_paint_colors` pins the rule.
- **Renaming a note can now bring its mentions along.** A rename moved the file but not the `[[mentions]]` that named it by its old stem or path, so they silently stopped resolving - the referring notes were untouched, the link panel showed the target as missing, and create-from-link would have offered to recreate the old name. The pane now offers the update as its own step after a rename, with the count ("5 mention(s) in 1 note(s)"), and writes nothing unless you answer Update: only the occurrences that actually resolved to the old name are respelled - a stem two notes shared was ambiguous and stays untouched - while alias and `#` fragment are preserved, CRLF and every other byte stay as they were, and fenced code, code spans and escaped openers are not links to begin with. The renamed note's own buffer is never rewritten, a new name a `[[link]]` cannot spell refuses the pass instead of writing something that parses as different syntax, and a note over the read cap is skipped rather than truncated to its prefix. Every write is the save path's (containment, atomic replacement, a stale-stamp refusal), the apply re-plans in the same call so an edit made while the question was open is read fresh, and the re-index makes the new backlinks show up in the panel at once. `gpty_core::links::retarget` and `gpty_core::vault`'s `preview_link_rewrite`/`rewrite_links_after_rename` carry the rules, with five core unit tests (styles, ambiguity, CRLF, unspellable names, the read cap) and two pane tests (offer/apply, decline).

- **The GUT gate no longer collides with a running workspace - and no longer writes into your real user data.** `scripts/gut-check` now runs the suite on a private endpoint and profile: one 0700 temp directory (removed by the trap) that `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `XDG_STATE_HOME` point at, with `GPTY_SOCKET` aimed into it and `GPTY_SECRET` cleared. `GPTY_SOCKET` moves both listeners at once, because the event socket's path is derived from the control one - a pipe name on Windows - so the old failure is gone on every platform: the suite spawns real panes, one instance owns each endpoint, and a developer's open workspace used to make every pane-spawning test refuse its bind and quit the test instance mid-suite, ending the run with no Run Summary (which the gate correctly reports as untrustworthy). Verified against that exact setup - a live GUI holding `/run/user/1000/gpty{,-events}.sock` - `gut-check: OK - 50 scripts, 560 tests, all passed`, and `./scripts/ci-check` passed end to end with no hand-set environment; the running GUI kept answering the CLI, and the developer's real data and state directories were left untouched (a full run adds no probe vault and does not touch `vaults.db`). Windows needed a different lever, because Godot resolves `user://` through the Known Folder API and no environment variable redirects it: the gate now also exports `GPTY_TEST_USER_DIR`, the one root `BasePersistenceManager` resolves every store through and the GDExtension resolves `history.db` through, so stores, scrollback and test-created paths all land in the same temp directory; `LOCALAPPDATA`/`APPDATA` are sandboxed for the Rust state/data directories; Godot's file logging is off by default, so GUT writes no engine log (the smoke, which needs a failure-time engine log, passes `--log-file`). The live smoke uses that seam too and no longer backs up or restores the real concept and plugin stores. Tests that need a path use `TestPaths.user_path`, and the suite runs the seam on Linux as well, so the Windows path cannot drift unnoticed.
- **The wiki pane's index opens on a fresh Windows profile.** `state_dir()` on Windows returned `%LOCALAPPDATA%\gpty` without creating it, while the Unix arm had always created its directory - so `vaults.db` opened on Linux and macOS, but the first vault index on Windows failed with `unable to open database file`, leaving the note list empty. The live smoke hid it because it seeds a plugin record into that directory before launching the GUI. `local_app_data()` now creates the directory on first use, the same contract as the Unix `private_state_dir` (pinned by `local_app_dir_is_created_on_first_use`). The Windows GUT run is what surfaced it: the empty list failed a wiki test, and the gate's `-d` (Godot's `--debug`) turned the out-of-bounds follow-up into a 1.7 GB flood of interactive debugger prompts; the gate no longer passes `-d` and caps the run at `GUT_TIMEOUT` (600 s).
- **A note with YAML frontmatter is no longer labelled by its file stem.** `note_title` scanned the body for the first heading but took the first non-empty line as proof that there was none: an Obsidian-shaped note (`---` / `title: …` / `---` / `# Real heading`) opens with `---`, so every such note was labelled - and, since `notes_fts` indexes `title` beside `body`, ranked - by its file stem in search results, heading and all. A leading *closed* frontmatter block (`---`…`---` or `...`, CRLF files included) is now skipped before the heading scan; an unterminated `---` is not frontmatter and behaves exactly as before, and no `title:` key is read - that belongs with a properties UI, if one is ever built. The block itself stays ordinary visible Markdown and stays indexed, so searching a property's value still finds the note.
- **A large note's preview no longer freezes the app.** Two costs stacked behind the live preview of a big note. The renderer emitted Godot's `[ul]`/`[ol]` list tags, and Godot lays a list out *superlinearly* in its item count - measured 38.9 s to shape 1.7 MiB of two-item lists, and 146.7 s for a real 1 MiB note, on top of the ~0.3 s the render and parse actually cost - while the pane re-rendered through a 75 ms throttle for as long as typing continued, so every burst paid that price again. Items now render as `• `/`N. ` lines inside one `[indent]` per list, which is identical on screen (checked side by side) and makes the shape pass linear - 0.82 s for that same 1.7 MiB, 0.26–0.97 s for a 256 KiB–1 MiB note in the shipped release build - and the editor's preview renders on **settle** (0.4 s of quiet, `MarkdownView.set_markdown_settled`) instead of on the streaming throttle, so a typing run queues no render at all and one lands when you stop. Side effect of the numbering being the renderer's own: an ordered list that starts at 3 now renders `3.`. Costs measured with the new `godot/tests/bench/markdown_bench.gd` harness: one preview update is ~0.32 / 0.55 / 1.10 s for 256 KiB / 512 KiB / 1 MiB (where the 1 MiB case used to freeze for minutes); `edit` mode still renders nothing.
- **Recovery copies of a vault that went away are reclaimed.** An unsaved buffer's copy is only ever read, offered or cleared through the key of the note being opened, so a copy whose vault was moved, renamed or deleted was unreachable forever - and nothing reclaimed it, while every vault move orphaned one copy per unsaved note. A prune now rides each copy write (the editor's 1.5 s throttle is the only writer, and the prune runs before the write is located, so even a write refused for a vault that is no longer a directory tidies the directory): a copy is dropped only when its own record names a vault that is definitively gone - the path is absent, or exists as something other than a directory - and the check errs toward keeping, so a vault that is merely unreadable (an unmounted network path, a permission error) keeps its copies, as does a note that merely was not listed. A record gpty cannot read or parse, and any file whose name gpty did not build, is never touched; the `.gpty-scratch-*.tmp` remains of a write that died mid-rename are reclaimed on the same pass once older than an hour.
- **A zero-hit wiki search left the pane with no way back.** Every placeholder - the search box included - hid the whole top row, so searching for something the vault does not contain replaced the pane with "No notes match "…"" and nothing else: no list, no Back, no box to amend the query in. The search box now stays whenever the vault itself is usable - amend the query or clear it (the box's clear button) and the notes return - and is hidden only for a vault that cannot be opened, or while a note is open. Found in a live build; `test_a_search_with_no_match_says_so` now asserts both the box's reachability and the way back.
- **Unsaved wiki edits can no longer be lost to a close.** The editor's guard only covered in-pane navigation: closing the pane (`Ctrl+Shift+W`, the titlebar's X, the sidebar's close button, an IPC `killPane`), changing its type, resetting the workspace, activating a profile, closing a workspace, reloading the layout set and quitting the app all destroyed a dirty buffer without a word. Every one of those paths now asks the pane first - `PaneBody.request_close` - and one answer drives the whole action: **Save** (writes, then continues), **Discard**, or **Cancel**, which cancels the reset, the swap, the workspace close or the quit as a whole. The app's quit is now explicit (`auto_accept_quit` is off) and runs through the same walk from the window manager's close request, the titlebar's close button and the shutdown flag (`daemon stop`, a refused socket bind), with a pane-per-pane ask across every workspace; the editor's **Back** button gained the same Save answer it lacked. An IPC caller, which cannot answer a dialog, is refused instead - `killPane` and `layoutLoad` answer an error naming the pane - the rule `layoutLoad` already applied to untrusted profiles. A save that fails (or an overwrite the user declines) cancels the close rather than proceeding over it.
- **A note with CRLF endings opened as unsaved work.** The editor works in LF while the text "dirty" is measured against was the file's own - CRLF and all - so every CRLF note came up dirty the instant it was opened: the Save button lit for an edit nobody had made and the close guard asked about it. Found while building the recovery copy above, which turned the mislabel into a false question ("unsaved changes recovered" for the file the pane had just read, written out as a copy nobody typed): `_saved_text` is now normalized into the editor's space at load, so dirty means the same thing for both kinds of note. `test_a_crlf_note_opens_clean` pins it.
- **The Markdown preview stopped at 512 KiB without saying so.** `GptyMarkdown.render` cut its input at a cap of its own - half the 1 MiB every pane reads under - so a 900 KiB note rendered its first 512 KiB and nothing else, silently, and the wiki pane's own truncation notice (appended *after* the body) sat past the very cut it was announcing, which is exactly the size it exists for; `code_viewer`'s rendered view did the same. The cap is now the number the panes read under - one 1 MiB constant, pinned by a seam test that reads the GDScript declaration and fails if the two drift - and the cut travels with the text: the render answer is JSON (`{text, truncated, shown, size}`), and `MarkdownView` shows it as a banner **above** the body, for a source past the cap (a pasted buffer, a routed capture, a long model turn) and for a cut the caller made (`set_source_notice`, which the panes now use instead of appending their notice to the source - a note at the read cap is at the render cap too, so that appended notice was the first thing the cut dropped). The text views keep their notice at the end of the text they hold. Cost, measured before raising the cap: the Rust render is ~14 ms/MiB release (~107 ms debug) and a live preview's whole path - render plus the label's own BBCode parse - is ~74 / 157 / 336 ms for 256 KiB / 512 KiB / 1 MiB in the debug build; that is a preview cost only, since `edit` mode renders nothing.

## Added

- **The media pane has transport controls and reports its state.** Play/Pause, a seek slider with elapsed/total time, and Loop sit under the media surface. Pause freezes the media clock and pauses the audio generator (a video-only pane offsets its clock on resume); a slider seek uses the backend's acknowledged seek and resets the timeline - frames, queued audio and the clock epoch - before the new position plays, stopping the audio generator rather than trying to clear a buffer that is still active; Loop restarts a finished file from zero and is saved with the tile, while Play on a finished non-looping file also restarts. `paneStatus` now answers media panes too through a generic `PaneBody.status_document()` hook - state, file, position, duration, paused, loop and volume - while terminals keep their process/grid document and panes with no status remain listed as `null`.
- **Audio plays through the same Rust backend.** Every audio format in the media table - Ogg Vorbis/Opus, MP3, WAV, FLAC, M4A/AAC - now decodes to PCM in `gpty-media` and is streamed into an `AudioStreamGenerator` at 48 kHz stereo; the native Ogg/MP3/WAV loaders are gone, so video and audio share one decoder path. Chunks are fed while the generator has room with a bounded local lead (an unconsumed backend queue would stall the worker, which also decodes video), the generator starts on the first real chunk so its playback position and the media clock share an origin, and video presentation follows the audio clock when audio is running (monotonic clock otherwise). Volume (dB) and mute are pane settings saved with the tile. An 8-bit mono WAV also exposed and fixed a real gap: `pcm_u8` is now in the component set, and a layout-less PCM frame is normalized before resampling instead of panicking inside the binding.
- **The media pane renders Rust-decoded video.** The pane's video surface is now an `ImageTexture` fed by the pinned FFmpeg backend rather than Godot's native `VideoStreamPlayer`, so `.mp4`, `.m4v`, `.mov`, `.mkv`, `.webm`, `.avi`, `.ts` and `.m2ts` join `.ogv` (which moved to the same backend - one video path, no fallback). Frames are drained only while a four-frame PTS-ordered backlog has room, and presented against a monotonic clock, so a decoder that runs faster than real time does not play the clip several times too fast; a stale frame is dropped only when a newer one is waiting. The surface keeps the clip's aspect ratio with letterbox/pillarbox fit, and a backend refusal clears the pane's file like any other unreadable path. Audio for these files is covered by the next entry.
- **Release bundles carry the pinned FFmpeg runtime.** The GDExtension now has an `$ORIGIN`/`@loader_path` runpath, and a single `scripts/bundle-media` helper places the matching `libav*`/`libsw*`/DLLs beside it for Linux, Windows and macOS - including a universal (lipo'd, ad-hoc signed) macOS set and injection into the exported `.app`. FFmpeg's LGPLv3/LGPLv2.1 texts and the component list travel in `licenses/`, the AUR recipe installs them under `/usr/lib/gpty` and `/usr/share/licenses/gpty`, and the Linux packer refuses a bundle whose libraries do not resolve. A locally extracted Linux bundle starts with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` unset.
- **A Rust media backend demuxes and decodes the wider format matrix.** A new `gpty-media` crate links a pinned, minimal FFmpeg build (9.0.2, LGPLv3, dynamically linked, no network protocols, only the components in `components.txt`) and exposes one session per file: demuxing plus H.264/HEVC/VP8/VP9/AV1/Theora video decoded to packed RGBA8, and MP3/FLAC/Vorbis/Opus/AAC/ALAC/AC-3/PCM audio resampled to interleaved f32 at the caller's rate and channel count. One OS thread per session reads packets and fills bounded queues; the pane polls, a full queue blocks only the decoder, and a seek is acknowledged by the worker so pre-target frames are dropped rather than delivered. The `GptyMedia` GDExtension node is the JSON + packed-array edge, and the path gate is applied again in Rust (absolute local regular file; no FIFO, device, URL or project scheme). The pane's video and audio paths both consume this backend.
- **A media pane plays local audio and video.** An eighth pane type, `media`, opens an absolute local file and plays it through the pinned FFmpeg backend, with the file name and playback state shown in the pane. The path is validated at use by the closed `MediaFiles` table (absolute, regular file, known extension) and never reaches `ResourceLoader`, so a file-supplied layout or profile cannot smuggle a `.gd` or `.tscn` in behind a media extension; remote URLs and project schemes are refused with an in-pane explanation. The file tree's in-app route now covers media too (supported files ask the workspace for a media pane, and reopening the same file focuses the pane already playing it), and a media tile restores its path. Transport controls and `paneStatus` transport state sit in the same pane, and the demux/decode matrix covers the wider container and codec set.

## Fixed

- **A refused second gPTY window exits instead of waiting on a question it cannot ask.** The startup-refusal path ran the normal quit walk, which asks every pane before closing; on Windows a live shell is conservatively "possibly busy" (`foreground_job` is null), so a headless second instance raised a confirmation nothing could answer and never exited. A refused instance never served a workspace, so it now says why and quits directly; a normal shutdown request still asks.
- **The media pane keeps the frames that are due.** Polling drained eight decoded frames per tick and then kept only the newest four, so a clip the decoder finishes in milliseconds lost frames that were already due: the picture stayed on the first one while audio advanced. The drain now stops at a four-frame backlog, and a stream whose timeline does not begin at zero starts its clock on the first pending frame's own PTS instead of holding the clip in the future for the length of the offset. A six-frame, 2 fps fixture pins the presented PTS sequence.
- **Seeking or restarting a media file no longer fights the audio player.** The reset called `AudioStreamPlayer.clear_buffer()` while playback was still active, which Godot refuses (the engine logged `Condition "active" is true`), so a seek or loop restart did not empty the generator. It now stops the player and drops the generator reference - the next `play()` creates a fresh, empty generator - and a seek while paused keeps the paused position.
- **The link graph keys its edges without NUL.** Godot strings do not hold NUL: `"\u0000"` decodes to U+FFFD and logs an engine error, so the separator-based pair key was not the identity it claimed. Counts live in a nested map keyed by the two endpoints, and the hit-test tie-break compares the endpoints directly.
- **The CLI no longer builds a worker pool it has no work for.** `gpty` now runs on a current-thread tokio runtime: every command is one request in a process that exits as soon as it has an answer, so the multi-thread runtime's workers bought no parallelism - they were only concurrency around `process::exit`, the plausible shape behind a one-off Windows `STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION` (`0xC0000374`) on an `inject` whose CLI printed nothing. It also drops the worker-pool startup from every invocation: 300 `gpty version` runs on Linux went from 1.04 s to 0.60 s. The Windows smoke now runs 100 throwaway CLI processes (≈ 200 connections - each process opens the version probe and then its command) right after the pane-status checks as the teardown stressor, and a nonzero exit fails there with its hex status instead of being retried.
- **Closing a pane, a workspace or the app asks before stopping a command that is still running.** A terminal now reports whether a process other than its shell owns the PTY - exact on Unix, where the foreground process group changes only for a command that actually took the terminal (a background `cmd &` never counts), and conservatively on Windows/ConPTY, which has no equivalent and treats a live shell as possibly busy. Every destruction path walks the same two-phase question: one dialog for the action's own hazard, naming every busy pane and raised once even when sixteen panes go at once, then each pane's own unsaved-work question. A shell at its prompt closes silently; closing a pane whose configured program *is* the child (a full-screen tool) reports nothing running, because that pane's close is the program's close. The sidebar's **Reset** is now **Close all panes** with a trash icon - it shared the counter-clockwise arrow with "change pane type" - and the palette command matches. IPC callers cannot answer a dialog, so `kill-pane` and `layout-load` keep refusing unsaved edits but treat an explicit kill or load as consent to stop what it replaces, and never raise a dialog in a GUI they cannot answer. `paneStatus` carries the new `foreground_job` field (`true`/`false` on Unix, `null` where detection is unavailable) for any other observer.

- **The first keystroke after launch reaches the shell.** A fresh workspace left `last_body` unset and no pane held keyboard focus - `_apply_active_workspace_view` only activated a *remembered* pane, and nothing on the startup path ever set one - so typing did nothing until the user clicked a terminal (UX-01, verified on v0.5.6 and still present in 0.7.0). The view refresh now resolves a fallback: the workspace's first terminal, else its first pane (so a read-only layout still has an active row), activated through the same `activate_pane` rule as a click. The same hole affected every other entry that builds panes without activating them - switching to a restored workspace that was never visited, and profile activation - and the one fallback fixes those too.

## Added

- **Each workspace has a working directory.** A workspace carries its own default directory, new panes start there, the pane's `PWD` stays in step with it, and the workspace's directory button shows a folder instead of a bare label. The directory is part of the trust decision for what a workspace's panes may open, so it is bound where the workspace is chosen rather than read from whichever shell reports last.
- **The Inspector pane remembers what you aimed it at.** The prompt and the switches are saved per pane (`user://pane_inspector.json`, keyed by the pane's attachment id) and restored on the next start; closing the pane discards the stored aim instead of leaving it to land on whatever takes that slot. Both stay app-owned runtime state: a layout or profile file still cannot set them.
- **A sidebar profile row opens a new workspace.** Aside from activating the profile in the current workspace, the row can open it in a fresh one, which is what the profile catalog was for.
- **`new-pane --split <side>` places the new pane where you asked.** `left`, `right`, `top` and `bottom` are honoured; when the grid cannot honour a side it falls back to the larger-axis split instead of failing.
- **The vault verbs answer only for a vault you have opened.** `vault search`, `vault read` and `vault weight` (and their MCP tools) serve a root registered by opening that vault in a Wiki pane's settings, and a refused root says it is not registered and how to fix it. Before this, the socket would index any path the caller named.
- **The knowledge base ships in the release bundle.** `godot/knowledge.json` is packed with the app, so a release install has the wiki without a source checkout.
- **gPTY's own processes harden themselves against environment reads.** On Linux the GUI and the CLI set `PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0`, which makes `/proc/<pid>/environ` and `/proc/<pid>/maps` unreadable to a program in a pane; on Windows both install a process DACL that withholds memory-read and thread-injection rights while keeping the peer-check and terminate masks the control socket uses. `GPTY_SECRET` now gates pane programs on both platforms.
- **The MCP entry is published from the release.** `server.json` is the descriptor, `ci-check` refuses a version that disagrees with the CLI crate, and `.github/workflows/mcp-registry.yml` publishes it over OIDC when a release is published - no secret, and no hand-published entry that drifts from the binary.

## Changed

- **A release is three downloads, not thirty-six.** The platform archives already contain the GDExtension and the pinned FFmpeg set, so publishing those libraries again made the Releases page a build-artifact dump and inflated the project's only install signal (v0.7.0's "73 downloads" were 7 real bundles). A release is now the three archives plus `SHA256SUMS`, and the checksum, attestation and upload lists cannot disagree about the asset set.
- **A window holds at most 96 live panes.** Counted across every workspace, because a hidden workspace's pane keeps its PTY, child process and grid. `new-pane`/`pane-run` past the ceiling answer with the limit instead of starting another process, and a layout or profile with more tiles restores what fits and says how many did not.
- **One IPC connection serves a batch.** A client that writes several newline-framed requests gets one answer per request, in order, and a bad frame costs that frame rather than the rest of the pipeline. The shipped clients still use one connection per call, so this adds a guarantee rather than moving a caller.
- **A refusal reaches the caller as its own sentence.** A handler's `{code, message}` travels flat to the CLI and to MCP - `error: rpc error -32000: Pane 'x' not found` - instead of a stringified JSON envelope, and an MCP tool that refuses is a successful response carrying `isError: true` with that sentence rather than a protocol error. The unused `gpty-ipc` typed request models are gone, so the handlers' `params.get(...)` keys are the wire vocabulary and `wire.rs` is the one place a renamed argument is translated.
- **Stores and logs are owner-only and content-free.** A store written by an older build is repaired to 0600 when it is next read (`O_NOFOLLOW`, `fstat` on the descriptor, `fchmod` only a looser mode of a file this user owns), the user directory is kept at 0700, and log files at 0600. An agent backend's stderr is sanitized, bounded, logged at `debug` and shown in the failure message instead of reaching the console at `warn`.
- **A file-supplied pane cannot name a resource to load.** Pane settings are a closed per-type table (`PaneTypes.settings_schema`) with a range or format per key, the restore path drops the keys only the app may set, and terminal fonts load from bytes so a font path never reaches `load()`.
- **A profile's trust comes from where it came from, not what it claims.** `ProfileManager` stamps each entry's origin, user entries are stripped of the fields that claim provenance, and the consent walk is chosen by that stamp - a `profiles.json` entry cannot borrow a builtin's name or a plugin's id.
- **The CLI prints the cause chain when a command fails.** An error that ends in `moving … into …` now says what the move answered.
- **Documentation-only pushes skip the code CI, and the local gate classifies too.** `scripts/ci-check` judges the pushed range (docs-only gets the docs gates, everything else the full suite, `--fast` the index, `CI_CHECK_FULL=1` forces everything), the pre-push hook runs it before the ref moves, and `ci.yml` ignores docs-only paths while the Docs workflow becomes their gate. The CI jobs also cache what they actually rebuild - the FFmpeg prefix above all - which is what made the Windows vcpkg rebuild stop landing in a job cap. CodeQL runs on pull requests and weekly instead of every push.

## Fixed

- **A selection stays on its text.** A bare `Ctrl` or `Shift` no longer snaps a scrolled-back pane to the bottom, so `Ctrl+Shift+C` copies scrollback; the selection follows its text when the view scrolls (wheel, PageUp/PageDown, a search jump) and when output arrives, instead of holding a fixed screen row; copy reads grid rows, so a selection scrolled out of view still copies in full; wrapped lines copy joined instead of gaining a newline at each wrap; and the selection is dropped when the width changes or an app switches to the alternate screen, which is alacritty's rule - the old highlight survived and landed on different text.
- **A paste cannot close its own bracketed-paste bracket.** Pasted text drops the control characters that could end the bracket early (and `DEL`), on both the bracketed and the plain branch; the filter is one cached PCRE2 pass, because the per-character loop it replaced took 34.8 s for 1 MiB where the pass takes 6 ms.
- **A pane cannot grow the GUI by opening an escape string and never closing it.** The grid's parser bounds an unterminated OSC at 64 KiB and closes it, which is the same bound the line parser already applied; before this, a pane printing `ESC ] 0 ;` and an endless payload took the GUI from 3.3 MB to 260 MB in 1 MiB steps. On Windows ConPTY buffers the string itself before gPTY sees a byte, and the smoke's step now proves the difference rather than claiming it.
- **A media seek no longer freezes the window.** A seek claims a serial, queues the command and returns instead of waiting for an acknowledgement with a 5 s deadline, so a file that keeps the decoder inside a libavcodec call can no longer stall the Godot thread once per slider step - measured at 1 µs where the old path returned an error after 5 s. The pane is told nothing from the replaced timeline is presentable until the worker applies the seek.
- **A media open cannot hang, and cannot be redirected.** The open reads a verified descriptor (`O_NONBLOCK | O_NOFOLLOW`, `fstat`-checked) and hands FFmpeg a custom `AVIOContext`, so a FIFO swapped in after the path check never blocks `open(2)`; the interrupt callback's leak is gone; a frame that would resample past the size cap is refused as `too_large` before it is allocated; and closing a pane no longer waits forever on a decoder - the join is bounded at 2 s, after which the worker is detached and frees its own contexts.
- **`first_pipe_instance` is claimed only when a create succeeds.** A transient failure on the Windows pipe used to spend the claim, so every later instance was non-first and a process racing for the name could own it - the restarted GUI then attached to that process instead of refusing. The claim is now recorded on success, and the `rust-windows` job runs the test that drives the sequence.
- **A fresh plugin install completes.** The destination's parent (`plugins/<owner>/`) is created before the rename, the review's acceptance now actually moves content, and the printed failure carries the underlying cause instead of only the two paths.
- **A profile accent stays in its workspace.** Each workspace records its own activated profile, so activating one in workspace 1 no longer highlights it in workspace 2; a new workspace starts with none and switching back restores that tab's own.
- **An agent's events stay in their workspace, and a renamed terminal keeps its companion.** Agent events are fanned out by terminal session id and attachment id inside their own workspace, so two workspaces running the same profile no longer cross their Reasoning panes, and renaming a terminal rewrites the companion's `source_attachment_id` instead of leaving it subscribed to an id that no longer exists.
- **A pane label two workspaces share is refused.** `inject`, `paneRead`, `paneStatus` and `killPane` resolve an `attachment_id` first; a label resolves only when exactly one pane carries it, and an ambiguous label is refused with the ids to re-address.
- **Scrollback's last line survives a pane close.** The writer re-drains a closed queue before breaking, and `PaneHistory::drop` joins the writer instead of returning early - the parallel test run that had been losing the last line is now deterministic.
- **A vault walk and a vault read stay inside the vault.** Symlinks and junctions are resolved and kept only when they canonicalize inside the canonical root; a skipped link is counted and shown in the pane's footer, and a second road to the same file no longer bypasses the check.
- **A plugin command checks the binary it is about to talk to.** The stale-binary probe runs before the `plugin` arm dispatches, so a newer CLI against an older GUI (and the reverse) says so instead of reporting a corrupt store.
- **The Inspector pane's prompt is runtime-only.** `system_prompt`, `auto_run` and `accept_concept_captures` are `file: false`, so a restored layout or a profile cannot preconfigure a pane to submit captured output under a file-chosen prompt, and `auto_run` defaults off.
- **Closing a terminal whose child outlived its I/O task asks first.** That pane used to read as idle, so closing it killed the surviving process group without a question.
- **The Inspector backend's stdout is read through one bounded frame reader**, so a long or split frame is no longer misparsed as several.
- **The bundled agent skill is inside the CLI crate**, so `gpty --skill` works from an installed crate as well as from the repository.
