A release-repair patch. v0.8.4's tag could not be pushed at all, and its macOS archive shipped before the FFmpeg alias fix reached the transport. No application behaviour changes.

## Fixed

- **A release tag could not be created at all.** The `tag` ruleset carried GitHub's `creation` rule with no bypass actors, and `creation` restricts ref creation to bypass actors - with none, nobody can create a tag, the administrator included - so `v0.8.4`'s push was rejected with "Cannot create ref due to creations being restricted". `scripts/check-github-settings` asserted the same wrong rule set, so the gate reported OK while the policy it guards made every release impossible. The ruleset now keeps `deletion`, `non_fast_forward`, `update` and `required_signatures` - a tag must be signed and cannot be moved or deleted - and the check compares against exactly that set, so drift in either direction fails.
- **The macOS archive carries one real file per FFmpeg library again.** v0.8.4's zip held three real ~9.29 MB copies of every library (95,698,840 → 96,084,344 bytes against v0.8.3) because `actions/upload-artifact` dereferences symlinks and FFmpeg ships the unversioned `libavcodec.dylib` as a real file that the bundler lipo'd into a second canonical copy. `scripts/bundle-media` now derives each `<name>.<major>.dylib` and `<name>.dylib` alias as a symlink from the canonical `<name>.<major>.<minor>.<patch>.dylib`, and re-derives them after the transported tree lands in the bundle, so the archive is one real file plus two symlinks whichever way the libraries arrive.

gpty's test strategy combines automated CI checks with a manual pre-release smoke test suite. Automated tests cover all pure-logic paths in Rust and GDScript; manual tests cover GUI interaction, IPC bridge roundtrips, and daemon lifecycle that require a running Godot instance.

## Automated (CI)

Run on every push and pull request:

```bash
# Rust - unit tests, integration tests, doctests
cargo test --workspace
cargo clippy -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check

# GDScript - unit + integration tests
godot --headless --path godot --import
./scripts/gut-check  # runs GUT and fails if the run aborted (GUT exits 0 regardless)
```

The same two commands run on Windows in the `windows-smoke` job, under the
runner's Git Bash: the suite takes its shells from
`SettingsManager.default_shell_command()` and its byte-emitting fixtures from
`godot/tests/helpers/shell_fixtures.gd`, so a GDScript test is not a
Linux-only artifact. `gut-check` prints any test that pends with its reason and
fails on a test that ran without asserting.

`gut-check` also gives the run a private **user root**, not just a private
endpoint: `GPTY_TEST_USER_DIR` names a temp directory that
`BasePersistenceManager` uses for every `user://` store and that the GDExtension
uses for `history.db`. On Windows, where Godot's `user://` resolves through the
Known Folder API and cannot be redirected by an environment variable, it
additionally sandboxes `LOCALAPPDATA`/`APPDATA`. The GUT run leaves Godot's
file logging off (so there is no engine log to redirect) and caps the suite at
`GUT_TIMEOUT` (600 s) so a hung test fails the gate, stops a run that has
produced no output for `GUT_STALL_TIMEOUT` (120 s) with the last test it
started and the command that re-runs that file alone, and it does not pass
`-d` (Godot treats it as `--debug`, so a runtime test error would break into
the interactive debugger instead of being reported); the live smoke uses
`--log-file` because it needs a failure-time engine log. The
effect is that a suite run cannot read a developer's saved layout, write probe
vaults or recovery copies into their state directory, or append to their real
scrollback. A test that needs a filesystem path must use
`TestPaths.user_path("name")` rather than `ProjectSettings.globalize_path("user://name")`,
and a fixture directory whose name is the same on two runs comes from
`TestPaths.fresh_dir("name")`, which clears the previous run's leftover first
(and whose bounds rule unifies the Windows drive separator before comparing);
the live smoke uses the same seam and needs no store backup/restore.

**Rust coverage:** core engine (parser, keymap, grid, concept routing, capture state machine, history, the vault index and its walk), the vault's native IPC handlers (search re-indexing, read containment, parameter validation), IPC types + protocol, CLI schema generation and response formatting (both output modes fail on an RPC error, and the JSON envelope is printed first), GDExtension FFI functions. The tile layout algorithm (split, kill, expand) lives only in `godot/scenes/terminal/terminal_manager.gd` and is tested there, in `godot/tests/unit/test_terminal_manager.gd`, against the real `spawn_pane`/`kill` - including every close order of five panes. A Rust copy of it once stood in for those tests and could not fail when the real code broke; do not reintroduce one. The IPC vocabulary is pinned across languages: a test in `crates/gpty-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs` reads the real registrations (`crates/gpty-gdext/src/ipc.rs`), the real dispatch (`ipc_handlers.gd`, plus the requests `workspace.gd` intercepts), and every `client.call` literal in `src/commands/*.rs`, and asserts they name the same methods as the advertised MCP tools.

**GDScript coverage:** concept merge/save/load, terminal manager tile lifecycle (spawn, kill, swap, labels, grid-full refusal), divider edge drag (`test_pane_edge_drag.gd`: pixel preview vs unit commit, one `tiles_resized` per release, MIN_TILE clamp, window-border refusal, drag survives leaving the strip), settings save/load roundtrip, profile CRUD and the three profile sources (the shipped built-in, installed-plugin profiles, user profiles - merge order, ` (n)` dedupe, and the plugin-revision consent gate), layout save/restore, sidebar signal emission, pane settings application, IPC dispatch against a real workspace (`test_ipc_dispatch_contract.gd`: listed pane ids and workspace-unique labels both address the pane they name, a label two workspaces share is refused naming both candidates, terminal-only methods refuse other panes, unknown methods answer -32601, an untrusted profile is refused, and a targetless `paneStatus` covers every tile with `status: null` for non-terminals), palette command generation, the pane-settings allowlist (`test_pane_hardening.gd`, `test_pane_settings.gd`: per-type keys, ranges, file-only refusals, and a drift guard that every pane type accepts every key it saves), and the byte-only font loader (`test_terminal_fonts.gd`, `test_pane_resource_loading.gd`: a crafted `.tres` that executes on `load()` is refused through a layout tile, a profile and `settings.json`).

**Known gaps (not automatable in headless CI):**
- Real PTY output timing: a headless pane spawns a real shell, but tests that assert on its output are timing-dependent, so they live in the live smoke (`scripts/smoke_pane_api.py`) instead - one harness for every platform, run by `ci-check` and by the `windows-smoke` CI job. Its concept step asserts a routed capture event fired by a runtime-built output marker, which is the live proof that committed *output* lines (ConPTY renders their breaks as cursor moves) reach the concept matcher on the platform running the smoke. Its final step seeds an installed plugin's record into the sandboxed store and asserts the plugin's profile is listed by `profile list` and restored by `profile load`, which is the live proof of the profiles-migration read path. Its vault step seeds a temp vault and drives `vault search` (twice - the second after editing a note outside gPTY, which proves the index-on-search freshness), `vault read`, and the `not_found` refusal, so the native vault handlers are exercised over the same socket an agent uses.

**Files without automated coverage** (manual checklist only):
- `godot/scenes/terminal/workspace.gd` - restore/sanitize wiring and concept event routing; IPC dispatch itself is covered by `test_ipc_dispatch_contract.gd`, which drives `WorkspaceIpcHandlers.handle` with a real `Workspace`
- `godot/scenes/terminal/terminal_pane.gd` - renderer and input paths are partially covered by `test_keyboard.gd`/`test_copy_routing.gd` mocks; real rendering is manual-only
- `godot/scenes/ui/settings_panel.gd`, `godot/scenes/ui/pane_settings_panel.gd`, `godot/scenes/ui/status_bar.gd`, `godot/scenes/ui/toast_overlay.gd`, `godot/scenes/ui/icons.gd`
- `godot/scenes/panes/code_viewer.gd`, `godot/scenes/panes/file_tree.gd`, `godot/scenes/panes/wiki_pane.gd`, `godot/scenes/panes/inspector_pane.gd`, `godot/scenes/panes/reasoning_pane.gd` - unit-tested for routing/session contracts; real OMP/Markdown rendering is manual (`cli_view_pane.gd` is the exception: `test_cli_view.gd` runs a real child and asserts its streamed lines)
- `godot/scenes/autoloads/focus_manager.gd`, `godot/scenes/autoloads/shortcut_manager.gd`, `godot/scenes/autoloads/toast_manager.gd`, `godot/scenes/autoloads/update_checker.gd`

## Test case format

New manual test cases follow this pattern:

```
**Given** preconditions (state before the test)
**When** action performed
**Then** expected observable outcome
```

For CLI commands, include the exact command and expected output format. For UI actions, describe the gesture and the visual change.

Ideas and gated work that is not scheduled. An entry here is either an idea that is not designed yet, or work that says in its own text what evidence would start it. Anything concrete and committed belongs in a numbered release, and moves there when it is defined.

## v0.1.0 - Core Engine

| Done | Area | Item |

| ✅ | TERM | **Multi-PTY terminal emulator** - spawn and manage multiple shell sessions in a tiling grid. Each session is an independent PTY with its own shell process, environment, and working directory. |

It is sequenced here, after attach/reattach, because the daemon changes who the clients are: a headless daemon or `gpty attach` over SSH has no GUI to show a consent dialog, so the consent channel has to be designed with the client model, not before it. Design: (1) *classify the caller* - a connection whose peer process descends from one of this daemon's pane shells (a parent-chain walk: `/proc/<pid>/stat` on Linux, `proc_pidinfo` on macOS, a process snapshot on Windows; an unsupported platform keeps today's behaviour rather than failing closed) is a **pane client**, anything else is an outside client with today's authority. On Linux prefer **cgroup membership** to the parent walk: run each pane in its own cgroup scope (`systemd-run --user --scope`, or a delegated subtree) and classify the peer by `/proc/<pid>/cgroup`, which survives a process reparenting to init or to a `systemd --user` subreaper; keep the parent walk as the fallback where no scope can be created; (2) *tier every method* - an explicit table next to the method registry puts each IPC method in observe (`list-panes`, `pane-status`, the pane's own state declaration), read (`pane-read`, `pane-wait`, the vault verbs) or control (`inject`, `pane-run`, `broadcast`, `new-pane`, `kill-pane`, layout and concept changes, plugin install), and a test fails when a registered method has no tier, so a new verb cannot ship unclassified; (3) *a user-owned grant* - a pane client gets observe by default and needs a grant for the higher tiers, stored in a user-owned store keyed by attachment id (the `PaneEnvStore` pattern: a file, profile or plugin can never grant it), shown on the pane's row and in its settings and revocable there; (4) *a policy of `allow` (today), `ask` or `deny`* - `ask` raises a consent dialog naming the pane, the method and what it would reach, once, remembered per pane; for a headless daemon the grant is pre-set through the user's own settings, never answered by a pane client. Which policy is the default is the owner's decision at pickup; `ask` is the recommendation, because it keeps the agent workflow (an agent in a pane calling `gpty inject` or `gpty mcp`, v1.0.0's launch demo) one click away while ending silent cross-pane control. (5) *scope is the workspace, with no grant that widens it* - a pane client's reach is its own workspace and nothing else: a command that names a pane in another workspace is answered exactly as a nonexistent pane ("not found", so the other workspace cannot be probed), and there is deliberately no grant, setting or `ask` prompt that crosses the boundary. Rejected alternative: a cross-workspace grant. The workspace is the unit the user already reasons about ("root things here, ordinary things there"); a permission that crosses it is the confused-deputy path, and it multiplies the grant matrix from pane × tier to pane × tier × workspace, which is how a permission model becomes impossible to explain or audit. The legitimate cases do not need it: an agent that runs tests in a pane while the user watches does so inside one workspace, and anything that really spans workspaces is done by the user from the GUI, by an outside client (their own terminal's `gpty`), or by moving the pane (v0.9.5). Outside clients keep today's reach across workspaces. A workspace marked sensitive (v0.9.5) is excluded from the socket altogether, for outside clients too. State the limit in SECURITY.md when it ships: a process that double-forks and reparents to init (or to a `systemd --user` subreaper) escapes the parent walk, and on systems without restrictive ptrace defaults a same-user process can also attach to the daemon or read its memory, so this is a speed bump against opportunistic scripts and injected agents, not a boundary against a determined local attacker. Tests: a pane-descendant client is refused at each tier it has not been granted and served at each it has; an outside client is unaffected; `ask` prompts once and remembers; a revoked grant is refused again; every registered method has a tier; a pane client naming a pane in another workspace, by id or by label, gets "not found" and nothing is delivered; the audit's two-pane probe, kept as a script by the v0.7.1 re-audit item, now fails to inject. On landing, rewrite the Known limitations entry and the in-scope line in SECURITY.md to say what is enforced. |
| ⬜ | IPC | **Rust-side IPC param validation** - deserialize and validate IPC request params in Rust (`gpty-ipc`) before dispatch. Promoted from Future: the daemon refactor is the natural home (Rust owns the request path end-to-end), and validating the pre-daemon GUI queue would be throwaway work. GDScript handlers remain untyped. |
| ⬜ | DOCS | **The v0.10.1 changelog records the permission and validation work** - release-time: write `docs/content/docs/changelog/v0.10.1.md`, link it from `CHANGELOG.md`, and cover the caller permission and the Rust-side validation. |

Adds a `game` pane type for small 2D games, Snake first, so waiting on an agent can be a break instead of a context switch. The chain is deliberately small and self-contained: built-in games only, no files, network or third-party code (a native pane SDK stays out of scope per the architecture boundary), and no part of the control surface or the daemon depends on it. It builds on the v0.8.0 theme tokens and palette and the v0.9.5 notification signals.

## v0.14.2 - Program Status (OSC 7501)

The Program Status Protocol is a generic, pty-native way for any program to say what it is doing — idle, working, done, blocked with a kind, or failed — and why, with a message, a progress percentage, and a tree of records under ids. It is the first agent-state channel gPTY can share with programs and harnesses it does not integrate with, and it rides the pty that already crosses SSH and containers, so it needs no socket or manifest; like `gpty_state`, it is spoofable by design and may only paint display state. On Windows it needs the v0.13 ConPTY passthrough row, because ConPTY re-renders the stream and drops unknown OSCs.

The implementation spec for these rows - the wire parsing, the limits, the record model, the exact JSON and FFI shapes, the UI constants and the test list - is a local working note at `TEMP/osc-7501-program-status.md` in the repository root. It is gitignored (the `TEMP*` entry in `.gitignore`) and never shipped; it exists so a row can be picked up without re-running the research.

| Done | Area | Item |
|:---:|:---:|---|
| ⬜ | TERM | **Program status reports (OSC 7501) are parsed, bounded and projected onto the badge** - the Program Status Protocol (spec rev 0.4, `superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status`) is the generic terminal answer to "what is this program doing": `idle`/`working`/`done`/`blocked`/`error`/`clear`, a `kind` with `blocked`, a `progress`, an `app` slug, a base64 `title`/`msg`, and a tree of records under hierarchical ids. Both parsers drop it today: the line parser interprets only `gpty_state` (`crates/gpty-core/src/parser.rs:239`) and alacritty's vte Performer ignores every OSC number it does not know, so no program can reach the badge with the protocol. Fix: a new `crates/gpty-core/src/program_status.rs` (grammar, record store, projection; no `vte` dependency) plus one `osc_dispatch` branch and a `program_status` field on `TermGrid` beside the tracker (`crates/gpty-core/src/term.rs:192`). Enforce the spec's limits before touching a record - 4096-byte sequence, 16-byte key, 32-byte `app`, 128-byte id with 32 per segment and 8 levels, 2732/2048 `msg` encoded/decoded, 256/192 `title`, 64 records with least-recently-updated eviction; skip a malformed pair but discard the whole report on a limits break, undecodable base64, or a control character in decoded text. Each report replaces its record completely; `clear` removes a subtree or everything; RIS (`ESC c`) clears every record while DECSTR does not; OSC 133 `A` and child exit drop `working`/`blocked`/`idle` and keep `done`/`error`; gate application on capture only, never on alt-screen or the post-resize window, because agent TUIs live on the alt screen; strip bidi/invisible formatting from `msg`/`title` before display. Project attention-first `blocked` > `error` > `working` > `done` > `idle` onto `AgentState` at Tier 2, and ignore `gpty_state` for that terminal from its first 7501 report until RIS. This is the second OSC the parser interprets, so the row carries the security review `docs/content/docs/agents/security.md:41` requires: display only, no report field ever written back or logged, limits checked first. Nothing answers today, so a probing program treats gPTY as unsupported and shows no status at all even though the parser work lands. Fix: `OSC 7501;?` queues `\x1b]7501;?:states=idle,working,done,blocked,error:kinds=permission,question,auth\x1b\\` (byte-exact, pinned in the note), coalesced to one reply per `feed` and one per 100 ms per terminal. ## v0.5.3 - Terminal Performance & Mouse

| Done | Area | Item |
|:---:|:---:|---|
| ✅ | TERM | **Render batching** - the text pass issues one `draw_string` per run of consecutive cells sharing font, color, and underline state instead of one per non-space cell (backgrounds were already merged). A run stops at a space, so an underlined space keeps its own segment - the old pass underlined every attributed cell, spaces included, and a first cut of the batching silently dropped that segment until a pixel diff caught it. Measured with the new `godot/tests/bench/draw_bench.gd` harness (forced full repaint vs idle frame, X11 + `--disable-vsync`): 90×30 1813 µs → 1388 µs, 200×60 4482 µs → 3867 µs (idle frame ≈ 300 µs, so ~20 % off the repaint at a realistic pane size), and both sizes render **pixel-identical** to the per-cell pass. Baseline from the v0.5.3 prep work: idle panes no longer repaint at all (the repaint is gated on the grid generation - measured 48–49 gate ticks/s per pane against 0 generation changes), so this item is only about cost *under load*. |
| ✅ | TERM | **UI Thread DoS mitigation** - a pane whose grid work (fetch + repaint) exceeds `PANE_WORK_BUDGET_MS` (4 ms, a quarter of a 60 Hz frame) now looks at the grid less often: the cadence stretches geometrically to `MAX_SYNC_INTERVAL` (0.1 s ≈ 10 Hz) and walks back as soon as a sync finds nothing new, so nothing is lost - the damage tracker coalesces everything into the newest grid state, and a flooding pane is unreadable at 60 Hz anyway. View changes the user drives (wheel, PageUp/Down, search jump) are exempt for 500 ms, so scrolling a large pane is never pushed into the flood cadence. Measured with `BENCH_FLOOD=1` in `godot/tests/bench/draw_bench.gd` (a pane repainting its whole screen in a loop, median of 3 runs): 200×60 costs 2.47 ms/frame → 1.46 ms/frame (≈400 → ≈690 fps in a 2100×1300 window), while a pane that fits its budget (90×30, ~1.5 ms/frame) is not throttled at all. 5 GUT cases pin growth, the budget floor, the exemption, the ceiling, and recovery. Reports are SGR when 1006 is on and legacy X10 otherwise, encoded from the same cell mapping selection uses, and the report is dropped (never clamped) past cell 223 where the legacy form cannot address it. Selection and scrollback are untouched while the bits are zero, and `Shift` bypasses reporting so text selection stays reachable in an app that grabbed the mouse (the manual checklist covers nvim/lazygit/htop). ## v0.7.1 - Trust Boundary Hardening

The October 2026 security audit (a read-only review at commit `97eec6b`: the Rust crates, the GDScript GUI, `cargo audit`, semgrep and proofs of concept in an isolated sandbox) found no remote-code-execution or memory-safety bug in the Rust core; its weaknesses are trust boundaries around the control socket and around files the GUI loads. Every item below was re-checked on 2026-10-19 against `5cf373a` plus the working tree, and each item says how: **re-run** (the probe was executed again), **measured**, or **re-read** (the code is unchanged and the original proof of concept was not repeated). None had been closed since the audit; two (the profile-consent item and the release-token item) turned out narrower than first reported, and the text says so. The audit also left two memory-growth concerns untested; both are measured here, and one of them (an unterminated escape string) is unbounded and became an item.

This is a patch release ahead of v0.8.0's UI work because most of these are reachable from data gPTY is documented to treat as untrusted (SECURITY.md: terminal output, files, other panes), and the first two were the project's own stated boundaries. Items are ordered by reachability and impact. The control-socket finding is split: its documentation half is closed here (the owner decided that gPTY's goal is for a pane not to be able to drive other panes without permission, so SECURITY.md now says plainly that this is not enforced yet), and its enforcement half is queued in v0.10.1, where the daemon's client model is decided. The threat model they are judged against is SECURITY.md's, and where an item changes behaviour that document changes in the same commit. Four build/CI rows were split into v0.7.2 on 2026-10-28 so this release's reachable fixes do not wait on repository policy; that section carries no runtime change.

## v0.8.5 - Release Repair

The patch v0.8.4 made necessary. Its tag could not be pushed at all: the `tag` ruleset carried a `creation` rule with no bypass actors, and `scripts/check-github-settings` asserted the same wrong rule set, so the gate reported OK while the policy it guards made every release impossible. Publishing then shipped a macOS archive whose FFmpeg alias fix never reached the transport. Both are release-pipeline work, the only kind of change this release carries.

| ✅ | BUILD | **The tag ruleset forbade creating a tag, so no release could be tagged** - found and fixed 2026-11-16 while cutting v0.8.4: pushing `v0.8.4` was rejected with "Cannot create ref due to creations being restricted". The `tag` ruleset (26369813) carried the `creation` rule with `bypass_actors: []`, and `creation` restricts ref creation to bypass actors - with none, nobody can create a tag, the admin included; `scripts/check-github-settings` asserted the wrong set in the other direction (`TAG_RULES` *required* `creation`), so the gate passed while the policy it guards made every release impossible. Fixed in the same session: the ruleset keeps `deletion`/`non_fast_forward`/`update`/`required_signatures` - a tag must be signed and cannot be moved or deleted - and drops `creation`, and `TAG_RULES` matches it, so the exact-set comparison catches the drift in either direction. ## v0.8.7 - Depth, Backdrop & Motion

The finish pass the visual-identity release leaves open: motion gets one switch behind it, the terminal body gets a scheme-owned backdrop, floating surfaces get depth, and a focus change becomes findable. The study book that seeded these rows (`sparks-and-sprites`: prose CC-BY 4.0, code MIT) is a catalogue of presentation mechanics, and only its interface half is adopted here - character animation, procedural generation, flipbooks, input verbs and cursor trails are deliberately out of scope, because gPTY is a reading and orchestration surface, not a game. Motion is allowed where it announces a change - the Getting Started guide, a pane's first paint, a created sidebar row, the tab just opened - and never on text being read: the terminal grid, a streaming Reasoning turn, a note body or source code stay still.

| ⬜ | CORE | **Input reports success after the PTY writer thread exits** - when a pty write errors (EIO once the slave side closes), `PtyHandle`'s writer thread logs and exits, but the terminal task's stdin drain keeps receiving: `write_with_backpressure` returns on the non-`WouldBlock` error and drops that message, the next `send_text` still finds room because the drain keeps pulling, and only the per-message `write_bytes` sees the disconnected writer - so `inject`/`broadcast` answer delivered for bytes that never left the process. The window is the 500 ms `EXIT_DRAIN_QUIET_MS` before a child-exit teardown ends the task, so reachability is low. Fix: close `stdin_rx` on a terminal write error so the refusal reaches the caller, while the read side keeps draining so the exit code and a final capture still land. |
| ⬜ | GUI | **A window moved to another display keeps the frame cap resolved at launch** - found 2026-11-21 while reviewing the Windows/macOS paths: `Workspace._apply_fps_setting` and `TerminalPane.refresh_sync_interval` read `DisplayServer.window_get_current_screen()` when the setting is applied, so they are right at launch, but moving the window to a display with a different refresh rate does not re-run either. With `max_fps = Native` the engine cap is the old screen's rate: with vsync on, 165 on a 60 Hz display is harmless because the compositor holds 60, while 60 on a 165 Hz display caps it at 60 until a settings change or restart; a terminal's follow-the-display cadence keeps the old interval in both directions. Fix: notice the current screen changing (a low-frequency timer, or a window event where the platform raises one) and re-apply `Engine.max_fps` plus each live terminal's `refresh_sync_interval`; an explicit cap is left alone. Tests: a seam that supplies the screen and its rate, asserting the cap and cadence follow a move and an explicit cap does not; no per-frame polling. |

Eight releases that measure the product and then close the gap between what gPTY claims and what it does. v0.9.0 is instrumentation: a diagnostics pane, opt-in hot-path timers and a gated performance budget, and the first hot-path fixes those numbers justify. v0.9.1 and v0.9.2 are terminal fidelity - first how text is drawn, then what the emulator answers. v0.9.3 and v0.9.4 are the security, release-integrity, project-file and build-hygiene work left by the November 2026 review. v0.9.5 is everyday ergonomics. v0.9.6 is distribution and reach. v0.9.7 is enterprise readiness and dual-licensing: commercial license structuring, non-repudiable audit logging of agent PTY sessions, administrative security policy guardrails, headless token-based orchestration, and air-gapped installation packaging. The nightly channel rides in v0.9.3 rather than v0.9.6: it is a release-pipeline change, and it has to exist before the signature-asset and SBOM rows edit the same upload list.

## v0.9.0 - Instrumentation & Hot Paths

The release that makes cost a number instead of an adjective. The diagnostics pane is read-only and never carries program content; the timers are opt-in; the budget is the figure the UI/UX claim is measured against. The rows after the budget spend the number: a partial grid sync stops paying for the whole grid, the PTY path's guard stops walking bytes one at a time, and the note index stops walking a body it is only searching for a bracket.

The analysis behind those rows - which loops were measured, which are already vectorized upstream, and which candidates this release deliberately does not take - is a local working note at `TEMP/simd-opportunities.md` in the repository root. It is gitignored (the `TEMP*` entry in `.gitignore`) and never shipped; it exists so a row can be picked up without re-running the research.

The same question asked of the GDScript layer - which work is interpreter-bound, allocation-bound or crossing the FFI per item, and which work belongs in Rust - is a second local working note at `TEMP/gdscript-opportunities.md`. It is gitignored and never shipped. The repeatable half is committed: `scripts/gdscript-audit` ranks the candidates, `godot/tests/bench/gdscript_probe.gd` measures the idioms, and `docs/content/docs/agents/gdscript-performance.md` owns the method.

Fix: a built-in `diagnostics` pane (read-only, no PTY) that samples on a timer rather than per frame and shows (a) frame time split into idle and repaint, (b) resident memory and its peak, (c) process CPU, (d) power draw where the platform exposes it, and (e) per-pane rows - type, grid size, scrollback rows, PTY alive, and the fetch/draw timings the status bar no longer prints. ## v0.9.1 - Terminal Rendering Fidelity

Probes run against a sandboxed v0.6.0 build (commit `b8bf5f9`) with the same synthetic-input + viewport-capture method as the UX audit (AGENTS.md, "UI/UX assessment method"), plus a read of the emulator's event path in `crates/gpty-core/src/term.rs`. Each item is marked verified (reproduced in the running app), code (read in the source, not run) or not tested. The theme: a daily driver is judged first on whether `htop`, `nvim`, `lazygit` and `ssh` look right inside the user's own shell. This is the drawing half; v0.9.2 is the answering half.

| Done | Area | Item |
|:---:|:---:|---|
| ⬜ | TERM | **A pane cannot spawn when `$HOME` names no directory, and an empty workspace directory silently means `$HOME`** - found 2026-11-04 while running the GDScript suite: every pane failed with `Failed to spawn PTY for '/bin/bash': No such file or directory (os error 2)` although `/bin/bash` existed and ran, because the environment carried a `HOME` whose directory had been removed. Cause (code, portable-pty 0.9.0 `CommandBuilder::as_command`): the workspace directory is passed as `cwd`, and portable-pty substitutes `$HOME` whenever that is absent - `self.cwd.filter(is_dir).unwrap_or(home)` then `cmd.current_dir(dir)` - so an unusable `$HOME` becomes a `chdir` failure whose errno surfaces as "the program does not exist". Its `get_home_dir` falls back to `getpwuid` only when `$HOME` is unset, never when it is set and missing, and the gdext `cwd` sanitizer (which does drop a stale workspace directory) has no equivalent floor for the fallback. Two consequences: a launch whose `$HOME` is a stale mount, a deleted home or a container path that is not there fails every pane with a message naming the shell; and the documented meaning of an empty workspace directory ("Empty inherits gpty's" cwd, `gpty-gdext/src/lib.rs`) is wrong - the pane starts in `$HOME` (the prompt in the `agent-badges` capture reads `~` while the app's own cwd is the repository). Fix: resolve the start directory in one place before the spawn - the workspace directory when it is a directory, else gpty's own cwd when that is one, else `/` - pass it explicitly so portable-pty's `$HOME` substitution is never reached, and correct both comments. Tests: `HOME` set to a nonexistent path still spawns, and a pane with an empty workspace directory starts where the resolver says. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **The default shell is the user's shell, not `/bin/bash`** - verified: on a machine whose login shell is `/bin/fish` (`$SHELL` and `getent passwd` agree), every pane ran `bash` (`ps -p $$ -o comm=`), so the user's prompt, aliases and plugins were missing with no hint why. `SettingsManager.default_shell_command()` returns the literal `/bin/bash` on every non-Windows platform; on Windows it returns `%COMSPEC%`, i.e. `cmd.exe`, which is not what a Windows user opens a terminal for. Fix: resolve the fresh-install default from `$SHELL`, validated by the same rule `validate_executable` applies (absolute path, regular executable file), falling back to `/bin/bash` then `/bin/sh`; on Windows prefer `pwsh.exe`, then `powershell.exe`, then `%COMSPEC%`, found by absolute path. Settings → Terminal lists the detected shells (including installed WSL distributions) as choices beside the free-text path, and shows what the default resolved to. A saved `shell_command` is never overwritten. Two knock-on points to handle in the same item: the GUT suites that rely on `default_shell_command()` for a POSIX shell (AGENTS.md "Testing") stop being bash-by-construction, so they must pin a POSIX shell through a fixture helper; and the Workspace Trust comparison is made against the user's configured default, so confirm a built-in or plugin profile that names no program still never prompts. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **A pane whose shell has exited says so and offers Restart or Close** - verified: after `exit` the pane stays on screen with a cursor and no message, and `gpty list-panes` still counts it, so a crashed shell, a dropped `ssh` or a finished command looks like a hung pane. The exit code is already tracked (`TermStatus.exit_code`, `paneStatus`) but never shown. Fix: when the child has exited, draw an unobtrusive footer ("Process exited (code N) - Enter to restart, Ctrl+Shift+W to close") from the status the engine already reports; Restart re-spawns the pane's own spawn plan (program, args and the user's own per-pane env) through the same `validate_executable` path and keeps the pane's `attachment_id`; a Settings choice `On exit: keep / close` (default keep, so scrollback stays readable). Tests: exit 0 and non-zero, Restart re-runs the same plan, and the pane list and IPC state agree in both. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **Text attributes the emulator parses are drawn: strikethrough, dim, hidden, curly/dotted/dashed/double underline and underline colour** - verified: in a probe row of `ESC[1m` (bold), `[3m` (italic), `[4m` (underline), `[4:3m` (curly), `[9m` (strike) and `[2m` (dim), bold, italic and underline render and the other three do not. Cause (code): `CellInfo` in `term.rs` carries only `bold/italic/underline/inverse/wide`, so alacritty's strikeout, dim, hidden and underline-variant flags (and the SGR 58 colour) are dropped before the packer and the GUI never sees them; the exact flag set to carry is confirmed against `alacritty_terminal`'s `Flags` at pickup. These are not exotic: nvim draws diagnostics with undercurl, and many CLIs use dim for secondary text and strike for removed lines. Fix: replace the bool fields with a small attribute bitfield packed into the existing flat arrays (no per-cell `Dictionary`, per the AGENTS.md rendering note), thread it through the renderer-facing packer and `terminal_pane.gd`'s run batching (a run breaks on an attribute change, as it already does for underline), and draw strike as a rect, dim as the blended foreground, and undercurl as a pixel-aligned zig-zag. **Must land before v0.10.0's grid wire protocol freezes the packed layout.** Tests: a pixel diff against the current render for plain text and the three working attributes (the v0.5.3 batching technique), plus one assertion per new attribute. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **Box-drawing, block and braille characters are drawn by gPTY, not taken from the font** - verified: `┌─┐│└┘` renders at the default 14 px with visible gaps and a missing corner; block elements and braille are the same class. Font glyphs for these ranges are sized to the font's advance and ascent, not to the cell, which has a fractional pixel size, so neighbours neither join nor tile. `htop`, `btop`, `lazygit`, `tmux` borders and every TUI frame are built from them. Fix: draw U+2500–U+257F (box drawing), U+2580–U+259F (blocks) and U+2800–U+28FF (braille) procedurally as pixel-snapped rects in the cell's own rect, the approach Alacritty and kitty take, bypassing the font and leaving the text-run batching untouched for everything else. Powerline separators rendered correctly from the bundled DejaVu Sans Mono in the probe and stay font-drawn. Tests: a golden-pixel assertion that horizontally adjacent `─` and vertically adjacent `│` cells meet with no gap at several font sizes, including fractional cell sizes and the UI scale from the v0.8.0 theme item. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **Fonts: a chosen family with a fallback chain, so Nerd Font icons and combining marks render** - verified (symptoms), code (cause): Nerd Font private-use icons (`\uF015`, `\uF07B`, `\uF121`) rendered as small placeholder shapes instead of icons, and `e` + U+0301 lost its accent; CJK, colour emoji and Powerline separators rendered fine. Settings → Appearance offers a single font file (default `DejaVuSansMono.ttf`), the code sets no explicit fallback list, and `CellInfo.ch` is a single `char`, so a zero-width combining mark has nowhere to live (alacritty keeps them per cell; confirm at pickup). Fix: a font picker over system monospace families plus a file, an ordered fallback list, an optional bundled symbols-only fallback (a Nerd Fonts "Symbols Only" build - licence review at design time, as in the Rust media backend item), and combining-mark support (carry the marks through the packed grid and draw them on the base cell's origin). **Security coupling:** the typed, extension-gated font loader this item builds on shipped in v0.7.1 as `TerminalFonts` (`FontFile` from bytes, an absolute regular file, extension + magic + face checks; `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.ttc`, `.woff`, `.woff2`, never a resource loader), so the picker, the ordered fallback chain (the loader takes one path today) and combining-mark support are built on top of it. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **A per-pane font is saved but overwritten on every restore, so a chosen font only survives in-session** - found while closing the v0.7.1 resource-loading item: `Workspace._restore_into` applies a tile's settings and then `SettingsManager.apply_to_terminal`, so the saved `font_path` loses to `cfg_font_path`; a per-pane colour scheme no longer round-trips at all (the v0.7.1 fix made it runtime-only and stopped saving it). Decide with the font picker and fallback chain above: either the tile wins for that pane (the value is already validated by the closed settings table and `TerminalFonts`) or the global wins and the pane panel stops offering a per-pane choice. Add the save → restore test for a chosen font, which the fallback chain will need anyway. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **A terminal pane spawned with `-c` can show an empty body after its command finishes** - found 2026-11-06 while recording `demo-panes`: two panes were spawned in one run - `gpty new-pane -t terminal -c 'ls' --title files` (output rendered) and `gpty new-pane -t terminal -c 'git log --oneline --graph' --title log`, whose body stayed blank for the four seconds until the next cue, while the pane existed, was focused and drew its title, so the spawn answered. Cause not measured: either the child's output raced the pane's grid attach (spawn, write and exit inside one frame) or the pane clears its grid when the child exits in the frame the first update is applied. Fix: capture `-c 'echo one; sleep 0.2; echo two'` and `-c true` at spawn to separate the two, then keep the grid's scrollback instead of resetting it on child exit; a regression test drives `-c` through `newPane` and asserts the text is in `pane-read`. |

## v0.9.2 - Terminal Protocol Fidelity

The second fidelity release: what the emulator must reply to, and the regression suite that keeps both halves honest.

| Done | Area | Item |
|:---:|:---:|---|
| ⬜ | TERM | **A program's palette change is stored by the parser and then ignored by the renderer** - the set half of the OSC colour family is already implemented one layer down: alacritty's `set_color` and `reset_color` (in the `alacritty_terminal` 0.26.0 crate) write OSC 4/10/11/12 into `Term.colors` and clear them for 104/110/111/112, exposed by `colors()`, whose `Colors([Option<Rgb>; COUNT])` type indexes by `usize` and `NamedColor`, so a program's `ESC]11;rgb:08/08/08` parses cleanly. gPTY then resolves every cell from its own 16-entry table instead: `TermGrid.palette` (`crates/gpty-core/src/term.rs:175`) through `CellInfo::from_cell` (`:344`) and `color_to_rgb` (`crates/gpty-core/src/color.rs:36`), where `Background` is `palette[0]`, `Foreground` is `palette[7]` (`:47-48`) and the cursor colour comes from settings rather than `NamedColor::Cursor`. So per-window theming - a shell writing its palette on start and resetting it on exit - is a silent no-op, and that is how whole-environment theme kits bind one theme to one window without editing terminal config. `TitleListener` (`term.rs:107`) drops every other `TermEvent`, which is the query half covered by the row below. Fix: resolve Named and Indexed colours through `term.colors()` first and the pane scheme second, draw the cursor from `Colors[NamedColor::Cursor]`, raise the same full-damage flag `set_palette` raises, bound indices to the table, and keep it display-only and session-scoped (a reset session starts from the pane's scheme, nothing is persisted). Tests: a shell fixture emits OSC 4/10/11/12 then asserts packed cell RGB and the cursor colour, and 104/110/111/112 restore the scheme. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **Answer the terminal-state queries the emulator raises: OSC 4/10/11/12 colours and text-area size** - code: `TitleListener` in `term.rs` handles `Title` and `PtyWrite` and drops every other `TermEvent` into `_ => {}`. alacritty raises colour-request and text-area-size-request events for OSC 4/10/11/12 and `CSI 14/18 t` and expects the frontend to write the reply, so a program that asks for the terminal's background or palette never gets an answer. nvim, `bat`, `delta` and `lazygit` use the background query to pick a light or dark theme, and some wait out a timeout on every start. Not tested against a specific program yet - the first step is to run those four and record which ones stall. Fix: reply with fixed templates built from the pane's resolved palette (`TermGrid.palette` now carries `.foreground`/`.background` beside the 16 ANSI entries, filled from the active scheme - 2026-11-20 - so the reply reads them instead of assuming slots 7/0) and the cell and pixel size - the same class as the cursor-position and mode reports already forwarded, so nothing from the stream reaches the reply except the requested index - with a cap on pending replies per frame. Test: a real child (the `ShellFixtures` pattern) sends the query and reads back `ESC]11;rgb:…` from the pane. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **The bell is seen** - code: alacritty's bell event also falls into `_ => {}`, so `BEL` does nothing (the probe's frame diff was too noisy to add evidence). Fix: a brief accent on the pane's title bar, a badge on the pane's sidebar row and, when the pane is not in view, on its workspace row; `DisplayServer.window_request_attention()` when the window is unfocused; an optional system sound; a Settings choice `Bell: off / visual / visual + attention`, and a rate limit, because `cat` of a binary rings thousands of times. No full-screen flash (reduced-motion friendly). Display only, and nothing returns to the engine. The unseen-event marker introduced here is the one v0.9.5's activity item reuses, so build it as a shared sidebar badge rather than a bell-only one. |
| ⬜ | SEC | **Clipboard writes from programs (OSC 52), consent-gated and write-only** - code: alacritty's clipboard-store event is dropped, so `y` in nvim over SSH, tmux `set-clipboard` and any remote copy never reach the user's clipboard. Reads (the `?` query, clipboard-load) stay unimplemented permanently: a program reading your clipboard is an exfiltration path. Fix: honour store requests under a per-pane policy `ask (default) / allow / deny`; `ask` shows a non-modal toast with the byte count and Allow / Deny / Always-for-this-pane; the payload is base64-validated and decoded in Rust, capped (64 KiB to start), never logged, and only the focused pane may write without a prompt even under `allow`. The policy is user-owned state like `PaneEnvStore`: a layout, profile or plugin manifest cannot carry or pre-grant it. Needs the security review the parser's own comment requires for any new OSC, a line in `SECURITY.md`, and tests that a file cannot set the policy, an oversize or malformed payload is dropped, and a read request gets no reply. On Linux the primary-selection target maps to PRIMARY only once the v0.9.5 mouse-and-clipboard item exists; until then it is ignored. |
| ⬜ | TERM | **The shell's working directory is known: OSC 7 as display, "new pane here" as the default** - verified: after `cd /usr/share` in one pane, a new terminal started in `$HOME`, and no pane shows its directory anywhere (title, status bar, pane list). Code: alacritty ignores OSC 7, so this needs a bounded tap on the byte stream; the `gpty_state` OSC in `LineParser` is the precedent, and the tap must obey the same alt-screen, capture-replay and resize suppression (confirm the right place at pickup). ## v0.9.5 - Everyday Ergonomics

Same evidence as v0.9.1 and v0.9.2 (the October 2026 daily-driver gap assessment; items are marked verified, code or not tested). Where those releases make gPTY render and answer like a terminal, this one makes it pleasant to live in for eight hours: selecting, linking, knowing what finished, rearranging, rebinding, and opening a project. It follows the daemon's client model in design - the OSC 133 marks and scrollback are served through `HistoryStore`, so the v0.10.0 reattach can replay them - but it does not depend on the daemon shipping first.

| ⬜ | TERM | **Scrollback can be deleted: clear a pane, delete closed-pane history, delete everything** - code: scrollback is plaintext on disk (SECURITY.md) and the app has no way to remove it. `HistoryStore::clear()` deletes one pane's rows but only a test calls it. The only deletion in the app is one sweep, 2 seconds after launch, of rows whose pane id is not open (`prune_missing_panes`), so a closed pane's output stays on disk until the next launch. The `lines` table holds only the pane id, the line number and the text, with no timestamps. Fix, in order. (1) *Clear scrollback and history* for the active terminal, as a palette command (and what the v0.9.5 context menu's `Clear scrollback` calls): it clears the pane's on-screen scrollback and deletes its stored rows. Each pane's writer thread queues lines for up to about 200 ms, so the clear goes through that writer or flushes it first, otherwise lines written just before the clear come back. (2) *Settings → History*: shows the store size (`history_store_stats` already reports it) and offers `Delete history of closed panes now`, which runs the launch sweep on demand, and `Delete all history`, which asks first, states how many panes and how much it will remove, and says that a live pane keeps what it shows on screen. (3) *Closing deletes*: an explicit GUI close of a pane (titlebar X, `Ctrl+Shift+W`, the palette, the sidebar) deletes its rows at once instead of leaving them for the next launch. Quit, a reset or layout load that restores panes under the same `attachment_id`, and a type swap do not delete, and the launch sweep still reclaims whatever is left. IPC `killPane` leaves its rows to that sweep too, so a program in a pane cannot erase history. The v0.9.5 workspace-restore item changes the whole-workspace close, whose rows are then kept for a bounded time. Not included: deleting by age for a live pane, which would need a timestamp on every stored line, and the per-pane line cap already bounds the size. None of it is reachable over IPC, the CLI or MCP. Tests: clear removes the pane's rows and nothing else, and a line queued before the clear does not come back; the on-demand sweep keeps open panes; Delete all asks first and removes every row; an explicit close deletes while quit and a same-id restore do not; the empty-list guard in `prune_missing_panes` still holds. |

## v0.9.7 - Enterprise Readiness & Dual Licensing

The release that establishes commercial viability, enterprise governance, and dual-licensing readiness. It bridges the gap between open-source community innovation and enterprise compliance requirements: providing commercial licensing exceptions, non-repudiable audit logging of agent PTY activity, administrative security guardrails, headless token-authenticated orchestration, and self-contained air-gapped installation archives.

| Done | Area | Item |
|:---:|:---:|---|
| ⬜ | PROJECT | **Dual-licensing framework and commercial proprietary exception** - the project is currently licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later with Section 7 additional permissions (`LICENSE-EXCEPTIONS.md`); enterprise adoption is blocked by corporate legal policies that forbid copyleft terms on developer workstations and internal plugin ecosystems. Structure a dual-licensing model: the community edition remains GPL-3.0-or-later, while a commercial enterprise license provides proprietary exemptions for internal extensions, closed plugins, and proprietary deployment. Update `LICENSE-EXCEPTIONS.md` and `README.md` with explicit commercial exception text and licensing contact guidance; add an automated license header and SPDX tag validation test in CI to ensure third-party embedded components remain compliant across both editions. |
| ⬜ | SEC | **Immutable PTY audit log stream for autonomous agent activity** - autonomous coding agents running in terminal panes can execute unmonitored shell commands, create network tunnels, or inspect sensitive files without an enterprise audit trail. Normal scrollback is ephemeral, user-clearable, and stored without cryptographic provenance (`crates/gpty-core/src/store.rs`). Fix: add an opt-in, append-only, non-repudiable audit log stream (Settings → Enterprise → Audit Logging, default off) writing to an owner-only, tamper-evident JSONL or SQLite journal. Each entry records ISO timestamp, pane attachment ID, agent identity (from `agent_state` / `ompEvent`), current working directory, executed argv/input, exit code, and a SHA-256 digest of stdout/stderr chunks. The audit stream cannot be truncated or disabled via IPC, MCP, or in-pane commands. Tests: IPC `clearHistory` cannot delete audit logs, an agent session records every executed command and hash, and a disabled setting produces zero audit overhead. |
| ⬜ | SEC | **Administrative security policies and execution guardrails** - in enterprise environments, security operators must restrict rogue or unvetted actions executed by autonomous agents. Fix: introduce system-level policy configuration (read from `/etc/gpty/policy.json` on Linux/macOS or `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\gPTY` on Windows) that outranks user configuration. Supported guardrails: (1) command allowlist/denylist for spawned panes (rejecting disallowed binaries like netcat, curl, or destructive commands), (2) mandatory `GPTY_SECRET` enforcement (rejecting unauthenticated IPC/daemon connections), (3) plugin installation gate (prohibiting unverified third-party plugins from the registry), and (4) disabled network media streaming in media panes. When a policy restricts an action, the UI and IPC report a structured "refused by administrator policy" error. Tests: policy file is read-only to non-root, denied commands fail with the expected error, and user settings cannot override policy values. |
| ⬜ | IPC | **Headless orchestration mode and bearer token authentication** - enterprise agent workflows (CI pipelines, remote build clusters, ephemeral agent fleets) require running gPTY headlessly with programmatic pane control over TCP/TLS or forwarded sockets rather than local-only UID matching. Fix: extend `gpty-ipc` with an opt-in enterprise server listener supporting bearer token authentication (constant-time token comparison via `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`) and mTLS. The headless daemon accepts remote agent connections, issues temporary scoped tokens per agent, and exposes the full JSON-RPC/MCP suite without requiring a local X11/Wayland display server. Tests: unauthenticated connections are rejected with 401/JSON-RPC -32001, valid bearer tokens grant scoped pane access, and tokens cannot be forged or leaked through status endpoints. |
| ⬜ | BUILD | **Self-contained air-gapped installation archive** - enterprises operating in defense, banking, and secure enclaves run in air-gapped networks with no outbound internet access. The current distribution relies on runtime downloads for certain documentation references, external update checks, and system font discovery. Fix: add a `make-enterprise-bundle` target producing a 100% self-contained offline tarball/zip containing bundled font fallbacks, complete offline documentation and wiki assets, pre-compiled FFmpeg shared libraries, and build-time flags that hard-disable update checking (`cfg_telemetry=false`, `update_checker` disabled). Tests: verify that booting the enterprise bundle in an `unshare -n` network-isolated namespace starts cleanly, renders fonts and documentation without network timeouts, and logs zero connection attempts. |
